Players can move Adam's soul in a slow free-flight state before rebirth. Capable of limited flying, giving him high mobility. His primary fire, Quantum Magic, is a hitscan attack that launches quick energy bolts to damage opponents. His secondary fire, Cosmic Cluster, allows Adam Warlock to charge-up his staff and release multiple energy bolts. The longer it's charged, the more projectiles will be fired, up to five energy bolts. The end-lag of Cosmic Cluster can be cancelled with Quantum Magic; by rapidly weaving uncharged Cosmic Cluster with primary fire, the player can slightly increase Adam Warlock's damage-per-second at the cost of increased ammo consumption. Avatar Life Stream is a bouncing healing energy that can affect up to two targets. This ability has two charges. Players can track the primary allied target by a special reticle that appears around their model. Adam Warlock receives a smaller amount of this healing upon casting; if no ally is targeted, he receives full healing effects. Dealing critical hits to enemy heroes with Quantum Magic decreases the cooldown of Avatar Life Stream by 1 second. Each successful hit against enemy heroes with Cosmic Cluster decrease the cooldown of Avatar Life Stream by 0.3 seconds. Soul Bond creates a link between Adam Warlock and all nearby characters, causing them to share and distribute all damage taken across the bond. Characters affected also gain a small heal-over-time for a few seconds. If Adam Warlock sustains fatal damage that would take him down, he instead retains 1 health. Each affected target can sustain up to 250 shared damage. Adam will gain limited slow free-flight while Soul Bond is active. The bond breaks under the following conditions: When the bond duration of 6 seconds expires. If too much damage is sustained, exceeding the 250 damage per affected ally. If Adam Warlock or affected allies leave the link's range. His Ultimate Ability, Karmic Revival, creates a quantum zone that automatically revives any fallen allies that are within the zone's radius. The quantum zone will continuously track allies to revive them within the time frame of 10 seconds. The zone can only revive each character once. Characters are briefly invincible when being revived, and gain bonus health equal to 70% of their maximum health for 5 seconds.

The quantum zone will continuously track allies to revive them within the time frame of 10 seconds. The zone can only revive each character once. Characters are briefly invincible when being revived, and gain bonus health equal to 70% of their maximum health for 5 seconds. The zone's radius is based on Adam’s current position, and works even while he is in Regenerative Cocoon. Weaknesses [ ] Susceptible to dives and flanking if his flying gauge is low. Regenerative Cocoon has a very long cooldown of 105 seconds. Cosmic Cluster shares ammo with Quantum Magic. Despite his high burst healing, he lacks sustained healing due to the longer cooldown of his Avatar Life Stream. In addition, he relies heavily on the positioning of his allies in order to maximize the bouncing healing of this ability. Adam cannot be far away from his teammates if he wants to heal them. Karmic Revival's range is not very high, meaning allies that are too far away from it won't be revived. In addition, the player must be careful when using this ability to avoid reviving characters only for them to be taken down again in succession. Adam Warlock is completely vulnerable while channeling this ability, and if executed before creating the quantum zone, the ability will go on a cooldown before activating. Characters revive with only 30% of their max health. Adam Warlock himself cannot be revived by this ability. His abilities require his allies to be grouped up near him in order to maximize his value. As Adam, you should take careful note of where your allies are positioned at all times, and try to coordinate with them to not split off too far from you so that your abilities can gain the maximum value. Compared to other Strategists, Adam Warlock is the only one aside from Mantis who does not have access to on-demand healing with his primary weapon, with his primary healing output instead coming from his Avatar Life Stream ability with limited charges. As such, it is not recommended to run him as a main healer as it can potentially leave your team without healing when they need it most. Adam's primary attack is Quantum Magic, which fires a hitscan shot from his staff that deals very solid damage. Alternatively, Adam can use his secondary fire, Cosmic Cluster, to charge up a rapid-fire volley of up to five projectiles. While each individual shot does less damage than his primary and lacks the ability to headshot, it is capable of dealing quick, un-reactable bursts to a single target. Thanks to these two attacks, compared to other Strategists, Adam makes up for his less consistent healing output with significantly higher damage output, allowing him to participate directly in a fight while supporting his team. While Quantum Magic is subject to damage falloff at 20 meters or further, Cosmic Cluster is not, making it a better choice for laying down suppressive fire at long ranges. Note that both of these attacks use the same ammo pool, so keep an eye on how many shots you have left so you can effectively maximize the usage of both attacks. Another thing to note is that if you charge up a Cosmic Cluster, it will always go up to its maximum of five shots, even if fewer than five shots remain in his current ammo. Avatar Life Stream is Adam's primary means of healing. With it, Adam will heal the targeted ally and any allies around them, doling out a significant amount of health to a large amount of players almost instantly. If no ally is targeted, Adam will heal himself instead. This ability works best when your teammates are clustered close together so you can maximize your spread of healing with each cast.

If no ally is targeted, Adam will heal himself instead. This ability works best when your teammates are clustered close together so you can maximize your spread of healing with each cast. In a pinch, using this on yourself while you are being targeted can buy you just enough time to escape or have a teammate come to your aid. Be wary of the limited charges this ability has. While its cooldown is fast, using the stream recklessly can potentially leave your team without healing when they need it most. Soul Bond is undoubtedly one of the most powerful abilities in the game. Upon activation, Adam creates a bond between himself and all nearby allies, granting them health over time and, most importantly, distributing all damage they take evenly among each bonded ally. If timed correctly, this ability can allow Adam and his teammates to survive immense amounts of damage. The damage cut is proportional to the amount of teammates he is bonded with: the more teammates there are, the more damage is cut. For example, Iron Man's Invincible Pulse Cannon, which deals a whopping 1000 damage to anyone caught in the center of its radius, instead gets cut down to a measly 167 damage split between six players if Adam is bonded with five other teammates. This ability has two main uses: the first is as a tool to allow your team to push forward into the enemy without fear of being burst down. With Soul Bond active, a large group of players can easily power through most sources of damage to reach a favorable vantage. The second is as a tool to save yourself when being targeted. Not only will it give you more durability to work with, but it will often alert nearby teammates that enemies are still nearby when they start taking damage as well, allowing them to come to your aid. Unfortunately, while the ability is incredibly powerful, it is burdened by its incredibly hefty cooldown of 30 seconds, meaning that Adam has to be extremely careful to not waste the ability lest he be left without his strongest tool for almost an entire team fight. While the bond is on cooldown, be extremely careful and do not take unnecessary risks. Regenerative Cocoon is Adam's passive, and essentially serves as a second chance. Upon death, instead of going straight to the respawn timer, Adam will turn into a free-flying spirit visible to all players.

While the bond is on cooldown, be extremely careful and do not take unnecessary risks. Regenerative Cocoon is Adam's passive, and essentially serves as a second chance. Upon death, instead of going straight to the respawn timer, Adam will turn into a free-flying spirit visible to all players. He can move around for a short time to find a spot to revive. After reaching a spot or after time ends, Adam will enter a cocoon for a brief moment before re-emerging, fully healed, and rejuvenated. Alternatively, he can cancel the ability to go straight to the respawn timer, preserving the ability's use. Adam is briefly invincible after leaving the cocoon, allowing him a fighting chance against any enemies who attempt to follow him. This ability can give Adam incredible staying power in a fight, however, its hefty cooldown means that he must be careful to not use it at a suboptimal moment. If you feel that a fight is lost regardless of whether or not you regenerate, it is better to simply cancel the ability and go back to the respawn timer, saving the ability and allowing you to more easily reconvene with your teammates. Adam's ultimate, Karmic Revival, serves as a do-over for his entire team. Upon activation, he will enter a brief cast animation before laying down a golden beacon at his location for 10 seconds. During this time, any KO'd allies within 30 meters of Adam's location will be revived at the beacon, albeit with only 30% of their max health along with 5s of bonus health equal to 70% of their maximum health, preventing most instant KOs right after revival. There is no limit to how many allies that can be revived within the ability's timer, however, if Adam himself dies, then the effect ends prematurely. The revival radius follows Adam's current location, not the beacon, which merely serves as the location where the revived ally will spawn at. This means that Adam can lay down a beacon out of range of a dead ally, and then walk over to them to revive them that way. Remember that the beacon does not entirely restore the health of revived allies, and it is up to other Strategists or Adam himself to restore the rest. DO NOT activate this ultimate out in the open.

Remember that the beacon does not entirely restore the health of revived allies, and it is up to other Strategists or Adam himself to restore the rest. DO NOT activate this ultimate out in the open. Not only is Adam a sitting duck in the middle of his casting animation. Instead, go behind cover near the beginning of a fight and then activate it, so you can not only safely activate it, but also keep allies protected for the initial vulnerable moments of their revival. While it may be tempting to hold onto this ultimate to get a massive team-wide resurrect, waiting until a fight goes awry to activate the ultimate often results in you being overwhelmed before it can get value. Instead, try to activate it before you feel that critical moments in a fight are about to occur so that you and your team have a safety net to fall back on in case things go wrong. Even if the ultimate ends up getting little value, Adam's high damage output means that he will often be able to charge up another ult within one or two more team fights. Personality [ ] https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Adam_Warlock_-_Hero_Spawned_02.ogg Perfection is unattainable. But that should not stop us from trying to achieve it. Adam Warlock Adam Warlock was created to be a perfect human: brilliant, powerful, and pure in heart. From his earliest memories, he has struggled with the expectations placed on him and the concept of what it truly means to be "perfect." His personality reflects this inner conflict: he is noble, contemplative, and frequently burdened by the weight of destiny. Warlock's ponder thoroughly before acting, driven by a strong moral code and a desire to grasp what is right and wrong on a cosmic scale. However, his feeling of purpose can occasionally alienate him; he sees the universe in philosophical terms and struggles to relate with individuals who live regular, flawed lives. Before his resurrection, Adam was a somber, nearly tragic figure. In his despondent search for a meaning to his life, he discovered solace in becoming a force for good. He is deeply introspective, continually pondering his place in the universe, his creators' purposes, and his own nature.

In his despondent search for a meaning to his life, he discovered solace in becoming a force for good. He is deeply introspective, continually pondering his place in the universe, his creators' purposes, and his own nature. He seeks balance not only in the universe, but also inside himself. This contemplative attitude makes him a natural leader and moral compass for others, but he is also prone to existential crises and times of doubt when he believes his actions will break the peace he strives to preserve. Adam is portrayed as a stern and distant philosophical genius who struggles with his dual nature of "perfect" good and chaotic evil as he also carries himself with an almost serene composure. He is a noble and virtuous being, yet quite arrogant. He typically speaks in a highly formal and verbose manner, making extensive use of alliteration to indicate his self-awareness of his power and destiny also giving the sense of wisdom far beyond his years. Warlock's vast viewpoint forms his distinct moral framework, causing him to make unanticipated decisions that favor the broader global balance over traditional good or evil. He also shows compassion and protective emotions for those he loves, such as the Guardians or innocent beings to whom he feels obligated. During an in-game interaction with Wolverine , he mentions his darker side, Magus , a version of himself corrupted by power and fanaticism. Despite not seeing or revealing Adam's transformation into Magus yet, he is known for being willing to absorb Magus into himself, despite the risk of corruption, to save others and the cosmos. Trivia [ ] Adam Warlock's first appearance was as the nameless "perfect being" called Him in " Fantastic Four " (1961) #66 in September 1967, later being reborn and renamed by the High Evolutionary as Warlock in " Marvel Premiere " (1972) #1 . In his first appearance Him was introduced inside a cocoon, before fully emerging from it in " Fantastic Four " (1961) #67 in October 1967. His signature Regenerative Cocoon ability is a direct reference to his comic book origins, where he undergoes metamorphosis to heal or evolve. Adam Warlock's staff is called the Karmic Staff. Angela's gameplay revolves around her Attack Charge passive, a visible gauge that empowers the damage of her primary fire. The gauge will decrease each time she lands a successful primary fire. She can build-up Attack Charge by flying forward with her free flight, Seraphic Soar, and by blocking damage with her secondary fire, Shielded Stance. Angela can switch between her spear and axe weapons by using two separate abilities: Wingblade Ascent has Angela soaring to the sky, giving her free flight movement, and giving her access to the Spears of Ichor stance. Divine Judgement has Angela performing a powerful dive attack, creating a Divine Judgement Zone, an area-of-effect aura that provides bonus health and increased attack speed to Angela and nearby allies, while dealing damage-over-time to enemies in radius. Upon descending, Angela will switch to her Axes of Ichor stance. Her primary fire changes depending on which stance she is: Spears of Ichor is a stab forward with high range. At full Attack Charge, the stab also launches enemies up. Players can weave her primary fire with the default melee attack button to animation cancel and increase her damage-per second. Axes of Ichor is a four-hit combo with her twin axes. The fourth hit propels Angela forward, which allows her to stick close to her targets. Her secondary fire, Shielded Stance, has Angela creating a shield that can absorb both melee and ranged damage. Each time damage is blocked her Attack Charge gauge increases. Assassin's Charge, which can only be used while in the Spears of Ichor stance, has Angela charging fast with her spear and becoming immune to knockback effects. If she hits an opponent, the victim will be carried briefly through the air. Angela can hit up to two enemies at once with this ability. Her Ultimate, Heven's Retribution, has Angela hurling her spear to a targeted area. Enemies caught in the impact zone will be temporarily bound by the ribbons on the spear and tethered to it. Activating the Ultimate again will result in Angela leaping towards the spear, damaging enemies and creating a Divine Judgement Zone.

Angela to Thor Angela is characterized as a powerful, proud, and driven warrior goddess. She has a strong sense of obligation, not only to her heritage, but also to what she believes is right. She is self-sufficient and independent, having been bred as a hunter and schooled by the angels of Heven to fight, command and survive. Described as self-confident, cocky, and quick-to-anger demeanor, she embraces a strong sense of combat and confronts great opponents, including armies and monsters, even when the odds are stacked against her. She is a skillful and fierce battler who faces difficulties with reasoning, strategy, and unflinching confidence. Unlike many of her peers, Angela does not rely on authority or tradition to lead her; instead, she trusts her intuition and makes her own decisions, carving a path that represents her ideals and own code of honor.

Despite being one of Odin 's children, Angela heavily despises her father. For the majority of her life, Angela had no idea who her real parents were. So, for years, she perceived Odin as a despotic god-king rather as her father. When she discovers the truth, she feels betrayed, angry, and disgusted for the lie her life had been, as well as Odin's perceived failure to save or find her when she was still an infant during the war between Asgard and Heven. Despite her battling nature, Angela is very protective and compassionate of those she cares about, such as her younger sister, Laussa , and her friends, including the Guardians of the Galaxy , which she was a member of for a time. Angela, despite her rugged, battle-hardened exterior, is thoughtful and sympathetic, emphasizing loyalty and connection with those she trusts.  While she can be cautious and guarded, she is also inquiring and willing to confront injustice, revealing that her strength is balanced by empathy and moral clarity. Trivia [ ] Angela was originally a character from the Spawn comic series, created by Todd McFarlane and Neil Gaiman. Her first appearance was in " Spawn " (1992) #9 in April 1993. A legal dispute between McFarlane and Gaiman ensued for the character's rights, with Gaiman being allowed to introduce a different version of Angela into the Marvel Universe. Brian Michael Bendis created her new origin story, being Odin's firstborn and Thor 's older sister, with her real name being Aldrif Odinsdottir. She debuted in " Age of Ultron " (2013) #10 in June 2013. In " Nowhere Left to Run ," Hela is confirmed as a member of Asgard’s royal family. This marks the first instance in which Angela and Hela are adapted as sisters. Within the lore of Season 4 , Angela becomes Laussa ’s guardian while searching for her lost sister, who was kidnapped by Hela. In the comics, however, this is reversed: Angela is the one who kidnaps Laussa, not Hela.

Her kit revolves around Fortune , a resource that's used by her abilities and is gained from hitting enemies. A max of 1000 Fortune can be held at a time. 50 Fortune is gained from any attack hitting an enemy, 300 Fortune is gained from hitting an enemy using her Turn of Fortune ability, 150 Fortune is gained from hitting an enemy with Phantom Pursuit, 0/50/200/500 Fortune can be gained from using the Tablet of Destinies relic, and 300 Fortune is gained from attacking an enemy with Claw Strike. 50% of Fortune is lost upon death, and 200 is always lost upon death.

50% of Fortune is lost upon death, and 200 is always lost upon death. Hitting an enemy for the first time applys Jinxed to them, Jinxed is a status effect that causes critical hits to have a chance not deal bonus damage. Can climb on walls and double jump. Her primary fire; Feline Fury, attacks enemies quickly in front of her, allowing her to gain Fortune quickly. Her secondary fire; Fortune's Favor, allows her to use her Fortune to gain 2 different attacks: Claw Whip is an enhanced primary fire with more range that gives her up to 50 bonus health per enemy hit with it, and costs 150 Fortune to use. Phantom Pursuit is a anchored dash that lets her attacks enemies at a range before returning to her original position. While using Phantom Pursuit she is untargetable, and costs 300 Fortune to use. Cat's Cradle is a quick lunging slash that can hit multiple enemies in its path. This ability has two charges. Turn of Fortune is a ranged attack with minimal damage that if successfully hit grants her 300 Fortune and 50 bonus health. Gilded Deal is a shop that lets Black Cat spend her fortune to buy one of 6 relics: Tablet of Destinies is a 100 Fortune cost relic that grants her a random amount of Fortune up to 500. Not for long... https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Black_Cat_-_Hero_Spawned_02.ogg Black Cat Felicia Hardy, better known as the infamous thief Black Cat, is defined by a playful, enigmatic, and fiercely independent nature. A world-class burglar with a refined taste for high-stakes heists, she thrives on the thrill of the chase and the challenge of the "impossible job". Her background as a former member of the Thieves Guild is reflected in her supreme confidence and professional pride, viewing her craft not merely as crime, but as a form of art. She carries herself with a flirtatious and elusive demeanor, often using her charm and wit to keep both allies and enemies off-balance.

She carries herself with a flirtatious and elusive demeanor, often using her charm and wit to keep both allies and enemies off-balance. Unlike many heroes or villains, Felicia lacks a rigid moral compass, often allowing her loyalties to be swayed by the highest bidder. This mercenary opportunism makes her a wildcard in the multiversal conflict; she is just as likely to aid a hero for the right price as she is to accept a contract from Mayor Wilson Fisk to infiltrate the Sanctum Sanctorum . To Black Cat, the ends—and the paycheck—usually justify the means, regardless of the target. Her most complex dynamic remains her relationship with Spider-Man , whom she views with a mixture of genuine affection and professional amusement. She relishes the "cat and mouse" game they share, often teasing the wall-crawler for his strict adherence to responsibility. While she occasionally finds herself on the side of justice, it is typically motivated by her personal connection to her "Spider" or the sheer excitement of the situation, rather than a commitment to the greater good. Trivia [ ] Black Cat's first appearance was in " The Amazing Spider-Man " (1963) #194 in July 1979. Following an initial teaser in the final gallery card of Season 6: Night at the Museum —which depicted a white fox and a black cat alongside Deadpool —the developers officially confirmed Black Cat and White Fox as the featured heroes for Season 7 via social media. [ 1 ] One week before the Season 7 announcement, her "wanted" billboard—which could be found on the Times Square map—appeared with claw marks on it as an easter egg. Official description Black Panther is Duelist hero in Marvel Rivals , and is the 8th hero introduced to the game's roster. He currently has one team-up ability: Gamma Charge — with Hulk and The Thing Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Strengths 1.2 Weaknesses 2 Costumes 3 Abilities 4 Strategy 5 Personality 6 Achievements 7 Proficiency Challenges 7.1 Challenges 7.2 Rewards 8 Gallery 9 Trivia 10 References 11 Navigation Overview [ ] Strengths [ ] An agile melee-focused Duelist who specializes in darting around the battlefield through high-speed dash attacks and executing vulnerable targets. Capable of getting in and out of combat while dishing out high amounts of damage to his opponents. Can run on walls and perform double jumps after detaching from it. Has slightly higher max health and base movement speed compared to other Duelists. His passive, Panther's Cunning, allows him to deal 20% more damage when below 100 health. This makes Black Panther a formidable fighter in isolated duels.

Has slightly higher max health and base movement speed compared to other Duelists. His passive, Panther's Cunning, allows him to deal 20% more damage when below 100 health. This makes Black Panther a formidable fighter in isolated duels. Almost all of his attacks apply Vibranium Mark on his targets, which can be used to refresh the cooldown on his abilities and also provide him with bonus health. His primary fire, Vibranium Claws, deals damage in quick succession. This, combined with his higher speed, allows him to stick to his targets efficiently. His secondary fire, Spear Toss, is a high-velocity projectile thrown in an arc that creates an area-of-effect blast that applies a Vibranium Mark to hit enemies. This is Black Panther's main way to apply the mark from safe distances, and is often used as a way to either poke enemies before attacking or dispatch low-health targets trying to flee. Spirit Rend and Spinning Kick are two mobility skills that deal damage. Spinning Kick also applies a Vibranium Mark. His Ultimate, Bast's Descent, summons a giant spectral panther that lunges forward, covering a huge area, while applying Vibranium Marks to enemies hit and simultaneously refreshing the cooldown of Spirit Rend. Weaknesses [ ] His normal melee attacks have a relatively low range, forcing him to stay close and personal with his targets, which leaves him open to retaliation from the enemy team. Relies on consistently applying Vibranium Mark to targets to maintain his bonus health and to refresh his cooldowns. Relies on quick decision-making, timing, and accuracy to aim Black Panther in the direction of enemies, as the cooldowns on his abilities are quite punishing. Very vulnerable to enemy fire if both Spirit Rend and Spinning Kick are on cooldown. It's best to use Black Panther behind the enemy backline. Always try to position yourself where the enemy team can't see you. You can do this by traversing the map with cover to reach the enemy supports before engaging. Like the first suggestion, it's best when they don't know you're coming, giving you slightly more time to eliminate them. Engage with your team. It's important to play Marvel Rivals together. Black Panther T'Challa, also known as the Black Panther and the king of Wakanda, is a highly disciplined, intelligent, and ethically grounded leader who carries the weight of both a warrior and a king. As ruler of the African nation of Wakanda, he exemplifies a rare blend of regal authority and emotional reserve, frequently deliberating before acting. T'Challa is known for being polite, respectful, caring, and honors loyalty for those around him, whom he considers friends, such as the Avengers and the X-Men and a high level of regard for others, particularly his late father, T'Chaka , and her younger sister Shuri whom he cares about and loves. When his father died, he was ready to take his rightful role as King of Wakanda. He is intensely protective of his people and culture, and while he cherishes tradition, he is not hesitant to question it when justice or progress requires it. T’Challa strongly believes in doing what is right, but he is also a realist. He understands the complexities of leadership, diplomacy, and war, and sometimes must make difficult decisions that weigh individual freedom against the needs of the many. He is not blindly idealistic but instead, he strives for balance between his duty to Wakanda and his role as a global hero. While often stoic, T'Challa shows a warm sense of humor with loved ones and openly expresses emotions like grief and rage when situations call for it. He religiously worships the goddess Bast as the mantle of the Black Panther and deeply respected Wakanda's customs and ideals and is ready to intervene if necessary.  In combat, he is a valiant warrior, great tactician, and unrivaled fighter, but he wants peace whenever possible.

Storm was formerly his partner, and she was the queen of Wakanda. They are nonetheless equals in power and vision, both rulers in their own way, battling for a better society which their emotional bond remained strong, demonstrating mutual admiration and care. Black Widow can switch between her melee and ranged modes freely. Her ranged primary fire, Red Room Rifle, is a single shot that deals high damage. Her secondary fire activates Straight Shooter, which enters a first-person zoomed view to land more precise shots, which are not affected by damage distance falloff. Her secondary fire activates Straight Shooter, which enters a first-person zoomed view to land more precise shots, which are not affected by damage distance falloff. If the player is currently in her melee mode, she will switch automatically to the rifle when activating the secondary fire. Her melee primary fire, Widow's Bite Baton, has her dual-wielding batons to quickly strike at enemies in close range. Edge Dancer is a low-range kick that knocks enemies back in the air; the player can press it again upon a successful hit to grapple towards the same or different target for a follow-up kick. This is Black Widow's main move to fend off backline divers such as Black Panther , Spider-Man , and Iron Fist . It can also be used to push enemies off of ledges. Fleet Foot grants her increased movement speed and access to a higher jump, which aids her in repositioning on the battlefield and to also outrun opponents. Her Ultimate, Electro-Plasma Explosion, deals high damage in a large radius, leaves enemies vulnerable for a short duration, and also leaves pools of red plasma on the ground that slows enemies, reducing their movement speed by 55%; this is one the highest slowing percentages in the game. This synergizes with her primary fire, allowing Black Widow to pin down and more easily eliminate high-priority opponents such as Strategists. Weaknesses [ ] Despite having access to melee options, Black Widow lacks the survivability to stay in the frontline; her melee options must be used sparingly to avoid run-ins with backline divers as much as possible. Has no defensive means to gain bonus health or self-healing. Switching between her weapons can feel a bit counter-intuitive at first to deal with immediate threats; the brief moment when entering into Straight Shooter must be accounted for. Edge Dancer has a very low range and a rather long cooldown. Enemies with high mobility tools can counter the slowing effect of her Ultimate. Black Widow to Winter Soldier Natasha is fundamentally cold, calculated, educated, and strategic. She was trained as a spy for decades since from a young age in the brutal Soviet Red Room program, where she learnt to read and kill people, manipulate circumstances, and stay three steps ahead of her adversaries. She could convincingly play being friendly, flirty, timid, vulnerable, and afraid. For the most part, she's a calm, strong-willed, independent and smart woman, being able to speak several languages and imitate accents at her job. Romanoff usually maintained a controlled, almost emotionless persona to keep whatever she was thinking a secret unless she was with individuals she completely trusted.

For the most part, she's a calm, strong-willed, independent and smart woman, being able to speak several languages and imitate accents at her job. Romanoff usually maintained a controlled, almost emotionless persona to keep whatever she was thinking a secret unless she was with individuals she completely trusted. Her intellect is always engaged analyzing, planning, and adapting. She is a master of espionage and deception. After years of expertise as an assassin, she is a cold-blooded individual who kills without hesitation, and her abilities often make her more dangerous than many enhanced heroes, especially she was boosted by a Russian version of a super soldier serum which gives peak human condition and enhanced longevity, hence her appearance is nothing in her actual age. Behind her cold exterior, however, is a woman dealing with guilt, trauma, and redemption. Natasha bears the burden of her history for years, like the shadows of assassinations, betrayals, and the people she harmed prior to joining the Avengers . This guilt motivates her to seek for justice, make amends, and defend others, particularly those who have been deceived or weaponized in the same manner she has been. She's deeply loyal to the few people she admits into her inner circle and frequently serves as a quiet emotional anchor for the team. Black Widow, like other heroes, has a strong connection with those who understand her grief, past, and search for redemption. She has a deep bond and friendship with Clint , who regards her as family, cares and worries about Bucky because he understands her like no one else, and Logan recognizes the strength behind Natasha's scars. In recent events while living in the 2099 Timeline , she becomes the head of the Red Room, which she now controls. Despite everything, Natasha is a survivor, someone who perseveres even when all else fails. She doesn't consider herself a hero in the traditional sense, but her actions repeatedly demonstrate otherwise. Blade is also immune to crowd control during the first 0.4 seconds of the block. For every 200 damage that is blocked, he regains 1 charge for Daywalker Dash. Daywalker Dash causes Blade to surge forward and apply a debuff to the first enemy he collides with. If the sword is equipped, Blade will perform a cleaving strike that applies stacks of healing reduction each hit. If Bloodline Awakening is active, each hit also grants an attack speed stack. If the gun is equipped, Blade will shoot a follow-up shot that inflicts slow. Bloodline Awakening allows Blade to toggle an awakened state where he boosts movement speed, gains lifesteal, suffers from healing reduction, and is forced to use his sword. While in this state, he can build up a meter that increases his attack speed with every slash he lands (up to 10 stacks). Excess healing is converted into bonus health. While above 5 stacks, Blade will perform a whirlwind slash at the end of every combo. Landing every hit of it will also grant 1 additional stack. Blade can see low-health enemies through whiles while in this state. His Ultimate, Thousand-Fold Slash, charges up a forward dash that deals damage on impact and then a barrage of laido strikes within the attack range. Enemies hit are inflicted with 40% healing reduction for 4 seconds. The longer Blade charges up the attack, the longer the dash distance becomes. Blade also restores health from damage dealt even if Bloodline Awakening is not active. When paired with Moon Knight , Blade gains access to Eclipse Edge. When activated, Blade dashes forward and enables a 3-second combo window to unleash a Moonblade Combo. Moonblade Combo quickly launches four projectiles that bounce between nearby enemies for damage. While his strikes start off weak, he can quickly become one of the most dangerous up-close fighters in the game the longer he remains left to his own devices. Even outside of that, he can still provide decent ranged damage as well as team utility with a slow and a unique anti-heal property. Blade has two primary positions he wants to take.

Even outside of that, he can still provide decent ranged damage as well as team utility with a slow and a unique anti-heal property. Blade has two primary positions he wants to take. The first is brawling near the frontline, whittling enemies down with his shotgun until noticing an opportune moment to strike and build up damage. Alternatively, he can also flank and attempt to target backline healers, pouncing on top of them to quickly whittle away at their life while being able to shrug off most of their attacks due to his lifesteal and their typically low damage compared to Duelists. Blade excels against compositions that like to hold static positions near the objective. In that situation, he can quickly build up his rage for Bloodline Awakening, allowing him to go on a rampage through the enemy without much hassle. In contrast, he struggles against foes who can easily keep their distance, particularly fliers such as Iron Man or Storm , as he relies on being in a fight constantly to keep himself up. Blade has two primary weapons at his disposal. The first is his Hunter's Shotgun. Unlike other shotgun-type attacks like The Punisher's Deliverance or Human Torch's Fire Cluster, this shotgun doesn't immediately fire out its pellets, but rather fires as a single projectile that then splits into pellets after travelling a set distance. The second is his Ancestral Sword, which is a fairly self-explanatory melee weapon that also has a unique spinning slash in its attack interval that deals more damage. With that in mind, the shotgun's optimal range is actually at medium range (roughly 10-20 meters). While the using the weapon, try to maintain that sweet spot in order to make sure the shot fragments right before it hits the target, causing all the pellets to hit for maximum damage. Keep in mind that the shotgun is a projectile, not a hitscan, so make sure to lead your shots instead of aiming directly at them at further distances. The Ancestral Sword by itself is not particularly impressive, as its slow attack speed and lack of range makes it difficult to secure kills on its own. Where it really shines, however, is its synergy with Blade's primary offensive ability, Bloodline Awakening. Scarlet Shroud gives Blade some much needed survivability.

Where it really shines, however, is its synergy with Blade's primary offensive ability, Bloodline Awakening. Scarlet Shroud gives Blade some much needed survivability. With it, he can block any frontal attacks for a set period of time, significantly reducing their damage. If he mitigates enough damage with the ability, he can also gain an additional charge of his Daywalker Dash. This is a very straightforward block ability. If you ever find yourself in a sticky situation, use this block while backpedaling back to your team or to cover. Additionally, the block grants you complete CC immunity for its initial moments, meaning you cannot be affected by stuns, knockbacks, slows, etc. With that in mind, you can effectively parry certain attacks or CCs, such as Luna Snow's Absolute Zero or Mantis' Spore Slumber. Try to get used to reacting to or reading when enemies will attempt to use such key attacks on you, and time your block to soak up the hit and continue your offense unabated. Daywalker Dash is Blade's primary means of mobility. It is a quick, forward-advancing dash that will end with an additional attack if he collides with an enemy. The attack will differ depending on what weapon he is currently using, and will also have a different effect. If he his holding his gun, he will fire a silver bullet that puts a debuff on the target that reduces their healing received. If he his holding his sword, he will perform the spinning slash from his normal melee cycle, which will slow the enemy. Daywalker Dash has multiple key uses. The first is as a tool to engage on top of an enemy or disengage from a bad fight. The second is as a combo tool in the midst of a fight to supplement his offense. Landing a silver bullet on a key target can be just the edge you need to secure a fight, but alternatively, you can land the sword dash during Bloodline Awakening to quickly build up your rage meter, allowing you to start your rampage earlier. Bloodline Awakening is Blade's bread and butter, and the key to him using his normally weak melee effectively.

Bloodline Awakening is Blade's bread and butter, and the key to him using his normally weak melee effectively. Upon activation, Blade reduces the healing he receives and becomes locked to his Ancestral Sword, but he now gains lifesteal on his attacks and will ramp up his damage and attack speed as he lands continuous hits. The ramping effect has up to ten stacks, and landing a spinning slash from either his normal melee cycle or his Daywalker Dash will instantly grant one stack. With this, his sword goes from unimpressive at best to one of the deadliest weapons in the game. At full charge, he can quickly cleave through anyone he gets close to, while also easily shrugging off their damage thanks to his lifesteal. Focus on hitting characters with low mobility first, such as a frontline tank like Magneto, then shift focus to fragile backliners such as supports once your stacks are built up. No matter what, however, focus on always trying to get hits in as often as possible, as the stacks will quickly decay if you don't continuously deal damage. While the ability is undoubtedly powerful thanks to the offensive boost it gives you, it also has a crippling Catch 22: the reduced healing. When it's active, Blade cannot rely on his supports to keep him alive mid-fight, and is forced to go on the offensive in order to heal enough on his own to supplement his healers. As such, in situations where Blade cannot safely reach the enemy to start damaging them, the ability can actually be a hindrance as it forces healers to spend more time trying to keep you up when there are 4 other teammates they also need to keep an eye. With that in mind, always try to cancel the ability as soon as you reach a safe position to be healed, as that will minimize the amount of downtime needed to get topped back up, letting you and your healers get back into the action faster. Being locked to melee can also be a hindrance, as if you're out of Daywalker Dashes against a foe that can easily keep their distance, you're left with no options to attack them. In that scenario, quickly cancel the ability and begin whittling them down with your shotgun.

Blade's ultimate, Thousand-fold Slash, has Blade charge up a forward dash that leaves behind a trail of blindingly fast sword strikes. The longer he charges, the longer the trail becomes, and foes within the trail suffer heavy damage as well as reduced healing. Due to the ultimate's slow startup and predictable trajectory, it can be difficult to land against most enemies, especially ones with fast movement. However, where it truly shines is with its zoning capabilities, as it can effectively split a key area in two to isolate enemies from each other, allowing you a golden opportunity to take out an exposed target. If all else fails, using it as a combo tool with a crowd-control ultimate such as Angela's Heven's Retribution or Groot's Strangling Prison can net devastating results. He is a half-human, half-vampire hybrid known as the "Daywalker," who wanders alone, motivated by a personal vendetta against vampires after one murdered his mother during childbirth. This event has shaped him into a hardened, stoic warrior who typically avoids people, preferring seclusion to emotional connection. Despite his violent nature, Blade follows a rigid moral code. He refuses to take human blood and devotes his life to defending humanity against supernatural threats, particularly vampires. His sense of justice is powerful and frequently harsh, which can put him at conflict with more idealistic heroes or traditional law enforcement. He is not hesitant to utilize lethal force if he believes it is necessary to defeat evil. He is someone who fights for the common good but does not always adhere to traditional heroic methods or ideals.

Blade has a clear mission: to slay his enemies and protect humanity from supernatural threats as he fights with a gritty and violent manner. Every day, he risks his life for it, frequently alone, without recognition, and with little personal return. Despite his cold attitude and rugged exterior, Blade does have a dry, sarcastic, and often dark humor. He also secretly enjoys one of Luna Snow 's K-pop songs, which he plays while hunting his adversaries. This adds to Eric's personality by demonstrating that he is not simply serious all the time, but also has this side to him. Eric is not heartless, as underneath him lurks a man plagued with empathy and guilt. He has witnessed far too much pain to remain apathetic. His compassion is typically manifested in subtle ways, such as preserving innocent lives, guiding others who have been cursed, or providing quiet respect to allies who earn his confidence. He rarely exhibits emotion publicly, but when he does, it's powerful because it feels genuine and earned. Blade's personality indicates a severe psychological conflict. He battles the vampire side of his nature on a daily basis, resisting the bloodlust that comes with his abilities. This inner battle lends a sorrowful dimension to his character; he is continually battling to remain human in both body and spirit. While he frequently appears cold and unfeeling, moments of loyalty, sacrifice, and even love reveal that beneath the armor of retribution is a man still looking for peace and belonging. Strategy [ ] Captain America is a hyper-aggressive dive tank who excels at diving in and out of combat and being a constant nuisance for the enemy backline. While his damage output may seem low on paper, his incredible mobility allows him to easily weave in and out of danger while still getting hits in, allowing his damage to add up significantly over time as he looks for an opportune moment to strike. Cap does lack the tools necessary to be a frontline wall for his team against large amounts of damage, so it is not recommended to run him as a solo tank. As a dive hero, one of the most important things to learn is how to pick your fights. Your exceptional mobility gives you the option to freely take or abandon any fight with enough foresight, which is an extremely valuable luxury. Before engaging, take a moment to see which enemies are on the field, so you know who you should target, who you should avoid, or even how long you can remain in the fight before you need to retreat. Prioritize backline supports or ranged characters first and foremost (ex: Loki , Luna Snow or Hela ), as forcing them to focus on you instead of on other matters frees up the rest of your team to make a play. In contrast, avoid brawl characters or characters with excessive CC or health (ex: Vanguards, Wolverine or Winter Soldier ), as not only will you have trouble taking them down by yourself, but they can quickly overwhelm you if you prolong your fight against them for too long.

In contrast, avoid brawl characters or characters with excessive CC or health (ex: Vanguards, Wolverine or Winter Soldier ), as not only will you have trouble taking them down by yourself, but they can quickly overwhelm you if you prolong your fight against them for too long. Map knowledge and cooldown management is a crucial part of surviving in the enemy's backline. Always make sure you have a movement option ready to make a quick escape before engaging, and keep careful note of where health packs, flank routes, and escape paths are located so you can get out of danger and recover quickly between fights. Sentinel Strike is your primary means of attack. By default, it is two quick melee strikes, however, after landing two strikes, it becomes an auto-locking shield throw that deals more damage and can be done up to four times. While the shield throw is what you want to use most of the time due to the higher damage, there are times where using just the melee attack is more useful. This can be done by using only the quick melee button instead of your primary fire, which is V by default on PC. The melee attack can not only hit multiple enemies at once due to its AoE, but it also pierces barriers from heroes like Doctor Strange or Magneto , allowing you to pressure their shield and damage them simultaneously. On that note, it is recommended to bind the quick melee to a more comfortable button to make it easier to integrate into your gameplay. You can actually cancel the animation of the shield throw to reduce the recovery between strikes, thus increasing your overall damage output. Simply hold sprint, build up your shield throws, and then time letting go of the attack button when you hear the shield hit the target. Listen for sound rather than relying on sight, and if done correctly, Cap should immediately reset to his neutral position after the attack lands, allowing him to throw out another attack right away. Leading Dash is your primary means of movement around the battlefield. It allows Cap to sprint around at high speeds, and from it, he can perform a Fearless Leap to jump high into the air, giving him even more movement to work with. As Cap, you should be using this at almost all times.

As Cap, you should be using this at almost all times. It has no cooldown nor does it have any limited resource, so you can use it to quickly run around the map, get to cover, or just chase someone down. Vibranium Energy Saw is a solid ranged burst tool. Captain America throws his shield forward, dealing a decent chunk of damage. It also has an auto-locking ricochet property, making it a reliable option even against evasive targets. With its ability to hit multiple enemies in one go, it can be a good idea to throw this at a distant group of enemies before engaging to build up some ultimate charge. With its auto-lock property on ricochet, it makes for a solid finisher when you just need one more hit in to KO a target. If you see an injured enemy, throw your shield at a wall next to them or at the floor around them to guarantee a KO. For the latter situation, getting some elevation with Fearless Leap before doing so is recommended. Liberty Rush is a strong movement option in Cap's arsenal. Cap will charge forward with his shield raised, dealing a small chunk of damage. This is a great option for rushing to an enemy or to get out from a bad situation. Getting some elevation with Fearless Leap and then using Liberty Rush in the air can get you out of tons of sticky situations. Cap is immune to CC during the charge, allowing him to power through stuns and other movement effects, albeit only for a brief moment. Be wary when using this ability in the middle of a crowd or in an enclosed space, as hitting a wall or enemy will automatically stop the charge. With that in mind, some enemies will intentionally try to take the hit to limit the distance you travel with the charge, thus giving them more time to shoot you down. Super Soldier Slam is yet another amazing movement option. Captain America can quickly slam down to Earth while airborne, traveling a solid distance and damaging and knocking up any enemies he lands on.

Super Soldier Slam is yet another amazing movement option. Captain America can quickly slam down to Earth while airborne, traveling a solid distance and damaging and knocking up any enemies he lands on. Like with Liberty Rush, this ability can be used to both engage on top of the enemy while dealing some damage as well as a quick escape after getting elevation with Fearless Leap. After the enemy gets launched up from the attack, aim vertically to account for their upward trajectory, getting some easy hits in while their movement is locked to a predictable path. Living Legend is Cap's primary means of mitigation. Cap raises his shield in front of him, blocking a limited amount of damage from the front and reflecting any projectiles shot at it back at random directions at 50% efficiency. Due to its low health, the shield shouldn't be used to attempt to soak up tons of damage for your team. Instead, treat it like a personal barrier, only pulling it up to protect against big damage attacks or CC that can stop you in your tracks. Make sure to put the shield away ASAP, especially before it gets fully destroyed, so it can recharge as quickly as possible. Cap's Ultimate is Freedom Charge, which bolsters the Captain's already impressive durability. While active, Captain America continuously generates a large amount of overhealth for himself, as well as leaving behind a red, white and blue trail that grants overhealth for teammates who stand in it. In addition, during the ult, Cap can launch up enemies with his sprint or shield. This ultimate allows Cap to dive straight into the fray with almost no fear, as his extremely high health combined with the quickly regenerating overhealth makes it near-impossible for anything short of either a powerful one-shot or massive focus fire to KO him. When the ult it active, run straight for the enemy backline and start wailing on their supports, forcing their frontline to pull back and support them and giving your team space to push up. Alternatively, you can also use it as a budget defensive ult for your team similar to a support. Cap's team-up with Winter Soldier, Captain's Spirit, bolsters the potential of Cap's sidekick by giving him an additional movement and damage option while also granting a powerful synchronized attack that deals damage, slows enemies, and grants overhealth to allies within the radius. The team-up mostly serves to bolster Winter Soldier more than it does Cap, as even with the synchronized attack, it is difficult to get off in the midst of combat due to you and Winter Soldier's roles in combat being so different. Personality [ ] https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Captain_America_-_Setup_03.ogg Almost everyone knows what's right. Not everyone does it. Captain America Captain America, widely regarded as the world's first avenger, the man out of time, and a great superhero and soldier, who is distinguished by his courage, compassion, patriotism, and morality. He always possessed a good and honest mentality, intolerant of injustice and abuses of power. Steve, who grew up weak and small in Brooklyn, discovered on his own that true strength is having the guts to confront maltreatment, regardless of one's power, and having compassion for the innocent. He has an unshakeable moral compass and a strong sense of integrity. From the start, even before becoming Captain America, Steve is extremely selfless and brave and determined to stand up for what is right. His acts are motivated by a deep sense of justice and morality. He is said to as a "good man" rather than a "perfect soldier," and he sticks to his principles regardless of the circumstances. At his core, Steve is highly selfless and altruistic. He continuously prioritizes the needs of others over his own, willing to risk his safety, reputation, and even his life to protect others who cannot defend themselves.

At his core, Steve is highly selfless and altruistic. He continuously prioritizes the needs of others over his own, willing to risk his safety, reputation, and even his life to protect others who cannot defend themselves. He fights for freedom and for the people against Nazi and HYDRA threats during WWII, facing one of his enemies, the Red Skull . Despite having been converted into a perfect fighter by the Super Soldier Serum, he retains his original values and personality. And even though years passed after his reawakening in the year 2099 , he maintained the same values he had in the 1940s. He is awakened far from his own time and forced into a future of galactic empires, collapsing timelines, and cosmic threats, yet he remains grounded in purpose, not certainty. Steve does not believe he was brought back by accident; he believes there is always a reason, even if he cannot see it. When everything familiar is swept away, his belief in meaning, rather than fate or prophecy, keeps him grounded. Despite being surrounded by superior technology and godlike forces, Steve's strength is fundamentally human. He is reflective, observant, and slow to speak, frequently dealing with loss and change within rather than externally. Furthermore, Steve's personality revolves around loyalty and protectiveness. He is intensely loyal to his friends and allies, particularly Bucky Barnes , whom he considers family. Bucky has watched out for Steve since they were young, protecting him from bullies and the harsh realities of life in 1930s Brooklyn. Even after Steve became Captain America, the balance shifted, but their friendship was unshakeable. Steve's steadfast faith in Bucky, even after he became the Winter Soldier, eventually saved him. Others saw Bucky a killer, but Steve saw his best friend, the man he grew up with leading Bucky's belief saved him when he couldn't trust himself. He is fiercely loyal to his friends and country. This commitment extends to the Avengers and the people he fights for, making him a trustworthy and staunch ally, tactician and leader. He frequently takes on a mentoring, almost older brother position within the team, constantly watching out for others and urging them to do the right thing.

This commitment extends to the Avengers and the people he fights for, making him a trustworthy and staunch ally, tactician and leader. He frequently takes on a mentoring, almost older brother position within the team, constantly watching out for others and urging them to do the right thing. His leadership style is based on trust, boldness, and consistency, and he inspires others with his actions rather than words. Others follow him because he continually puts innocent lives and shared sacrifice ahead of personal safety or glory. Even when confronted with an enemy he cannot overcome, particularly when that enemy is his closest friend, Steve adjusts without losing his ideals. He fights defensively, buys time, coordinates allies, and relies on others' skills, demonstrating the prudence of a leader rather than the stubbornness of a soldier. His courage is not impulsive; it is planned. Even in the midst of combat or moral dilemma, people naturally go toward him for guidance due to his stable character and unwavering commitment. Many generations look up to him, as he serves as a role model for many people, embodying honor, courage, and kindness. His demeanor is that of a defender and a leader, someone who fights not for fame or power, but because he believes in doing the right thing at any costs. After years of being awakened and caught in the middle of conflicting timelines, Steve eventually accepts that he belongs again, not because the world requires Captain America, but because the people around him do. His greatest power is not his shield or strength, but his unrelenting will to stand with others until they, too, find their way back, as he did. Dagger's Strengths [ ] Her primary fire, Lightforce Dagger, is a quick projectile that bounces on terrain. This ability can both heal allies or damage enemies, and has a semi-tracking feature which will cause the projectile to hit the ally or enemy closest to the aiming reticle. Four small white ticks appear around her allies or enemies to visually show where the projectiles will home in. There is a circle that appears when she uses it, healing the person she was aiming for, nearby allies and herself. Her secondary fire, Dagger Storm, launches a projectile that creates a large bubble of light on impact, providing healing-over-time. This is Dagger's primary tool of self-sustain. This ability can be attached to any surface, including walls and ceilings. The healing bubble persists even if the player switches to Cloak. Light Explosion creates a bright white, rectangular spell field that advances in a straight line along the casting path, healing all allies caught by it. This ability also provides a 15% healing bonus from all sources for 4 seconds when hitting allies. Shadow's Embrace allows Dagger to switch to Cloak. Doing this automatically reloads Lightforce Dagger's ammo when swapping back to Dagger. Their Ultimate, Eternal Bond, has both Cloak & Dagger perform four rapid spinning dashes along the ground, leaving a persistent energy carpet that simultaneously heals allies and damages enemies that step over it. Players can change the direction of this ability between the dash pauses. Each individual energy carpet lasts for 5 seconds. Dagger's Weaknesses [ ] Susceptible to dives as she lacks any form of mobility outside of her Ultimate. Lightforce Dagger does very little damage; she relies on Cloak to ward off aggressive enemies. Veil of Lightforce does not pass through walls or other terrain. Dagger Storm is one of the only abilities that can heal her, as if she is getting dived and no one is near, she cannot use Lightforce Daggers healing circle, and she is very vulnerable if she gets pushed or pulled out. She can still be damaged and taken down during Eternal Bond, especially by high burst damage.

She can still be damaged and taken down during Eternal Bond, especially by high burst damage. In addition, on certain maps with high terrain inclinations, Cloak & Dagger may get stuck during the dashes. Cloak's Strengths [ ] His primary fire, Darkforce Cloak, is a channeled energy beam that deals high consecutive damage. This ability has infinite ammo and the same auto-aim effect as Dagger's; Cloak will automatically attack the nearest enemy within its radius. His secondary fire, Dark Teleportation, creates a large energy field around Cloak that temporarily phases him and all nearby allies, making them invisible to enemies and immune to all damage and crowd control effects. Cloak and his allies also gain movement speed while within the energy field. Cloak gains a limited form of free-flight during this ability. The invulnerability granted by this ability can even avoid Ultimates, such as Iron Man 's Invincible Pulse Cannon and Jeff the Land Shark 's It's Jeff! Terror Cape, which visually appears similar to Dagger's Veil of Lightforce, creates a dark purple, rectangular spell field that advances in a straight line along the casting path, obstructing enemy vision. This ability also inflicts enemies with the Vulnerability debuff, which amplifies all damage taken by 20% for 3 seconds. Light's Embrace allows Cloak to switch to Dagger. His Ultimate is the same as when controlling Dagger, with the same attributes. Cloak's Weaknesses [ ] Darkforce Cloak has limited range, requiring Cloak to get into mid-close range. This, combined with his low max health, can make it risky to engage directly against enemies without the rest of the team. Cannot heal his team. Dagger Representing a "yin and yang" pair of inseparable street vigilantes, Cloak and Dagger are distinguished by their tragic past, profound sense of connection, and contrasting powers, with Cloak controlling darkness/teleportation and Dagger creating light/healing, fighting together against crimes, threats and evil forces. Tyrone Johnson, also known as Cloak, is a personality identified by a strong feeling of duty and a dark, brooding intensity. He is highly introspective and carries the weight of the world on his shoulders, frequently serving as the "conscience" of the partnership. His personality is defined by a constant struggle with the "Hunger"—a cold, black void within him that pushes him to seek the light or life force of others. Despite the overpowering "hunger" of his dark powers, he nevertheless has a strong sense of justice. He is committed to combating crime and protecting the oppressed, and he is a meticulous planner who frequently serves as a steady, calculated contrast to Tandy's rash actions. Despite being burdened by his powers and the dread he sees, he serves as a faithful protector, particularly to Dagger. Tandy Bowen, also known as Dagger, has a personality that stands out from her partner's. She personifies resilience and hope, frequently acting with a more impetuous and energetic intensity.

Tandy Bowen, also known as Dagger, has a personality that stands out from her partner's. She personifies resilience and hope, frequently acting with a more impetuous and energetic intensity. While Cloak is the shadow, Tandy is the literal and figurative light; she is more outgoing and emotionally expressive, but this may sometimes come across as a glass-half-full optimism that conceals her own underlying weaknesses. Her personality is defined by her capacity to "see" the light or hope in people and use her abilities to bring clarity or relief. She is fiercely independent and has a street-smart edge, frequently pushing the duo to act when Cloak's cautious temperament would otherwise lead to hesitancy. Despite a terrible upbringing marred by neglect, she remains optimistic and excels as an acrobatic combatant. When their personalities combine, Cloak and Dagger form a perfect, albeit tragic, symbiosis. Their relationship is based on a close fundamental emotional and physical need: Cloak's darkness requires Dagger's light to be complete, and Dagger's light need Cloak's darkness to protect her from becoming overwhelmed by her own power. Tyrone acts as a balancing force for Tandy's rebellious inclinations, providing a cool viewpoint when she is ready for whatever lies ahead. In contrast, Tandy pushes Tyrone outside of his comfort zone, pushing his cautious temperament and encouraging him to appreciate life's unpredictability. This generates a "yin and yang" dynamic in which his grounded, protective caution counteracts her impulsive energy. They depict the full gamut of the human experience, from the struggle with inner demons to the desire of relief. Their combined personality is one of great loyalty and codependency, and they work together as a single unit to balance the painful reality of their duty with a constant, flickering hope for a better future. Trivia [ ] Cloak & Dagger's first appearance was in " Peter Parker, the Spectacular Spider-Man " (1976) #64 in March 1982. Cloak & Dagger are currently the only heroes that allow you to play two separate characters as one (having to alternate between one and the other). In the comics, Cloak & Dagger's relationship has traditionally been depicted as a complex, platonic codependency driven by their contrasting powers rather than a formal romance. In Marvel Rivals they are explicitly portrayed as a romantic couple, aligning with more modern interpretations of the duo. His passive, Radar Sense, detects nearby enemies and allies through walls. Daredevil uses Fury as a resource, holding up to three charges that are gained through abilities. His primary fire, Justice Jab, is a basic melee strike that grants 0.5 Fury per hit. After using Devil's Latch or Infernal Fury, he enables a 5s window of time to use Righteous Cross as his next attack - where he lunges forward for one heavy strike and gains 0.5 Fury on hit. His secondary fire, Objection, has Daredevil enter a defensive stance for up to 1.5s where he deflects attacks and projectiles from the front. He also gains 2 Fury after the ability ends if he deflected at least one attack. Devil's Latch is a grapple ability that grants 1 Fury upon completion and enables Righteous Cross. If the grapple hits an enemy, the target will be reeled in; which is great for closing distance and preventing opponents from escaping. Infernal Fury consumes 2 Fury to unleash either Devil's Chain or Devil's Throw, both of which enable Righteous Cross afterward. Devil's Chain is a close-range strike that grants 25 bonus health on use and additional bonus health based on damage dealt. If an enemy is hit within the strikespot at the end of the attack range, they take nearly double the damage, granting you more bonus health. Devil's Throw hurls the batons to bounce between walls and nearby enemies, slowing down targets upon hit. Daredevil also gains 50 bonus health when this attack is used. Devil's Chain is great for sustain during one-on-one fights, while Devil's Throw is better for 'accidental picks' and damage spread. Sonic Pursuit marks a target and grants Daredevil damage reduction and a movement speed boost (which decays the farther he is from the marked opponent). Daredevil can also dash to marked enemies, blinding them and granting himself 2 Fury upon completion. If an opponent is KO'd within a few seconds of being marked, the dash cooldown will also be reset.

Daredevil can also dash to marked enemies, blinding them and granting himself 2 Fury upon completion. If an opponent is KO'd within a few seconds of being marked, the dash cooldown will also be reset. This is how you can bounce between opponents quickly and still have the resources to play aggressive. His Ultimate, Let The Devil Out, creates a visible dome around the player that ramps up a damage over time and blindness effect for enemies within line of sight. While active, you continously regain Fury as well. Weaknesses [ ] Since the brawn of his kit ties into Infernal Fury, Daredevil becomes extremely vulnerable when he has drained all his Fury and cooldowns. Devil's Latch and Sonic Pursuit can be disrupted by earthbound before either ability is completed, causing you not to gain Fury afterward. Let The Devil Out is rather situational since it reveals your location while active, making you a high-priority target if your own team is not able to assist you. Inputs can feel rather sticky because of his aggressive playstyle. Daredevil Matthew Murdock, known as Daredevil, is a complex character defined by his dual existence. By day, he is a gifted and principled lawyer committed to upholding justice within the confines of the legal system.

By day, he is a gifted and principled lawyer committed to upholding justice within the confines of the legal system. By night, he turns into Daredevil, a masked vigilante who fights crime on the streets of Hell's Kitchen, New York, though he adheres to a strict "no-kill" rule. This conflict between law and vigilantism exemplifies the moral uncertainty that defines much of his character. Matt is sincerely committed to doing the right thing, but he is always debating how far he is ready to go to protect the innocent while punishing the wicked. Daredevil is driven by a deep feeling of remorse and duty stemming from a difficult childhood. After being blinded in an accident while saving a man's life, Matt's remaining senses were enhanced to superhuman levels. His father, Jack Murdock, a boxer, instilled in him a strong moral code and the value of standing up for oneself, but Jack's murder for refusing to fight taught Matt that the world is cruel and unjust. This tragedy instilled in Matt a quiet intensity and a readiness to sacrifice himself for others, often to self-destructive means. Matt is an emotional and thoughtful person. He struggles with his Catholic faith, frequently turning to the church for help while also questioning God's role in his life. He is troubled by failure and struggles with emotions of unworthiness, particularly when his acts as Daredevil inflict collateral harm. Nonetheless, he persists in his quest of justice, even if it alienates those he loves or puts him in danger. Matt Murdock's emotional life revolves around his relationship with Foggy Nelson and Karen Page . They symbolize his link to the world beyond the mask, his humanity, his hope, and his greatest vulnerabilities. Matt, Foggy, and Karen form a captivating and emotionally charged trio. When they come together, as friends, coworkers, and occasionally more, they represent the best parts of Matt's life. While Matt’s known for his brooding and moral seriousness, he has a sense of humor and had rare genuine laughter that happens occasionally, often in more relaxed moments with friends or during flashbacks to lighter times. One occurred while interacting in-game with one of his close friends Black Panther .

While Matt’s known for his brooding and moral seriousness, he has a sense of humor and had rare genuine laughter that happens occasionally, often in more relaxed moments with friends or during flashbacks to lighter times. One occurred while interacting in-game with one of his close friends Black Panther . As serious as he is, he can't help but laugh at the idea of Hell's Kitchen in space. One of the most volatile dynamic relationship of Daredevil with other Marvel characters is the vigilante known as The Punisher . Matt Murdock believes in the rule of justice, redemption, and the value of life, including for criminals. While Frank Castle sees the legal system as permanently damaged and takes justice into his own hands, killing those he deems guilty. Their interactions are frequently characterized by tension, mutual scorn, and hesitant respect.  Their meetings frequently push Matt to confront his own constraints and question the efficiency of his code, rendering their battle deeply personal and morally complex. With Spider-Man , they have a connection that is based on similar principles, mutual trust, and a profound understanding of each other's hardships. Their partnership exemplifies the greatest of superhero friendships, as it is founded not only on fighting together, but also on confronting, understanding, and quietly supporting one another through the moral weight of being heroes. In recent events, Matt confronts The Hand one last time and descends into Hell, willing to commit further sins if it means saving lives. He destroys their demon leader, the Beast, regaining the strength he previously held when guilt forced him to serve as its Fist. Though he succeeds, the victory shatters him: he understands the conflict is far more than one demon, his faith is weakened, and his sacrifices seemed pointless. Yinglong , one of The Beast's captives, promised to help Daredevil harness this demonic power. Daredevil followed Yinglong to the Eighth City, where Yinglong taught him how to control the Beast's power without being possessed and where he changed the prison world into a refugee haven, no matter their crimes and become his champion to restore the lost Eighth City, earning himself a new name: "Dizang". He even kept the goddess Hela in the refugee haven after her defeat in Klyntar .

He even kept the goddess Hela in the refugee haven after her defeat in Klyntar . Matt's view on everything he'd done and sacrificed has shifted significantly since moving to the Eighth City according to in-game interactions with Jean Grey and Hawkeye . Given that this version of Matt is from the Collapsing timeline , the amount of pain, suffering, and sorrow he experienced is immense. Still, he continues to hold to his strength and beliefs while he experienced hell repetitively while fighting the "Beast" within him that granted him powers. His resilience, mixed with a blazing inner anguish and suffering, transforms him into a terribly tragic yet heroic figure, a man who straddles the border between light and darkness, never quite fitting into either. Each one of Deadpool's roles technically count as a separate character. Deadpool has different stats per role. In the Competitive Mode , each Deadpool role must be banned separately. Deadpool has two passives: Healing Factor provides Deadpool with a healing-over-time effect of 25 per second if he has been out of combat for 5 seconds. This passive will automatically activate if he takes more than 200 damage within a 2-second window; during this, the effect is 50 per second instead. He will also become immune to damage for a brief duration, making him practically immune to one-shot abilities. This has a 45 second cooldown. Maximum Flair is tied to Deadpool's Ultimate activation; unlike other characters, he doesn't generate Ultimate charge over-time, instead gainining "Style Points" depending on his actions. Whenever he hits an enemy or heals an ally, he gains Style Points, starting on on rank E, and once it reaches rank S, he can activate his Ultimate. He gains the most amount of Style Points when he lands his abilities in quick succession. Actions taken in combat grant Deadpool experience points, shown as a red gauge underneath his health; once this gauge is filled, Deadpool can upgrade one of his abilities, empowering them.

Although ability upgrades are unique to each role, Deadpool's experience gauge is shared across all three variants. This means that if a player swaps roles mid-match, the specific ability upgrades will reset, but all earned experience is retained, allowing the player to immediately re-allocate their upgrade points to the new role's skills. Deadpool has two primary weapons in all three of his roles: Dual Desert Eagles fire hitscan bullets with moderate damage and fast attack speed. When upgraded, every shot charges up an icon that once full, will launch an explosive projectile with a slow projectile speed. Deadpool also gains increased max ammo. Kick@$$ Katanas is a melee weapon with a very fast attack speed. The second strike is a fast jab attack that can easily prove to be the brute of his damage. When upgraded, the jab strike can deal critical damage. Bouncing off an enemy with the double jump will guarentee a jab strike as well, enhancing his offensive capabilities. Deadpool In Your Area is an ability for all roles: Deadpool creates a zone around himself for 5 seconds that clutters the screen of nearby enemies and deals continous damage. The taunt effect is removed once Deadpool suffers enough damage. When upgraded, for all roles, enemies have their health bar taped over if they stay in the area for too long. Deadpool can choose to take a selfie with enemies he lands a final blow on before they respawn, granting additional XP. While doing so, Deadpool cannot be damaged and is immune to crowd control. Weaknesses [ ] If Deadpool is defeated, his style gauge is reset to rank E, even if he reached rank S and charged his Ultimate. This means that he's the only character in the game that can lose his Ultimate once charged. While Deadpool charges his Ultimate faster than other heroes, it does have a cooldown of 60 seconds after each use. This makes his Ultimates favor frequency over effectiveness. As a Vanguard, Deadpool struggles to gain XP the most between his two other roles. As a Duelist, his utility can often feel outclassed by the Vanguard role. Upgraded Hazardous Hijinx will also not begin to recharge until Deadpool misses a dash. As a Strategist, he heavily relies upon his team to support him while his Ultimate is active to make large plays.
