Let's F$#%$% go! https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Deadpool_-_Hero_Spawned_05.ogg Deadpool Deadpool, the Merc with a Mouth, is widely renowned as the mercenary with a warped sense of humor and a deep self-awareness, as seen by continuous, irreverent jokes, sardonic wit, energetic behavior and his ability of fourth-wall breaking. This irreverence makes him appear unserious, hiding a deeper pain and the absurdity of his existence and his mental instability caused by his healing factor. He is frequently shown as a flirtatious, bubbly, chaotic and anti-heroic, but ultimately compassionate individual who cares deeply. Wade, unlike other heroes, understands that he is a fictional character, which drives his sarcasm, unpredictable behavior, and refusal to follow societal norms. He frequently taunts, jokes and belittles his opponents for his own amusement. He also has no shame and can create a comedy out of any circumstance, even if it does not go his way. Wade is described as the ultimate loudmouth because he speaks continually, obsessively, and frequently without filter or pause. His dirty mouth is faster than his brain, spouting curse words, pop-culture references, memes, insults, meta commentary, and adult jokes even during battles. Silence makes him uneasy, so he fills every second with noise, jokes, and meandering monologues, regardless of who is listening.

His dirty mouth is faster than his brain, spouting curse words, pop-culture references, memes, insults, meta commentary, and adult jokes even during battles. Silence makes him uneasy, so he fills every second with noise, jokes, and meandering monologues, regardless of who is listening. As a mercenary and anti-hero, Wade accepts jobs for money, revenge, or simple boredom, frequently switching sides if his feelings alter mid-mission. Unlike trained assassins, he fights brutally and chaotically while constantly talking, taunting enemies and using unpredictability as a tactical advantage. His violence is extreme and dramatic, but it is not mindless; he understands combat and knows how far to push a situation in order to survive. He resides in the gray area between kindness and selfishness. He does not believe in being "good" in the traditional sense, but he consistently chooses to protect the innocent, particularly when he detects vulnerability or pain in himself. His actions are frequently vulgar, harsh, and morally ambiguous, but they are motivated by emotional devotion rather than abstract justice. His interactions with other heroes are chaotic, inconsistent, and deeply revealing, highlighting the conflict between how he acts and who he truly wants to be. From great admiration and friendship to frustration and outright dislike. With Wolverine , they have a complex, frequently hostile, but eventually strong friendship transitioning from enemies who continually conflict to reluctant allies forced to work together. They are complete opposites: Logan is moody and stern, while Wade is loud and humorous, resulting in a typical odd pair interaction characterized by frustration and mocking combined with real affection and respect. Now with his connection with Spider-Man , their banter is frequent, but beyond the jokes, Deadpool really desires Spider-Man's approval because it would imply that someone truly nice can accept him. While Wade's aggression and lack of boundaries frequently disturb and annoyed Peter, he still regards him as a human and friend. Additionally, Wade genuinely cares for the ones he love and his allies and one example is Jeff the Land Shark , as he loves and cares for him treating as his lovable son. Overall, Deadpool is a tragic, humorous, flirtatious, and a loudmouth who laughs, fights, and speaks incessantly in order to endure, all while longing for significance and intimacy in a world that has left him damaged yet unkillable.

He currently has one team-up ability: Primal Punishment — Anchor Hero for The Punisher Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Strengths 1.2 Weaknesses 2 Costumes 3 Abilities 4 Strategy 5 Personality 6 Achievements 7 Proficiency 7.1 Challenges 7.2 Rewards 8 Gallery 9 Trivia 10 References 11 Navigation Overview [ ] Strengths [ ] An extremely bulky, self-sustaining Vanguard who uses powerful melee attacks to inflict damage over time and generate bonus health by doing so. Devil Dinosaur has two passives: Prehistoric Plating reduces damage taken on a critical hit by 50%, makes you immune to displacement effects, and reduces the Ultimate charge that enemies/allies gain by damaging/healing you by 35%. Apex Advantage converts 150% of the damage you deal to bleeding enemies into bonus health. His primary fire, Primal Bite, performs a slow but high-damage melee strike that inflicts bleeding on hit. His primary fire, Primal Bite, performs a slow but high-damage melee strike that inflicts bleeding on hit. Bleeding effects last for 4s and cause targets to take 1.5% of their max health as damage every 0.5s. His secondary fire, Impact Beam, drains a resource meter to fire a damaging beam of energy. It inflicts bleeding and slow to enemies it hits, and knocks down airborne targets. Savage Predation has Devil leap into the air, dealing damage and inflicting bleeding upon landing. If Devil collides with an already-bleeding enemy during the leap, the ability ends and he clamps down on them; allowing Devil to briefly carry the target in his mouth before throwing them forward. Buddy Barrier summons a spherical barrier around yourself that has 450 HP and lasts for up to 6s. Enemies caught within the inside of the barrier are also slowed. Frenzied Feast has Devil perform a flurry of bites, the fifth being a heavier bite that lunges you forward. All damage dealt is converted into bonus health. Devil also deals additional percentage damage to bleeding targets. This allows him to rack up an extremely high amount of bonus health when attacking high-health heroes such as other Vanguards. His Ultimate, Devil-Beast Rampage, empowers Devil for 10s; and while active, Devil greatly boosts his movement speed and unleashes shockwaves that inflict bleeding and knock back opponents. Savage Predation and Frenzied Feast have reduced cooldowns while active. Upon activation, Devil gains a large sum of bonus health and emits a large sonic wave projectile that slows enemies upon hit. When paired with The Punisher , Frank can mount Devil to ride on top of him, forcing him to use only Adjudication/Deliverance and Scourge Grenade; but gaining damage reduction. Devil absorbs a portion of the damage and healing that Frank receives while active. Weaknesses [ ] Due to its large size, Devil Dinosaur may have movement problems in specific areas, with some maps even having sections where it is impossible for him to pass. Devil's head hitbox is quite wide, so despite his passive, heroes who benefit from landing critical hits like Mantis or Phoenix are strong adversaries against him.

Can prove powerful in one-versus-one scenarios but is extremely weak against larger crowds of enemies. Despite his fearsome appearance and the "Devil" moniker, he is far from a mindless predator; instead, he displays a noble and fiercely protective spirit, often showing a level of discernment that transcends basic animal instinct. His personality is a blend of raw, prehistoric power and an unwavering sense of loyalty, making him a formidable guardian with a heart that is remarkably compassionate toward his allies. His profound friendship bond with Moon Girl is the true heart of who he is. She serves as his moral compass and tactical anchor in a world that is completely foreign to him. To Devil, Lunella isn't just a partner, she is the voice of reason that channels his wild impulses into something purposeful. Following an initial teaser in the final gallery card of Season 7: The Hunt Is On —which depicted a Devil Dinosaur plushie on a bookshelf—the developers officially confirmed Devil Dinosaur as one of the featured heroes for Season 8 via social media. [ 1 ] This teaser picked up the storyline from Season 6: Night at the Museum , where Devil Dinosaur was freed from the Museum of Contemplation along with other creatures by Deadpool , taking them all to his new Monster Kingdom . Unlike most characters, the main version of Devil Dinosaur is native to Earth-78411 (also known as Dinosaur World) rather than the mainstream Earth-616. While he often resides in the modern Marvel Universe alongside partners like Moon Girl , he remains a displaced inhabitant of this prehistoric reality. Upon his release in Season 8, Devil Dinosaur was released without a trait assigned to him, being the first and so far only character in the game to lack one entirely. Each time Doctor Strange deals damage with his primary fire or melee attack, he gains stacks of Dark Magic, up to 100. If he reaches the maximum amount of Dark Magic and does not release it after 3 seconds, he is afflicted by the Anti-Heal curse, which makes him unable to be healed for a few seconds. The stacks of Dark Magic that Doctor Strange possesses visually appear as a glowing purple symbol on his cape that becomes more pronounced as more stacks are accumulated. Dark Magic decays after a few seconds if the player doesn't deal damage. Decay is stopped immediately if further damage is done (excluding decay from max percentage.) Doctor Strange gains 3.5 Dark Magic if he hits enemies with Daggers of Denak, and 10 Dark Magic with his melee attack. The player can release the Dark Magic by using Maelstrom of Madness, which deals more damage the more Dark Magic he currently has (1.2 damage per stack). Doctor Strange Doctor Stephen Strange is a complex character whose personality evolves significantly. Initially, he is presented as arrogant, stubborn and egotistical, a brilliant neurosurgeon who takes delight in his intelligence and expertise, which contributed to his career. His confidence frequently borders on arrogance, making him dismissive of anything that contradicts his viewpoint. This egoism underpins much of his early conduct, as he is obsessed with control, achievement, and recognition, with little empathy for those outside of his own professional area. This, however, changed after a terrible car accident ended Stephen's surgical career, leaving him a shattered man and always displeased because he was unable to return to his previous rich life.

Stephen's personality shifts after visiting Kamar-Taj. Faced with the loss of his identity and purpose, he grows desperate while simultaneously being open to new options. His journey into the mystical arts with the Ancient One and Wong teaches him humility, patience, and selflessness, which were before underdeveloped or lacking. Strange transforms into a reality protector as he learns magic and accepts the duties that come with it, demonstrating a willingness to sacrifice personal goals for the greater good. Despite his change, Strange retains aspects of his former personality, including his acute intellect, quick wit, and a certain level of humor. After learning the mastery of a hundred spells and reading mystical books, he is now ready to face dangers for the greater good and become the Sorcerer Supreme. Together with his friend Wong , they lived at the Sanctum Sanctorum as supernatural protectors of Earth. He also adopted and takes care of Bats , a ghostly dog which is his only pet to cheer him up. As the Sorcerer Supreme, Doctor Strange has a great deal of responsibility and vast knowledge which requires him to be a multiverse guardian, protecting reality from magical perils beyond human comprehension such as entities and demons. Strange's personality evolves under this mantle, becoming more measured and contemplative, often bearing the burden of foresight and responsibility for his actions. He becomes a stoic, sometimes enigmatic figure, mindful that his actions may have far-reaching consequences. For Stephen, meditation is one of his primary hobbies. It helps him access mystical energies, focus his thoughts, and keep control over the intricate spells and dimensions he manipulates. In meetings and connections with other heroes, Doctor Strange frequently serves as a mentor, strategist, and skeptic. His extensive mystical knowledge and experience give him importance, and he prefers to approach issues with caution and deliberate planning rather than rash action, which reflects his status as a member of the Illuminati . In addition, Stephen is sometimes hesitant and often welcomes students at his Sanctum, especially in the mystical arts, to help train the next generation of sorcerers, notably Magik and Zelma Stanton . He also has mutual respect with other magic users, such as the Scarlet Witch .

Elsa Bloodstone has two different versions of her primary fire: Double-Barrel Blaster is her default weapon, which is a shotgun that fires two rounds in quick succession. Monster-Piercer fires one heavy shotgun blast from her elephant gun. The bullets pierce through enemies and deal percentage damage. Her secondary fire, Living Bullet, shoots a round that splits into seeking shards on impact. Enemies hit by the shards are marked and grant Elsa a 40% movespeed boost for 1s when hit by either of her guns. Shards deal extra damage to barriers and enemies with bonus health. Helix Advance is a basic dash that grants bonus health. It also enables a 6-second window where Elsa's next primary fire will be Monster-Piercer. Ruthless Pursuit performs a dash then launches enemies into the air. Elsa can then reactivate this ability within a 5-second window to fire a follow-up shot. It propels the player back & slows down opponents. Also grants bonus health upon activation. Both the dash and follow-up shot enable the window for Monster-Piercer. Smoky Snare deploys a small trap that becomes invisible and invincible after 1s of being on the ground. When stepped over, the target is briefly immobilized while Elsa is able to perform a targeted dash. Elsa also gains two levels of Instinct when eliminating a trapped enemy. This ability proves effective for locking down flank routes and further hindering enemies caught by a pull. Her Ultimate, Apex Predator, summons the Glartrox to charge forward and drag along enemies its his path then bite down for damage once he reaches the end of its travel distance. Because of this, trigger discipline is paramount; you must make every burst count to maintain pressure during a duel.

Monster-Piercer functions more like an activated ability state rather than a standard secondary weapon. Once activated, you have a 6-second window to use it. Its damage is significantly higher than the primary fire, so while it shouldn't be wasted, you must ensure you utilize it before the timer expires. The ammo for Monster-Piercer is tracked separately from Double-Barrel Blaster, meaning your primary magazine remains intact while using it. Effectively alternating between both weapons allows for a continuous damage rotation and minimizes downtime spent on reloads. Elsa’s gameplay revolves around Helix Advance. This ability provides essential mobility for engaging or escaping, while granting 40 Bonus Health per cast (with a maximum of 75). Additionally, every shot fired immediately after using this ability becomes a Monster-Piercer round, making Elsa incredibly powerful during this window. Inherited Instinct, Elsa's passive, reduces the cooldown of Helix Advance from the standard 10 seconds down to a minimum of 4 seconds when fully charged. It is highly recommended to use this ability everytime it is available to maintain a high uptime on your Bonus Health and extra damage. The passive meter is charged by dealing damage and gains a significant boost from getting final hits, but it decreases substantially upon death. Play aggressively to keep your meter high, but avoid overextending so you don't lose your cooldown advantage. Ruthless Pursuit offers versatile mobility; the first activation is a directional dash (including vertical movement), and the second fires a shot that propels Elsa in the opposite direction. Both movements are perfect for chasing down enemies, getting to higher ground, or chasing down enemies. The deployable trap from Smoky Snare becomes invisible and invulnerable once placed, making it a powerful tool for battlefield control. If an enemy is caught, Elsa can quickly close the gap from a long distance. This, combined with Helix Advance and Ruthless Pursuit, gives her incredible burst mobility. Smoky Snare can be used defensively by placing it near Elsa or her allies to peel against enemy divers.

Smoky Snare can be used defensively by placing it near Elsa or her allies to peel against enemy divers. The trap remains invisible even to Daredevil , and can't be destroyed by Phoenix 's ultimate once deployed, making it a reliable resource against the entire roster. Living Bullet deals 60 damage to any enemy it hits and has no limit on the number of targets it can pierce. It also ricochets off surfaces, making it very easy to strike enemies behind cover or around corners. Because of that, it is an excellent tool for finishing off low-health targets. Shield abilities will absorb Living Bullet, so avoid firing directly at barriers when trying to bounce your shots. With her ultimate, Apex Predator, Elsa summons the Glartrox . This beast is incredibly useful for disabling and displacing the enemy team. It is crucial to monitor enemy positioning to catch as many targets as possible. Apex Predator can clear a capture point during Overtime, or pull enemies out of powerful defensive area ultimates like those of Invisible Woman or Luna Snow . One of the most useful uses of Apex Predator is knocking enemies off the map. As Elsa, it's incredibly helpful to be on the lookout for opportunities to do this on maps with cliffs. It is important to note that the Glartrox will NOT capture enemies under the Unstoppable status, so it should be avoided in an attempt to stop them. Even so, Apex Predator CAN move The Thing , making it a very useful tool against this hero. Using other crowd control effects on enemies captured by Glartrox will release them from his grasp, so you should avoid using abilities like Luna Snow 's Absolute Zero or Mantis 's Spore Slumber. Personality [ ] If you're not careful, mate, you start to become the monster yourself... https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Elsa_Bloodstone_-_Hero_Spawned_04.ogg Elsa Bloodstone Born in Boston but raised in England within an occult, monster-hunting family, Elsa Bloodstone is characterized by her sharp wit, no-nonsense attitude, and a spirited bravado forged by a lifetime of hunting the supernatural.

Raised under the brutal and demanding tutelage of her father, Ulysses Bloodstone, she developed a thick skin and a fierce sense of self-reliance, yet she carries herself with a vibrant, almost adventurous energy rather than a cold exterior. Elsa often maintains an air of supreme confidence—bordering on a playful arrogance—stemming from her status as one of the world’s preeminent monster hunters. For Elsa, monster hunting is more than a grim familial obligation; it is a genuine passion that fuels her restless spirit. She possesses an unshakeable bravery that manifests as a constant desire for the thrill of the hunt, often seeking out the most formidable "beasties" with infectious enthusiasm. Whether she is eagerly volunteering for a troll hunt in Asgard or tracking the legendary Great Beasts of the north, her drive to test her skills in the heat of combat is a central pillar of her identity, showcasing a fearlessness that thrives on the adrenaline of battle. In her interactions, she is frequently sarcastic and blunt, often peppered with British colloquialisms like "mate" or "luv", rarely softening her words for the sake of diplomacy. While she operates with a pragmatic perspective towards danger, seeing monsters as mere target practice, she is far from unapproachable. Elsa demonstrates a deep respect for genuine skill, openly acknowledging the prowess of allies like Hawkeye or Spider-Man , and even bestowing the title of "honorary Bloodstone" upon those who prove their worth in combat, such as Sai . Despite her "lone wolf" tendencies, Elsa possesses a dry, dark sense of humor and a hidden streak of genuine warmth. She often balances her professional detachment with a spirited charm, whether she is gleefully anticipating a challenging hunt or jokingly offering tea after a takedown. This complexity is most evident in her personal ties; while she maintains a high-tension, comedic rivalry with Deadpool , she is also capable of profound empathy. She demonstrates a surprising tenderness toward those she respects, such as recognizing the kindness beneath the rocky exterior of Ben Grimm , and displays an endearing soft spot for creatures like Jeff the Land Shark . These flashes of vulnerability prove that her heroic heart is just as prominent as her hunter's instinct.

Elsa Bloodstone, Deadpool and a Brood Queen in "The Ballad of Wade Wilson". Trivia [ ] Elsa Bloodstone's first appearance was in "Bloodstone" (2001) #1 in December 2001. Elsa was datamined on September 12, 2025, where she replaced Trapster 's ID 1059. [ 1 ] Elsa Bloodstone was speculated to make her debut in Season 6 alongside Deadpool due to a gallery card in Season 5: Love is a Battlefield teasing the theme of both characters quoting "a blathering, foul-mouthed mercenary and a monster hunter as deadly as she is beautiful." A silhouette of Elsa Bloodstone can be seen on the cover art of the 'Museum Security' gallery card for Season 5: Love is a Battlefield . Elsa’s Young Blood costume features her with blonde hair, referencing her original design in this comic book series. While she is now iconically known for her red hair, the change was a creative shift in Marvel Comics starting with the "Nextwave" series (2006) . Elsa's trap featured in her "Smoky Snare" ability contains Diablo inside, a classic Marvel smoke-based giant monster first introduced in "Tales of Suspense" (1959) #9 . The pairing of Elsa Bloodstone and Deadpool as the new heroes for Season 6 draws from their established history in Marvel Comics. The two characters shared a prominent storyline in the 2019 "Deadpool" series , where Elsa served as a frequent ally and brief romantic interest to Wade Wilson, providing a clear precedent for their debut together in the game. Her primary fire, Telepathic Pulse, is a mid-range beam that deals damage up to 15m. It is a continuous beam of damage that also can deal more damage the more damage dealt with it. Telepathic Pulse has a meter that rises when dealing damage, the higher the number the higher the damage and when maxxed out to 100 it deals significant damage.

It is a continuous beam of damage that also can deal more damage the more damage dealt with it. Telepathic Pulse has a meter that rises when dealing damage, the higher the number the higher the damage and when maxxed out to 100 it deals significant damage. Telepathic Pulse has a max usage of 70 ammo but Emma can use this ability for a significant duration before needing to regenerate this attack. Her secondary fire, Mind's Aegis, creates a diamond shield in front of Emma and the longer it's held down the more distance the shield can be placed at. Mind's Aegis has 400 health and has infinite duration until destroyed or reclaimed. Mind's Aegis can be placed at a long distance and thus can be used to defend allies further ahead or be used to block damage coming from a doorway or entrance. Mind's Aegis shield is stationary once placed and can also be recalled similar to Invisible Woman's Guardian Shield ability. This shield can block Ultimates such as Iron Man's Invincible Pulse Cannon and Hela's blast shots from Goddess of Death. Psychic Spear is an ability that allows Emma to shoot a psionic projectile that, once hitting an enemy, creates a crystal formation of the enemy's sentience that projects forward towards Emma. The damage dealt to this formation reflects onto the enemy. When the crystal sentience of the enemy is destroyed before it disappears will deal significant damage to the enemy. Telepathic Pulse can pierce through the crystal sentience allowing for Emma to deal double damage if the enemy and the crystal sentience are in the same line of fire of her beam. Diamond Form is an ability Emma can use to transform her body into diamond which disables her access to her psychic abilities, however, granting her access to strong counter abilities and passives. Diamond Form lasts for 8 seconds. In Diamond Form, Emma's primary fire is replaced with Faceted Fury a strong melee attack. In Diamond Form, Emma can use Carbon Crush allowing her to dash forward a certain distance and when connected to an enemy she will grab them by the throat and slam them down behind her while dealing damage, turning herself around in the process. Carbon Crush stuns enemies and can be used to cancel enemy Ultimates during their start up.

Carbon Crush stuns enemies and can be used to cancel enemy Ultimates during their start up. Carbon Crush allows Emma to dash into the sky and can grapple enemies above if they're within range. In Diamond Form, Emma can use Crystal Kick allowing her to knockback an enemy a certain distance away dealing lots of damage. If an enemy is hit with the Crystal Kick into a wall or solid surface, they will receive extra damage hitting the wall. In Diamond Form, Emma has strong resistance to all forms of damage, and gains Unstoppable; complete immunity from displacements such as stuns, knockbacks, and Jeff the Land Shark's Ultimate It's Jeff!. Her Ultimate, Psionic Seduction, Emma can project a large cone of psionic waves that deal damage overtime. The longer enemies remain within this psionic wave they will be able to be mind controlled, this is indicated by a diamond meter above each enemy's head. When mind controlled via Psionic Seduction, enemies don't have access to their movement and will instead be lured towards Emma until they die or the ultimate ends. When mind controlled via Psionic Seduction, enemies within their Ultimate can have their Ultimate cancelled. Weaknesses [ ] Her main attack Telepathic Pulse has a limited range of 15m which requires her to be mid-range to deal damage against enemies. Diamond Form also has no ranged attacks so whenever players utilize this form it is advised to do it when in melee range., unless they're within range of her Carbon Crush ability. Diamond Form's abilities have cooldowns allowing only one or two uses of Carbon Crush and Crystal Kick each within this form. While Diamond Form grants Emma strong resistance, she still takes damage and can be killed within this state. Emma is still susceptible to be killed by Iron Man's Invincible Pulse Cannon. Due to Emma not having any abilities that allow her to move faster outside her Carbon Crush within Diamond Form, she does not have fast mobility and thus can be easily overwhelmed if being chased or surrounded by enemies. Emma Frost The White Queen stands out by her charm, ego, cleverness, elegance and cunning, viewing herself as superior due to her wealth, appearance, and mutant capabilities. Emma is characterized as having a sharp intellect, a cold temperament, and an iron will; she is known for her bold and unapologetic persona. Known for her assertive, controlling, flirtarous, unbothered and dominant personality, Frost is full of self-confidence and fierce independence, frequently acting on her own terms and unafraid to question authority, including that of powerful figures such as Professor X and Magneto . Emma carries a strong presence and is frequently described as someone who demands to be respected, if not feared. She is elegant and collected, rarely allowing emotions to impair her judgment, but having deep feelings beneath the surface. Emma Frost, who was presented as member of the Hellfire Club, was influenced by her early experiences with betrayal, deception, and arrogance. These events toughened her while also instilling in her a strong sense of self-worth and a deep distrust of others.

Emma Frost, who was presented as member of the Hellfire Club, was influenced by her early experiences with betrayal, deception, and arrogance. These events toughened her while also instilling in her a strong sense of self-worth and a deep distrust of others. Emma grew into a more heroic personality, eventually becoming a key member of the X-Men . Despite this transformation, she maintains her sharp tongue, caustic wit, and moral ambiguity. Despite a generally cold personality, questionable methods and her pragmatic approach to alliances, she may display loyalty, caring, protectiveness, and a heroic drive, notably in her noble desire of preserving mutantkind as a member of the Quiet Council , which is frequently expressed through her great participation in fashion and the Hellfire Gala . As the Hellfire Gala's founder, she is always known for her strong sense of fashion and takes care in her looks, employing both her outfits and her diamond form for protection and expression. Her diamond shape acts as both a physical and emotional shield, adding to her polished yet detached public demeanor. Furthermore, she has a strong protective and nurturing side, especially when it comes to her students, mutant children, and those she considers part of her chosen family. She is a passionately dedicated teacher who expects greatness while providing genuine care and guidance. She also cared for her daughters. She saw the Cuckoos as more than just kids; they were mirrors of her own past, symbols of hope and family. Even Emma has a warm spot for the adorable landshark, Jeff . She is protective, caring, loving, and treats Jeff like he is her son. Most of the time, her interactions with other characters such as Cyclops and her old Generation X students demonstrate her sensitivity, albeit often disguised by snark or tough love. As with Scott, they have an intimate, emotional, complex, and deeply transformative relationship. Now with Iron Man , they have a distant, cautious, and strategic rather than emotional. Both are powerful, affluent, and extremely educated individuals with large egos, and they have frequently clashed owing to competing priorities. While they occasionally collaborate when their goals are similar, they are normally wary of each other.

Official Description Gambit is a Strategist hero in Marvel Rivals and the 44th hero introduced to the game's roster during Season 5: Love is a Battlefield . He currently has one team-up ability: Explosive Entanglement — Anchor Hero for Magneto and Rogue Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Strengths 1.2 Weaknesses 2 Costumes 3 Abilities 4 Strategy 5 Personality 6 Achievements 7 Proficiency 7.1 Challenges 7.2 Rewards 8 Gallery 9 Trivia 10 References 11 Navigation Overview [ ] Strengths [ ] An agile resource-based support that can match damage output with healing output, utility and debuffs. In turn for long cooldowns, he can support his team by destroying enemy positioning and increase survival through cleansing negative effects. His kit revolves around his Sleight of Hand resource, which can be consumed to grant temporary passive bonuses, as well combined with different card inputs to activate empowerment abilities. Sleight of Hand has a total of four stacks that regenerates over-time. His primary fire, Kinetic Cards, throws a short spread of three projectiles that explode on contact, damaging enemies while healing allies.

Sleight of Hand has a total of four stacks that regenerates over-time. His primary fire, Kinetic Cards, throws a short spread of three projectiles that explode on contact, damaging enemies while healing allies. His secondary fire, Bayou Bash, creates an burst of energy in front of Gambit that damages enemies and heals allies within the blast radius. This ability has two charges and can self-heal, making it more effective to repel against flanking enemies. Cajun Charge is a basic short-distance dash forward that briefly enables Big Easy Impact when using Bayou Bash immediately after the dash. Big Easy Impact consumes a charge from Bayou Bash and causes Gambit to dash a longer distance, creating three small explosions that damage enemies and heal allies as he travels. This proves to be a solid mobility tool when backing up or escaping from fights, since it also has two charges. Healing Hearts consumes a stack of Sleight of Hand to grant healing-over-time to self for 6 seconds, and enable either Bridge Boost [Flush] or Purifying Pick-Up [Raise] at the cost of another stack. Bridge Boost is great for healing sustain, while Purifying Pick-Up is an extremely powerful counter to stuns and debuffs. Bridge Boost launches a targeted healing projectile to an ally that bounces onto other nearby allies up to six times. It also amplifies healing received for 4 seconds. Purifying Pick-Up throws a swarm of projectiles all around Gambit that heal allies and cleanse negative effects upon impact. Allies can be purified up to two times per cast, while Gambit can only be affected once. Breaking Spades consumes a stack of Sleight of Hand to grant a damage boost to self for 6 seconds, and enable either Explosive Trick [Flush] or Bidding Barrage [Raise] at the cost of another stack. When it comes to powerful bursts of utility Gambit quite literally holds all of the cards. With his ability to queue up two separate Deck buffs Gambit can improvise on the fly, his role fluctuating between a traditional healing Strategist and a dive Duelist. All of which topped off with a nuclear ultimate that can completely turn the tide of a match. If quickly placing bets to steal the advantage in short term scuffles appeals to you, Gambit is the man for the job. Kinetic Cards is the perfect encapsulation of Gambit's gameplay philosophy. A primary that sends out a three-shot spread of explosive cards, incentivizing Gambit to get up close and personal to make the most of its impressive healing and damage. While lacking the ability to land critical hits this primary can still achieve above average results from short to mid-range. Further enabling Gambit's role as a jack of all trades. Striking a balance between finishing off enemies and keeping allies alive is of the upmost importance when utilizing Kinetic Cards, since it has fairly low ammunition and an even longer reload time. This primary's spread gives it the ability to easily chip out fliers and consistently hit enemies that utilize hitbox manipulation to avoid attacks. Such as Jeff's Hide and Seek.

It also holds a notable advantage against Duelist flank attempts on your team's backline, especially when facing more slippery Heroes like Spider-Man and Iron Fist . But can be less effective against dive-oriented Vanguards. Its consistency can make it a great option when rushing in with Big Easy Impact against more aggressive poke Duelists like Moon Knight . Especially if they are found out of position. Long range pestering can still be useful when paired with either Flush Empowerment. More on this quirk later when going over Deck Empowerments. Something to keep in mind with Kinetic Cards is that its shots can be angled to hit both the allies in front of you and the enemies past them. Make sure to use this trick whenever possible Gambit players should reload any time he is given the breathing room to do so. As running out of Kinetic Cards in the moment leaves him and his team open to counterattack. Weaving in melee attacks against low health enemies at close range can make a significant difference, especially considering the unique multi-hit property of his melee string. Bayou Bash is Gambit's go-to panic button that holds two charges. An AOE slam that can help to finish off enemies at close range and quickly regain chunks of health for Gambit and his allies. It also gains benefits from either deck buff, either supplementing Gambit's already potent self-sustain or securing eliminations. It is advisable to be somewhat reserved with its usage due to its punishing cooldown. This tool will see the most use when healing Gambit and another Strategist while out of cards. Giving him the time to fit in a reload. This is a strong opener after rushing in or away from the frontline with Cajun Charge and Big Easy Impact. Though it can be risky to burn both uses so quickly. Bayou Bash is counted as a melee attack and ignores shields. Do not use this midair, it will lock Gambit into the animation until he hits the ground. Cajun Charge is a short-range omnidirectional dash with two charges. It is a decent movement tool for making small adjustments to Gambit's positioning.

It is a decent movement tool for making small adjustments to Gambit's positioning. Allowing him to stick close to his allies and enemies in a pinch. Also grants the Hero a degree of verticality for when Big Easy Impact is unnecessary. Though on average saving Cajun Charge uses for Big Easy Impact is a much better idea. Big Easy Impact is where Gambit's gameplay loop begins and ends. Allowing him to dive past his team's frontline or back into it for as long as he has a usage of Cajun Charge and Bayou Bash in reserve. Granting himself and allies healing while damaging enemies. This excellent movement option passes through enemies and is omnidirectional, allowing him a brief state of pseudo flight to get wherever he pleases. Just like with Bayou Bash, Big Easy Impacts benefits can reinforce either Deck Buff if active. Big Easy Impact is the first step in the card trick process. Quickly deciding between defense or offense according to his positioning and the current state of the match. This will be expanded upon in the next section on Deck Buffs and Deck Empowerments. Big Easy Impact excels at counter-dive, allowing Gambit to chase after retreating Duelists and grab eliminations. Big Easy Impact has similar properties to Bayou Bash, allowing it to rush through shields and Magneto's Meteor M to deal damage. Big Easy Impact is a tool that grants Gambit the freedom to take risks not present with any other Strategist. Speeding into team fights and scattering Deck Empowerments in a flash. As well as the ability to sometimes aid allies in their dive attempts. As long as a proper escape route is kept in mind. Always keep in mind when Big Easy Impact will deal enough damage to secure an elimination with and without Breaking Spades active. Its damage can be difficult to avoid for enemies. Reading the room and your current positioning to place a bet on which Buff Stance will net the most value is the most important Gambit skill. If holding an excess of Sleight Of Hand charges using and holding onto a Deck Buff until it depletes is not significantly punishing. The next Sleight Of Hand should be recharged by then. Healing Hearts is Gambit's defensive Deck Buff, passive regeneration that allows Gambit to patch up small amounts of damage or chip he may encounter. This will be the go to Deck Buff for when his team is on the back foot or when he wishes to reinforce a state of advantageous sustain attrition. Healing Hearts Flush Empowerment, Bridge Boost is a bouncing healing projectile that grants a duration of enhanced healing. A nuclear burst heal option similar to Adam Warlock's Avatar Life Stream. Though it inherits many of the same inconsistencies with who it heals and when. Ensure that the highest priority target is within lock on before firing. Throw this out when incoming damage on your team becomes unmanageable. Or in dire circumstances to cancel out sources of anti-heal. Bridge Boost has a decently far range, not requiring lock on to bounce off of walls to nearby allies, throwing a hail mary to point can make a huge difference when making the trip back from spawn. Bouncing Bridge Boost off of a wall close to Gambit will target him first, once again similar to Adam Warlock's healing method. This can be a great panic button for when Healing Hearts passive regeneration is not enough to survive a fight. Healing Hearts Raise Empowerment, Purifying Pick-Up is a sweep of healing explosions that can cleanse any status effect or form of cc. Spider-Man's Spectacular Spin stun can be nullified with proper timing of Purifying Pick-Up. This timing method could theoretically allow Gambit to preemptively bail himself out of other CC effects. Breaking Spades is Gambit's offensive Deck Buff. Granting him a sizable damage increase to his Kinetic Cards and abilities for the duration. This buff will see more use in neutral while pestering enemies and any state where his team holds even the smallest advantage. Breaking Spades Flush Empowerment, Explosive Trick is a long range AOE that grants a noticeable chunk of damage alongside an Anti-Heal effect. This can finish off enemies chipped by Kinetic Cards at a distance and place low health Vanguards in a dangerous situation. Explosive Trick is fantastic against Heroes with strong self sustain like Cloak & Dagger and Luna Snow . As it cuts their regeneration by 1/4. Reinforce your advantage with Healing Hearts buff to seal the deal. Explosive Trick isn't very impactful against powerful healing Ultimates. Gambit got more than one ace up his sleeve! https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Gambit_-_Hero_Spawned_04.ogg Gambit Remy LeBeau, commonly known as the mutant thief Gambit, is a Louisiana native whose personality combines suave charm, intrigue, and moral complexity in a way that few other X-Men characters do.  At his core, he is a suave, smooth-talking Cajun whose charisma frequently deters both allies and adversaries. He conducts himself with casual composure, employing comedy, flirting, and witty conversation as social tool. He is a charismatic and roguish figure with a strong moral compass that occasionally clashes with his criminal background, but he always fights for what he believes is right. Remy is heavily guarded beneath the surface. His childhood on the streets of New Orleans, as well as his involvement in the Thieves and Assassins Guilds, made him hesitant of disclosing too much about himself. He frequently conceals his fears, regrets, and insecurities beneath a veneer of confidence and mischief. Even when surrounded by friends, he frequently feels like an outsider which someone who operates on moral ambiguity, never certain whether he merits the company he keeps. But Gambit is far from cold. He is fiercely loyal, particularly to those he accepts into his inner circle. When he commits to someone, whether it's a teammate or a romantic relationship, his loyalty is unbreakable. His connection with Rogue , in particular, demonstrates his emotional depth: he loves passionately, calmly, and without expectation, willing to bear loneliness or heartache in order to give her the space she needs to feel safe. This commitment extends to the X-Men, even when his past undermines the team's faith in him.

Gambit's romance with Rogue is one of the most iconic in Marvel history. Their chemistry is undeniable; his flirtatious charm and her guarded sensitivity create a dynamic that is both playful and profoundly emotional. They bring out the best and worst in each other, yet their relationship is built on trust, compassion, and an unwavering sense of longing.  Even when they're apart, their bond feels indestructible, based on a shared knowledge of what it means to live with a rough background. Remy's a gambler, both practically and emotionally, and he believes in taking risks even when they hurt. Anna Marie is cautious, thoughtful, and seeks to minimize harm.  She automatically protects others, even at the expense of her own desires. Despite their differences, they share a common emotional core: both have felt like outsiders, are afraid of harming others, and consciously doubt their own worthiness for love. Gambit recognizes Rogue's strength and tenderness, while Rogue sees Gambit's charm and wounded sincerity. They fill each other's voids: he gives her warmth, acceptance, and patience, while she provides him with purpose, trust, and protection to improve and understand each other in a way that few others can. And that's why Remy cares and loves her wife very deeply. With his interactions with some characters, Gambit and Wolverine share a complicated brother-in-arms dynamic. Logan is initially skeptical of Remy because of Gambit's secrecy and dubious past, which contradict Logan's instincts. However, they eventually develop a reluctant respect. Both men understand what it's like to live with guilt, function in moral ambiguity, and be perceived as dangerous even when their intentions are good. Storm and Gambit have one of the most intimate and meaningful friendships among the X-Men as Gambit once cared for Storm while she was temporarily de-aged, gaining her trust and developing a protective relationship.

Even Gambit and Rocket form an unexpectedly funny duo. Their mutual passion of thieving, explosives, and breaking the rules creates instant chemistry. Rocket admires Remy's willingness to get his hands dirty, whereas Gambit finds Rocket's humor and wild energy interesting, if occasionally demanding. He even cares and heals Rocket's wounds with his Chronovium powered cards after a gambling fight in the planet Knowhere recently. Gambit's moral compass is complex, but not broken. He is a thief by trade, and there is still a part of him that enjoys risk, secrecy, and doing the unthinkable. But he sincerely wants to do good.  He fights not only to protect others, but also to show to himself that he is deserving of forgiveness that something he frequently questions. Despite his tragic history, Gambit retains an upbeat, even playful disposition as he approached risk with a reckless grin, as if life were a high-stakes game that he refused to lose. His charisma, daring nature, make him one among the X-Men's most captivating characters: a guy defined not by perfection, but by dedication, passion, and the captivating appeal of someone who is always one step ahead, whether in a battle or a card game. Has slightly higher health compared to other Vanguards. His primary fire, Vine Strike, extends Groot's arms to deal damage from a long range. Despite its appearance, it counts as a projectile. His secondary fire, Spore Bomb, launches a projectile which splits itself into six smaller shards upon impact. Can deal very high damage if both the main projectile and its splinters hit the target. His melee attack, Furious Flora, is distinct for dealing knockback every two hits. It can be weaved with his Vine Strike for higher damage-per-second. Groot is able to build wooden walls that can block enemy view; players can change the direction the walls are built to even serve as platforms.

It can be weaved with his Vine Strike for higher damage-per-second. Groot is able to build wooden walls that can block enemy view; players can change the direction the walls are built to even serve as platforms. These interact directly with his passive, Flora Colossus, which grants Groot the ability to "awaken" the wooden walls if he's nearby them, which provides extra effects. Ironwood Walls have higher health (700) and are longer in width. When awakened they provide Groot with 40 bonus health-per-second (up to 250). Groot can only have one active at a time. Thornlash Walls have much lower health (250) and are shorter in width. When awakened they deal damage to enemies nearby that are attacked by Groot and his team. Groot can have up to three active at a time, and can build them continuously by holding the button. Throwing Spore Bomb directly at the wall if there is an enemy near it will cause the wall to lash out multiple times, both to the bomb as well to the split spores that spawn from it. Both walls can deny plenty of attacks and even Ultimates. In particular, it can block Jeff the Land Shark 's It's Jeff! if the wall is placed in front of him before he tries to devour the team, as it'll block his line of sight. Placing any of Groot's walls over certain hero-spawned obstacles will instantly destroy them, such as Peni Parker 's Arachno Mines, Moon Knight 's Ancient Ankhs, and Namor 's Aquatic Dominions. His Ultimate, Strangling Prison, launches vines that pull enemies in and imprison them for a few seconds while dealing damage-over-time. Enemies affected by this ability cannot move but are still able to attack and use non-mobility abilities. If Groot throws the Ultimate at one of his walls, enemies will be pulled and pinned onto it. Not very effective in moving objectives since he is forced to constantly reposition his wooden walls and burn his cooldowns. Moving objectives will instantly destroy his walls if they are placed in front of them.

By placing Groots Ironwood Walls or Thornlash Walls, Groot can effectively seperate the frontline of the enemy team from the backline. By doing this, Groot's walls block incoming healing, allowing your team to swiftly eliminate the seperated tanks. Groots Thornlash Walls have a much greater range than the Ironwood Wall. Groot can use this to his advantage by blocking (remaining) enemies from retreating. Groot can also do this with his Ironwood wall at much closer ranges with a bigger area. While playing Groot, remember that his Thornlash walls actually do damage. By placing walls behind your enemies, you can strategically eliminate them quickly with their clicks if they ever get in range with your walls. Groot is one of the strongest heroes while playing in tight corners, gaps, or areas. By playing in these areas, Groots walls can (almost) completely block all pathways from retreating to the enemy team.

Groot is one of the strongest heroes while playing in tight corners, gaps, or areas. By playing in these areas, Groots walls can (almost) completely block all pathways from retreating to the enemy team. These can be areas such as the entryway to Klyntar, when the payload turns on Spider Islands, above entryways on Mission Areas, and most effectively when the maps walls arise on Steller Spaceports Mission Area. Groot is a perfect counter against Peni's spidernests. By placing your walls, Thornlash or Ironwood, Groot can cancel/destroy Peni's nests immediately. Groot has an extremely powerful ultimate. After shooting his vine cluster, any nearby enemies are trapped into 1 point, unable to move. When paired with any high-burst damage, it can (almost) effectively eliminate the trapped enemies. This can be Namor's ultimate, Moon Knights ultimate, Iron Man's ultimate, or even Squirrel Girl's main attack. It's recommended to place walls before or after you use your ultimate. Remember, Groot's walls deal valuable damage, allowing you to get high amounts of burst damage in your ultimate. Personality [ ] https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Groot_-_Hero_Switch_01.ogg I am Groot! Groot Groot possesses a delicate, childish innocence combined with a deep, instinctive insight. Despite his vocabulary of "I am Groot," he has an array of emotions, including tremendous curiosity, delight, grief, and affection. Groot is naturally gentle and empathic, creating small but profound ties with his friends around him, particularly with his partner in crime Rocket . He does not seek attention or leadership; rather, he observes, listens, and reacts with genuine emotional honesty. He is widely known for being a flora colossus of a few words, said words being I am Groot, with only a select few of people who understand him like his fellow Guardians of the Galaxy , even more so with telepathic heroes such as Emma Frost or Phoenix . But while a few words short he makes up for in a heart bigger than himself and a reliable nature as firm as his bark. While his mouth is only capable of a few words he understands more than others may realize as Emma and Jean demonstrate.

But while a few words short he makes up for in a heart bigger than himself and a reliable nature as firm as his bark. While his mouth is only capable of a few words he understands more than others may realize as Emma and Jean demonstrate. As an alien plant hero, Groot also holds a love for nature whether it be flora or fauna, Groot had kindness for all, including the plants of Klyntar , a harsh and dangerous planet. Despite his gentle nature however, Groot is also shown to violent and aggressive should the situation arise, especially if you hurt those he cares about. Overall, Groot's personality grows alongside his physical growth, reflecting various stages of emotional development. His primary beliefs stay constant: he is caring, protective, and believes in the concept of chosen family. Groot exemplifies the concept that strength does not always require loud words; it can grow silently, like a tree, and remain steady when it matters the most. Groot is a compassionate, devoted, and altruistic kind giant whose strength stems from empathy rather than words. As one of the few characters in this game with a true one-shot, he has a unique niche of being able to kill through high healing numbers with good accuracy, making him a powerful answer to healing-heavy compositions provided he has the skill to make it work. As befits an archer, Hawkeye is most comfortable at a distance. However, unlike other ranged specialists like Black Widow or Hela , Hawkeye doesn't typically want to be as far away as possible to his targets, as not only are his projectiles less reliable at long distance due to their travel time, but his passive will only activate if his target is within 40 meters of him. Instead, he wants to strike a balance between being close enough to an enemy to activate his passive and increase his damage, but not so close that aiming becomes too difficult for him. Hawkeye feasts against enemies who lack the proper means of reaching or contesting him. Heroes that rely on playing mostly static positions such as Peni Parker , Winter Soldier , and most of the Strategists will struggle heavily against him. In contrast, heroes with shields or the mobility to rush him/get out of his sightline quickly, such as Spider-Man , Captain America , or Venom , will be difficult for Hawkeye to deal with, as he is severely lacking in defensive tools and in-combat mobility. Hawkeye has two primary arrows at his disposal.

Hawkeye has two primary arrows at his disposal. The first is his Piercing Arrow, an accurate, high-damaging projectile that deals hefty damage when fully charged and with full Archer's Focus. These arrows do not have an ammo pool, meaning Hawkeye does not need to reload aside from simply nocking another arrow. Alternatively, he can also use Blast Arrow, which has him prime three explosive arrows that he fires in a cone shape in front of him. Unlike his Piercing Arrow, these arrows have a limited resource that prevent them from being spammed, and they also do not get any benefit from Archer's Focus. With full charge and focus, a single headshot from Piercing Arrow will deal a whopping 350 damage, enough to kill almost every non-Vanguard in the game in a single hit with the exception of Mister Fantastic . With enough focus and accuracy, your ability to instantly get a kill on a target will make you an incredibly valuable asset to your team. Because of your unique ability to land an instant kill, target priority is crucial when playing Hawkeye. You should always be prioritizing backline Strategists or Duelists, while usually only going for Vanguards when they are either the only targets left or when there are no openings to target their squishier allies. Piercing Arrow is the attack you will use in 90% of situations. You should refrain from firing this attack wildly, as not only will the arrows be slower and harder to land, but you lose out on the damage you get from both charging the attack and from his passive. Instead, take time to charge the shot and your passive before you fire, and also take a moment to see how your target is moving so predicting their movement becomes significantly easier. If it is safe to do so, taking off-angles or flank routes can be a highly rewarding, if not risky option to get a better view on key targets. However, make sure you plan out an escape route before firing, as once you do, smarter enemies will be alerted to your presence, and if you can't escape in time, you will be in serious trouble. Blast Arrow is primarily used as a more reliable close-range option when compared to his Piercing Arrow.

Blast Arrow is primarily used as a more reliable close-range option when compared to his Piercing Arrow. Though it may lack the ability to one-shot that his Piercing Arrow has, you should not underestimate Blast Arrows' potential: its wide AoE makes it a very consistent damage option at close to mid range, especially against agile flankers, clustered groups of enemies, or when fired from a high-ground position. While the limited charges do prevent the arrows from being fired in rapid succession, do note that they automatically recharge at a rate of 0.5 seconds even while primed, meaning that if you pace out each of your shots, you can fire these arrows indefinitely. Crescent Slash is Hawkeye's primary defensive option. Hawkeye will perform a quick forward slash that deals a small amount of damage and knocks the target backward, putting distance between him and the target. This is your primary means of getting pesky flankers off of you. Always make sure to keep this ability ready for when you think you're about be dove on, and if it is on cooldown, play closer to your team since you don't have the added layer of safety the ability offers. Hypersonic Arrow is a powerful offensive tool in Hawkeye's arsenal. After a brief windup, Hawkeye will fire a fast arrow that pierces any enemies or shields it hits, slowing the target and dealing two instances of damage that add up to a total of 110. This is one of the few non-melee attacks in the game capable of piercing barriers from characters like Doctor Strange or Magneto (note that it cannot pierce personal barriers from heroes like Hulk ). Because of this, it is a good idea to launch this at a shield tank in order to deal some solid damage to them and any enemies standing behind them, netting you a decent chunk of ult charge and potentially killing an injured target in the backline. The slow effect on this ability also makes it a decent opening attack, allowing you to deal a solid chunk of damage and slowing them down for an easy follow-up shot that could net a potential pick. Hawkeye has a unique quick melee, Ronin Slash, in which he swings his wakizashi shortsword in front of him up to two times in succession.

Hawkeye has a unique quick melee, Ronin Slash, in which he swings his wakizashi shortsword in front of him up to two times in succession. This attack has the unique property of being able to deflect projectiles, completely nullifying their damage, however it cannot deflect AoE effects such as explosions or effects caused by projectiles on hit such as stuns or other types of crowd control. This can be a decent last-ditch defensive option against up-close targets, letting you deflect some of their assault while dealing a small amount of damage and buying time for a teammate to come to your aid. Due to the unreliable nature of this property, however, you should not rely heavily on it to keep you alive when being attacked up-close. Instead, treat it as a last resort for when you don't have time to prime a shot and focus on trying to kill your attacker outright with either a carefully-aimed Piercing Arrow or with your Blast Arrows. Skyward Leap gives Hawkeye free reign to take most high-ground positions. It is a high vertical double-jump with some horizontal air control. The cooldown for this ability starts when you hit the ground, so try to get grounded ASAP after using it to minimize its downtime. This can also be a last-ditch movement option to buy yourself time against a close-range attacker if your Crescent Slash is on cooldown. However, note that you will be an easy target for ranged enemies while airborne, so use this tactic with discretion. Archer's Focus is Hawkeye's passive, in which his Piercing Arrow's damage will increase the longer he aims near a target. This passive is key to Hawkeye's success, and why as Hawkeye, you should attempt to space out and plan your shots rather than firing wildly. One well-timed shot with fully-charged focus is often all it takes to swing a fight in your favor. Hawkeye's ultimate, Hunter's Sight, supercharges Hawkeye's already impressive ranged capabilities. After a brief windup, Hawkeye enters a super-focused state, during which his Archer's Focus will charge significantly faster and all enemies in his line of sight will leave behind stationary purple afterimages while moving around.

After a brief windup, Hawkeye enters a super-focused state, during which his Archer's Focus will charge significantly faster and all enemies in his line of sight will leave behind stationary purple afterimages while moving around. Hitting these afterimages will deal full damage to the target, however he cannot headshot the afterimages. The afterimages will also disappear if the target exits his line of sight, though they will linger for a brief moment before doing so. This ultimate is an exceptional clean-up tool, allowing you to quickly sweep an injured team or force them to use a defensive ultimate to counter you. Barriers act as a wall to your line of sight, so shield Vanguards such as Doctor Strange, Magneto, or Captain America can nullify your afterimages of them with their shields. During the ultimate, focus on prioritizing backline squishies or characters with high agility, as you can quickly whittle them down while nullifying the latter's ability to dodge, drastically reducing their lifeline. In contrast, avoid targeting Vanguards unless there are no other targets, as their large health pool means that shots from the ultimate will often be wasted on them. Due to the significantly increased charge rate for his passive during his ultimate, rapid-firing arrows is actually the way to go, as it can net you the most damage in the least amount of time. Much like with Doctor Strange's Eye of Agamotto, you can hit enemies multiple times in a single attack by hitting both the target and their afterimage with your Blast Arrows. A fully-charged Blast Arrow volley hitting both an enemy and their afterimage is enough to KO a 250 hp target in a single hit, and leaves 275 hp targets at critical health so a single quick melee can finish them off. If it is safe to get closer to an enemy, this can actually secure a KO during your ultimate more reliably than trying to burst them down with your Piercing Arrow can. Hawkeye's team-up, Moonlit Slash, gives some extra utility on his slash. On top of its initial damage and knockback, it now also fires a shockwave that amplifies healing for allies and gives a damage vulnerability to enemies.

On top of its initial damage and knockback, it now also fires a shockwave that amplifies healing for allies and gives a damage vulnerability to enemies. This can offer some extra support to your team from a safe distance, however keep in mind that it will sacrifice your one defensive ability, making you more vulnerable if you use it haphazardly. Personality [ ] https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Hawkeye_-_Hero_Spawned_06.ogg Every fight, I say to myself: I might go down, but I'll go down swingin'. Hawkeye Clint Barton, also known by his codenane Hawkeye, is calm in a crisis and proficient at improvising his way out of a tight situation. His personality combines dry wit, sarcastic, dependability, assertive and quiet resilience. Unlike many of his superhero peers, Hawkeye lacks superpowers, which only adds to his relatability and underdog appeal. He is frequently seen as the most grounded member of the Avengers , acting as a human heart and anchor amid a group of gods, super-soldiers, and geniuses. His caustic wit and laid-back demeanor conceal a strong feeling of duty and pain, particularly as someone who has witnessed both personal loss and the darker aspects of heroism. A skilled and resourceful individual, Clint is a calm, skilled and calculating S.H.I.E.L.D. agent, marksman and fighter, who focuses on knowledge rather than brute force, frequently employing sarcasm and humor to deal with difficult situations. Clint is deeply devoted to his teammates and to those he loves and cares about. He frequently serves as the group's emotional core, providing silent support and a sense of normalcy. His close relationship with Natasha Romanoff and protective disposition toward newer or younger heroes like Kate Bishop , demonstrate his caring, loyal and guiding qualities. At the same time, he has flaws including being headstrong, impulsive, and prone to guilt. This complexity is especially visible in narratives involving moral dilemma or personal tragedy, such as his role as Ronin during a time of trauma as he worked from the shadows.

Her primary fire, Nightsword Thorn, is a high-damage hitscan attack. Her secondary fire, Piercing Night, throws four blades that explode after a few seconds. These projectiles can latch onto enemies, and each blade deals individual damage in addition to exploding after a brief duration. The blades will explode even if they are not attached to enemies. Soul Drainer is a lobbed energy sphere that deals minimal damage but can briefly stun multiple enemies in a small radius. This ability can even interrupt certain Ultimates. Astral Flock transforms Hela into a high-speed crow and allows her to fly forth in any direction, being useful as an escape or repositioning tool. She is completely immune to all damage and crowd-control abilities during flight. Her Ultimate, Goddess of Death, sends Hela high into the air. The player's field-of-view changes to first person, and the player can then throw Nastrond Crows that explode on impact in a huge radius and deal heavy damage. When activating Goddess of Death, Hela gains a hefty separate health bar of 1000 points. Even if this health bar is depleted, she will not die, but will instead revert to her normal form with the health she previously had before activating her Ultimate. Weaknesses [ ] Poor means to deal with divers, especially when Astral Flock is on cooldown. Lacks any self-sustaining abilities. Hela cannot be healed by teammates during Astral Flock's flight. Hela to Venom The goddess of death, Hela, is defined first and foremost by absolute confidence. She does not question her right to rule or destroy; she assumes it.  Unlike villains driven by insecurity or desperation, Hela operates from confidence in her power, her lineage, and her superiority.  This makes her terrifyingly calm, as she doesn’t rush, panic, or overexplain. Violence to her is not emotional chaos but a natural extension of authority, delivered with elegance and precision. She is driven not only by raw conquest, but also by cosmic responsibility and ambition. As ruler of Hel and Niffleheim, Hela regards herself as a necessary force in the natural cycle of death. She rarely acts out of bitterness; instead, she strategizes, bargains, and manipulates, seeing mortals and gods alike as parts in a much broader game. She has a fundamental dislike for power that is based on titles rather than competence. Kings, according to her, are loud, untrustworthy, and prone to vanity. Odin 's infirmity and Loki 's distractions further confirm her opinion that rule should be consistent, disciplined, and gained by perseverance. Unlike others, she never rests, abdicates responsibilities, or pretends her task is optional. This fills her with chilly pride: she believes herself as the only monarch trustworthy enough to bear an endless load without complaint. Hela is noted for her strategic patience and deep opportunism. Hela does not seek to dominate for the sake of dominance; instead, she waits, observes, and takes advantage of cosmic imbalances. Her interest in Chronovium , Celestials , and Timestream Entanglement stems from calculation rather than curiosity. Every combat is evaluated based on its outcome, such as souls, champions, and leverage. Even partnerships are viewed as tools, transient structures designed to fall at the most profitable time. She expects betrayal and sees it as a sign of intelligence, not malice. Beneath her cruelty lurks an idea that death and darkness are not evils, but rather necessary.

Beneath her cruelty lurks an idea that death and darkness are not evils, but rather necessary. This belief is why the dark god Knull 's remarks speak to her: she sees herself as a balancing force, doomed to be loathed for doing what the universe requires leading to her being his Queen in Black. Hela does not seek validation from mortals or gods, but she does seek recognition from equals, beings who recognize that existence necessitates death. Her acceptance of Knull is not romantic weakness, but ideological alignment with someone who speaks the same cosmic truth she has for millennia. Hela is appealing in terms of power rather than affection. She doesn't kneel, even when she agrees to govern with another. Overall, Hela is a cold-hearted, ideologically driven force of inevitability, a queen who despises fraudulent power and values endurance, competence, and cosmic purpose before titles or sentiment. She is patient, calculated, and unabashedly brutal, seeing death and darkness as necessary forces that maintain universal balance. Alliances are tools, treachery is inevitable, and power is only meaningful when it is permanent. Her acceptance of Knull is not submission but rather an expansion, a recognition of shared values rather than a desire for affirmation. Above all, she is marked by absolute certainty: no matter how hard life and light fight, everything ends, and when it does, it falls under her control. Despite being the daughter of Loki in the comics and Norse mythology, there is a possibility that she is Odin's daughter—and therefore sister of Thor , Loki, and Angela —in this game, just like in the MCU. This was initially proved in their dialogue in Loki's lore " Destined Kingship ": Loki: "O sister, great queen, it– " Hela: "Whenever you call me queen, Loki–or, for that matter, sister– I know you want something. This was later changed in Season 4: Heart of the Dragon , as all mentions of Loki referring to Hela as a sister were removed. The Marvel Rivals Swimsuit Special Thor’s skin, " Worthy Waves ", shows him carrying a small backpack labeled “ BROTHER ,” which contains toys of Loki and Hela, which suggests that Thor considers himself Hela’s brother. In the " Nowhere to Run " Gallery Card from Season 3: The Abyss Awakens , it says: "her own kin would come to deliver justice soon enough", confirming her blood relation to the Asgardian family. With the revelation that Angela is Odin ’s firstborn, Hela would be Angela’s younger sister. Official description Bruce Banner , also known by his alter ego, the Hulk , is a Vanguard hero in Marvel Rivals , and is the 2nd hero introduced to the game's roster. As Bruce Banner, he is very frail and has a limited moveset, but has access to ranged attacks and a knockback ability. However, his Ultimate allows him to transform into the Hulk, his main combat form, with an extremely low energy cost, the lowest of any Ultimate in the game. As Hulk he serves as a bulky frontliner with high mobility and specialized in melee pressure. If Hulk's health is depleted he reverts back to Bruce Banner, effectively giving him two health bars. Bruce Banner's primary fire is Gamma Ray Gun, which has a high rate-of-fire but deals low damage. However, each successful hit adds Gamma Energy, necessary to transform back into Hero Hulk; headshots grant even more energy. Bruce Banner's Gamma Grenade knocks back enemies, but most importantly creates a spell field on the ground that grants Gamma Energy. The grenade also deals knockback to Bruce himself, which with a well-timed jump, can be utilized to escape from enemies or to reach high ground (this can be useful for getting out of spawn slightly faster). Bruce Banner always starts matches with his Ultimate, Puny Banner, available, which allows him to transform into the Hulk. During his transformation he is completely immune to all damage and crowd control effects. The Hulk's primary fire is Heavy Blow, quick swings with a decent range and arc to dish out consistent damage.

During his transformation he is completely immune to all damage and crowd control effects. The Hulk's primary fire is Heavy Blow, quick swings with a decent range and arc to dish out consistent damage. Despite being more suited for melee, the Hulk has access to two projectiles: Gamma Burst, which Hulk performs his signature thunderclap which launches a single shockwave projectile that can pierce enemies in a line; and Radioactive Lockdown, a blast of gamma energy that deals minimal damage but stuns enemies for a few seconds. Radioactive Lockdown can prevent enemies from capturing objectives as the gauge will not fill if they are stunned. Incredible Leap allows the Hulk to jump over larger distances, the height increasing the longer the move is charged. Additionally, if Hulk jumps directly on a wall, he clings onto it. Lastly, if the leap hits a flying enemy, they will be knocked down and dragged with him. Indestructible Guard projects an energy shield around the Hulk and all nearby allies, preventing and absorbing all damage taken, converting it into Gamma Energy to fuel the Hulk's Ultimate. If the Hulk is damaged while the shield is up, it converts 100% of the damage into Gamma Energy and 10% of the damage from his allies. The Hulk's Ultimate, Hulk Smash, temporarily transforms the Hulk into Monster Hulk, which restores and nearly doubles his max health and enhances his abilities: Heavy Blow has more range and deals more damage at the expense of being slightly slower. Gamma Burst's projectile becomes slower, but deals almost double damage and has a much lower cooldown (1 second down from 8 seconds). Radioactive Lockdown's projectile is faster and has a much lower cooldown (5 seconds down from 15 seconds). Monster Hulk also instantly gains a new Ultimate, World Breaker, wherein he grabs an enemy and delivers a series of devastating slam attacks for massive damage. During this ability, he gains a 30% damage reduction. Weaknesses [ ] Bruce Banner is incredibly frail, having the lowest max health in the game, on top of having no mobility tools other than with Gamma Grenade, and a very limited moveset. Despite having projectiles, the Hulk is susceptible to enemies with long-distance attacks that can out-zone him.
