TEAM-UP BONUS - +100 Max Health Strategy [ ] Hulk is a high-risk, high-reward tank who can quickly shift between harassing the enemy's backline and protecting his own on a whim. His high mobility allows him to quickly engage and disengage the enemy, giving him free reign to take or abandon almost any fight with enough foresight. Because Hulk lacks the tools to be a frontline wall for his team in the same way that Magneto or Doctor Strange can, it is not recommended to run him as a solo tank. One of the most important skills to learn as Hulk is learning which fights to take. Your large frame makes you highly susceptible to focus fire if you rush in haphazardly, so you should learn to engage the enemy when they're distracted by the rest of your team so they're forced to divert their attention between you and them. On the flipside, when you feel that a fight is going awry, you should not hesitate to jump out lest you be caught by the enemy.

On the flipside, when you feel that a fight is going awry, you should not hesitate to jump out lest you be caught by the enemy. As Bruce Banner, you have the lowest health in the game at only 200, and both your weapon and sole ability in Gamma Grenade are highly ineffective. You should only be transforming back into this form while in the midst of jumping back to your team, as if you're transforming into Bruce Banner in the midst of the enemy, you are almost certainly dead. While in this form, focus on playing as safe as possible, landing as many shots with your gamma gun as you can to build up your gamma energy and transform back into Hulk as soon as possible. Throwing the Gamma Grenade at your feet as Banner will automatically give you 8% of your gamma energy, so try to do so as often as possible to hasten your charge time. Note that during all of your transformations—whether it be from Bruce Banner to Hero Hulk, Hero Hulk to Monster Hulk, or either of the two Hulks to Bruce Banner again—you will be completely invincible, meaning you cannot receive any damage or be affected by crowd control. As Hero Hulk, you have two main methods of attack. His primary fire, Heavy Blow, is a series of fast, reliable melee swings with a wide AoE. While each individual hit may not be powerful, it will quickly build up high damage numbers the longer you remain next to the enemy, which, thanks to Hulk's incredible mobility, you can easily do. If the enemy is further away, your secondary fire, Gamma Burst, has you clap your hands to launch a fast projectile that deals solid damage. The projectile has infinite range, allowing Hulk a burst damage option even at far distances. As an added bonus, successfully landing the Gamma Burst on an enemy will reduce the cooldown of Indestructible Guard by one second. Your Gamma Burst is your highest-damaging attack outside of your ultimate, making it great as an engage when jumping to an enemy or as a finisher on someone who is injured. Hitting multiple enemies with a single Gamma Burst will reduce the cooldown by one second for each enemy hit, potentially allowing you to shave off six whole seconds from the cooldown if you can somehow hit every enemy with a single clap.

Hitting multiple enemies with a single Gamma Burst will reduce the cooldown by one second for each enemy hit, potentially allowing you to shave off six whole seconds from the cooldown if you can somehow hit every enemy with a single clap. Weave your clap in between your basic attacks constantly to reduce your Indestructible Guard's cooldown and thus drastically boost your own survivability. Indestructible Guard is your primary means of mitigation. Hulk will create a gamma bubble shield on himself and all allies within five meters of him. Any damage dealt to the shield will charge his ultimate. This ability has multiple strong use cases. The first is as a way to engage on top of an enemy safely, protecting you from their initial burst so you can start punching away without worry. The second is as a way to secure your escape, allowing you to mitigate damage and crowd control thrown your way while you try to jump out. The third is as a quick peel option for your teammates, protecting them from big damage ultimates like Iron Man's Invincible Pulse Cannon or a flanker harassing the backline. Radioactive Lockdown has the potential for huge denials for the enemy team. Hulk fires a projectile that deals minimal damage but will exile the target for two seconds. While exiled, the target is essentially treated as if they do not exist: they cannot move, act, or receive damage or healing from any outside sources except for Hulk himself. Hitting an exiled enemy as Hulk will prematurely remove the status effect. Like his Indestructible Guard, this ability has multiple use cases. First off, it serves as a way to quickly prevent a target from escaping: giving you time to leap toward them and start pummeling them before they can start running. The next is as a way to temporarily disable a target in the midst of a fight, buying you and your team some time to recover before they come back. Finally, you can use it to interrupt or even outright nullify big ultimates or abilities such as Scarlet Witch's Reality Erasure or Spider-Man's Spectacular Spin. Due to the ability's long cooldown, take care to not use the ability haphazardly, as it has the potential for huge denials when timed right. Incredible Leap is Hulk's primary means of movement.

Due to the ability's long cooldown, take care to not use the ability haphazardly, as it has the potential for huge denials when timed right. Incredible Leap is Hulk's primary means of movement. Hulk can charge a leap for up to two seconds before jumping forward a large distance. While leaping, he can cling to a wall by holding his jump button while colliding with one, and if he collides with an airborne enemy mid-leap, he will drag them down to earth, leaving them stunned. This is undoubtedly your most important ability as Hulk. It is key to everything you want to do, from engaging to disengaging to even dealing with pesky fliers. There is no cooldown on this ability nor is there a limit to how long you can have a leap charged, so always try to charge this ability even in the midst of fighting so you can have a leap ready to go at a moment's notice to either disengage or continue chasing an enemy. Try to get used to the timing it takes to charge up a minimum-power leap (roughly 0.7 seconds) so you can string multiple low-power leaps back to back. This can allow you to maneuver around the map faster than simply walking around or waiting for a fully-charged leap can. Hulk's ultimate, Hulk Smash!, transforms Hero Hulk into the towering Monster Hulk. In this form, you gain a massive health boost, immunity to knockbacks and seizes, and stronger versions of your Gamma Burst and Radioactive Lockdown on significantly shorter cooldowns, however you also lose access to your Indestructible Guard. This form can last up to 12 seconds or until Monster Hulk sustains enough damage. If he transforms back with health still remaining, he will transform into Hero Hulk with health proportional to the amount he has left, but if he loses all of it, he will transform back into Bruce Banner. As Monster Hulk, all of your attacks deal increased damage with shorter cooldowns, and your Heavy Blow deals knockback as well. This allows you to cause immense chaos in the midst of an enemy, and stringing in your melee attack between Gamma Bursts and leaps can lead to deadly combos. Monster Hulk's ultimate is World Breaker, which has him grab a nearby enemy to deal high damage and put them in a hard stun state.

This allows you to cause immense chaos in the midst of an enemy, and stringing in your melee attack between Gamma Bursts and leaps can lead to deadly combos. Monster Hulk's ultimate is World Breaker, which has him grab a nearby enemy to deal high damage and put them in a hard stun state. It is not recommended to use this ability right after transforming as it wastes precious seconds of the transformation: instead, use it as a finisher for the form to squeeze as much value out of the high health pool and innate damage reduction the ultimate offers as possible. While transforming into Monster Hulk, you will immediately be healed to the full Monster Hulk health level regardless of how injured you were before activation. As such, when you have your ultimate, don't hesitate to play aggressively so you can lull the enemy into a false sense of security when they think they have you cornered, only for you to transform and turn the tide back against them. Just make sure you don't activate it too late before you sustain too much damage and are forced to transform back into Banner. While you are immune to knockback and forced displacement effects, you are not completely immune to all crowd control. Grabs from characters such as Emma Frost's Diamond Form or Jeff's ultimate can still snag you, potentially leaving you wide-open, and you can still be stunned. Hulk is currently one of the few characters in the game with multiple team-ups. His first is Gamma Charge, in which he offers Black Panther a gamma shield when his health is low. The second is Fastball Special, in which he or The Thing can throw an allied Wolverine into the enemy to cause chaos. In the case of Fastball Special, it may be worth it to leap in with your Wolverine before throwing them, as you can then place an Indestructible Guard on yourself and your fellow Wolverine to protect the both of you as you cause chaos to the enemy. Bruce Banner in Hell's Heaven Dr. Bruce Banner is an extremely intellectual, quiet, shy and introspective person. An intelligent scientist, he is motivated by a strong interest in the environment around him, notably in gamma radiation and bioengineering. He is compassionate and cares about the well-being of others, frequently sacrificing his own life and safety for the greater good.  He's frequently regarded as a "nerd" in the traditional sense: highly smart, socially distant, and more at ease in a lab than in a crowd with his problem-solving abilities also align with the traditional nerd archetype. It is noted to recognize that Bruce is more than just book smart. He's emotionally knowledgeable and extremely empathetic, yet his socially uncomfortable and self-consciousness can make him appear socially isolated. Nevertheless, his intelligence carries a heavy burden. Bruce is continuously consumed by remorse and self-loathing as a result of his inability to control the Hulk, the destructive power within him. He is a very thinking man who frequently has self-doubt and fear about the risk he poses to others around him. He has severe emotional scars, primarily from his horrific childhood. His father, Brian Banner, was an abusive alcoholic who feared Bruce's intelligence and thought he was a monster. That fear escalated into aggression, both toward Bruce and his mother, forming Bruce's deep fear of fury and loss of control. His suppressed trauma, terror, and bottled-up anger would eventually erupt as the Hulk. Unlike many other heroes, Bruce did not seek fame or power. He simply wanted to assist others with science and ended up becoming someone he fears and often makes jokes with himself and people whom he works with to cope with his personal struggles. One in-game interaction has him joking to Steve Rogers when he impersonates the Hulk's voice just for fun.

One in-game interaction has him joking to Steve Rogers when he impersonates the Hulk's voice just for fun. While many of them admire his intelligence and understand his hardships, Bruce frequently feels like an outsider. He has a close relationship with Tony Stark , who regards Bruce as an intellectual equal and collaborates with him on scientific initiatives like the TRD (Timestream Reintegration Device) created by Dr. Reed Richards .  Natasha Romanoff and him have a unique, deep connection based on a shared awareness of inner struggles as well. Recently, Bruce Banner invented the Gamma Belt to regulate his transformation into the Hulk, allowing him to become the Hulk quickly while also providing him some residual control over the monster, especially over the Monster Hulk form, the most destructive side of the Hulk. It was also intended to avoid relying on emotions for transformation and to store gamma energy which is why Hulk is capable of releasing gamma energy during his form. Despite this, Bruce has repeatedly demonstrated that he is a hero. He rescues lives, helps to those in need, and defends others with both his brains and his huge authority. He bears the consequences of his actions as the Hulk, and his quest is more than only containing the Hulk, but also learning to accept both sides of himself as a scientist and a monster. The Hulk When Banner transforms, his mental faculties frequently revert to an impressionable stage, resulting in intense emotions, a lack of foresight, and a proclivity for destructive actions. The Hulk is the physical manifestation of Bruce Banner's repressed anger and frustration. He represents pure, uncontrollable rage and destruction, with a personality that contrasts sharply with Bruce's own calm and reasoned demeanor. Hulk is driven by instinct and emotion, and when he emerges, it’s often in response to overwhelming stress, danger, or threats to Bruce's safety or those he cares about. He’s incredibly strong and almost invulnerable, with an almost childlike mentality at times. Hulk always likes to destroy and smash all the time and that's his true nature.

He’s incredibly strong and almost invulnerable, with an almost childlike mentality at times. Hulk always likes to destroy and smash all the time and that's his true nature. One of the Hulk's traits is his antagonistic banters or picking fights with other heroes like The Thing and Wolverine . However, when he transforms back into Banner, he remains calm, which is why one of their in-game interactions with The Thing asks Bruce about the green guy who is about to change quickly. Hulk doesn’t communicate in the same way as Banner, often speaking in short, blunt phrases, and he is highly protective, particularly of those he sees as vulnerable. There are two sides of the Hulk. One is known as the Hero Hulk, it is controlled, communicative and tactical, while Monster Hulk is a state of raw, pure rage and uncontrolled destruction. Overall, despite his primitive rage, Hulk's demeanor contains a layer of innocence, since he does not completely comprehend the implications of his actions and is frequently perplexed by the world surrounding him but there are times that Hulk protects the innocent and smashes every enemy in his sight.  Hulk's relationship with his alter-ego Banner is built on equal parts opposition and mutual respect. While Banner often prefers a pragmatic and/or moral solution, Hulk often prefers to follow his instincts, which usually amounts to just smashing whatever is in his way. Because of that, the two egos often find themselves vying for control over their shared body, with both sides believing that their option would be for the better. In spite of their animosity, though, both Hulk and Banner understand that they are two halves of the same whole and cannot exist without the other, so they find some way to coexist regardless. Also, though the two of them often bicker, they also have genuine respect for the other ego over the things they have that the other lacks: Banner respects Hulk's strength and confidence to dive headfirst into danger, while Hulk respects Banner's humanity and faith in him to do the right thing, even if he must sacrifice control of his body to let him prove it. Overall, Hulk's rage belies a being who is every bit as heroic and noble as his human alter ego. Though ineloquent and unpredictable, when push comes to shove, Hulk will always stand on the right side of the fence.

According to the Prince of Orphans who was talking to Lin Lie , Hulk hails from the Collapsing Timeline which he becomes the Green Door's guardian. His secondary fire, Blazing Blast, creates a small AOE field that damages overtime. Human Torch has a limit of 3 Blazing Blasts he can create at any time, each Blazing Blast takes 3 seconds to regenerate. Each blazing blast field lasts up to 6 seconds before disappearing. Enemies take the most damage if hit with the blazing blast directly, but will take continuous damage if they stand within its field. Plasma Body allows for Human Torch to fly at a slightly faster rate. This ability cannot be used at the same time as using his other abilities. Pyro-Prison can be activated when two or more Blazing Blasts are active, when 2 are active and are within range of each other can create a firewall which will damage enemies who walk over it. When this ability is used when 3 or more Blazing Blasts are active, it will create a geometric shape with the Blazing Blasts acting as connected dots. When making a shape like a triangle, rectangle, etc. the area inside also acts as a flame field to which any enemies caught within will take overtime damage. Flaming Meteor is an ability that allows the Human Torch to dive down rapidly and cause explosive damage which also knocks back enemies caught within the blast. This ability will also destroy any Blazing Blasts caught within it's damage field, dealing extra damage with the blast radius of Flaming Meteor. Human Torch also gains temporary Bonus Health upon landing. His Ultimate. Supernova, causes the Human Torch to explode with fire causing damage to enemies around him. While in this state his Blazing Blasts will turn into Flame Tornadoes in which deal significantly more damage to enemies within it's radius. While in this state his Plasma Body and Blazing Blasts do not have a cooldown and thus can be used infinitely while the ultimate is active.

While in this state his Blazing Blasts will turn into Flame Tornadoes in which deal significantly more damage to enemies within it's radius. While in this state his Plasma Body and Blazing Blasts do not have a cooldown and thus can be used infinitely while the ultimate is active. This comes at the expense of Pyro-Prison being unusable for Supernova's duration. When paired with Invisible Woman , Human Torch gains access to United Siblings, which when activated converts 100% of damage taken into bonus health for 5 seconds. Weaknesses [ ] His main attack has a slow projectile speed and does less damage at long range that it does mid range. Pyro-Prison cannot create fire walls between Blazing Blasts if they each are on different elevations. Human Torch's Blazing Blasts and Pyro-Prison are stationary when placed and thus cannot do active damage to enemies outside their range. Human Torch The fiery, cocky and flamboyant Johnny Storm known as the Human Torch, is often defined by his youthful exuberance, recklessness, impulsiveness and strong sense of individuality. As the team's youngest member, Johnny is impetuous and thrill-seeking, always looking for excitement and often cracking jokes and acting before thinking things through, whether it's through high-speed flight, demonstrating his abilities, or participating in friendly rivalries, particularly with his teammate Ben Grimm . His confidence sometimes border on arrogance, but it derives from a strong desire to be noticed and admired, which is linked to his standing as a celebrity and public figure. Johnny is portrayed as a charming ladies' man who enjoys attention and often tries to impress women with his looks, fame, and powers. He’s confident, smooth-talking, and not shy about flirting, often using humor and flashy displays of his abilities (like flying or “flaming on”) to grab attention. His flirtatious nature is part of his fun-loving, extroverted personality. Despite his brash attitude, Johnny is a devoted companion and kind brother to Susan Storm . His emotional depth emerges during times of crisis, when he rises up to protect those he cares about, revealing a hidden maturity beneath his humorous confidence. He frequently utilizes comedy as a coping technique and to lighten the mood, but he is not immune to the weight of duty, especially as he develops and learns from the team's many adventures. Johnny's top priority is his family.

Johnny's top priority is his family. He has a deep, caring, and protective relationship with his older sister, Sue. As siblings, they have a natural mix of fondness, teasing, and sometimes disagreements, but their bond is solid. Johnny's link with her serves as a rare emotional anchor, and he often softens around her in ways he does not with others.  With Ben, their bond is a blend of competitiveness, profound friendship, and brotherly love, frequently exhibited via constant mocking and pranks. But behind it all is unwavering loyalty and respect. And, with Reed Richards , they have a mutual loyalty and concern for one another as teammates and family. Reed serves as a mentor or elder brother role to him, and they gradually gain a deeper understanding of one another. Additionally, Johnny and Peter Parker form one of the heroes' most well-known friendships. Their relationship is a unique blend of rivalry, banter, brotherhood, and deep mutual respect, forged over years of shared adventures, personal struggles, and a rare ability to truly understand each other as young heroes living double lives and Parker is most likely Johnny's closest friend outside of the Fantastic Four.  Overall, Johnny can be immature and self-centered, but experience tempers his conduct, making him more considerate and dependable. Still, his love of fun, fast cars, girls, and fame is an integral part of who he is. Johnny Storm embodies youthful vigor and passion, a hothead with a decent heart who is constantly striving to balance his ego with his heroic obligations and protecting the innocent who needs saving as the Human Torch. Trivia [ ] Human Torch's first appearance was in " Fantastic Four " (1961) #1 in November 1961. Johnny is the second Marvel character to use this mantle; the original Human Torch was an android named Jim Hammond, who debuted in " Marvel Comics " (1939) #1 in October 1939. He is considered the first hero published under the Marvel (then Timely Comics) banner. This connection is referenced in-game through Johnny's interaction with Ultron , where he calls Johnny a "fleshy inferior" compared to the Hammond android, expressing a preference for the original Torch's synthetic nature. Human Torch was datamined from multiple sources around December 2024, along with 15 other characters, including Angela , Blade , Captain Marvel , Deadpool , Emma Frost , Hit-Monkey , Invisible Woman , Mister Fantastic , M.O.D.O.K. , Phoenix , The Hood , The Thing , Ultron , and Valkyrie . [ 1 ] Human Torch was the first hero to have their Lord Icon changed. His original one was just his Prestige Artwork image but mirrored, while his new one is a close-up shot of the final frame of his Default MVP . The "First Steps" Team-Up ability with The Thing is a clear reference to the flying move they did in the film The Fantastic Four: First Steps (2025) . Johnny has a swimwear modelling contract with Janet Van Dyne, where he cannot be seen in any swimwear other than one of Van Dyne's designs. The orbs will return to Invisible Woman once reaching maximum distance, dealing damage and healing on the way back. This attack is not affected by damage falloff. She can reload primary fire without breaking her invisibility. Her secondary fire, Guardian Shield, creates a medium-sized energy barrier directly in front of the selected ally. Healing the ally and slowing enemies in the range in ~25%. Guardian Shield has 250 health and has infinite duration until destroyed or reclaimed. If reclaimed, the shield's health will quickly replenish if previously damaged. This ability can be reclaimed without breaking her invisibility. Pressing the reclaim button while no shield is on the field will place it in front of Invisible Woman. Allies near the shield also gain a healing-over-time effect. Allies standing behind the shield count as if they're out of the opponent line of sight, meaning that tracking abilities will not target them, such as Scarlet Witch 's Chaos Control and Cloak 's Darkforce Cloak. This also includes Ultimate abilities, most notably Star-Lord 's Galactic Barrage. Enemies that pass through the shield are slowed by 30%. Psionic Vortex is a projectile that creates an energy field that pulls enemies in while dealing continuous damage and slowing them by 50%. The vortex will form if it hits an enemy or the scenario, but the player can press the button again after firing the projectile to erupt the vortex earlier. The slow is only applied if enemies are near the center of the vortex. If this ability hits a flying enemy, they'll fall down to the ground and can't fly upwards until they leave the vortex's radius. Force Physics allows Invisible Woman to push or pull opponents through psionic energy while dealing damage. Once activated, the player can press different inputs to push or pull. Beneath her calm and loving façade is an unwavering determination, driven by loyalty to her family and a strong sense of duty to use her powers for good. She maintains an ideal balance between her personal life and her heroic duties, frequently serving as the team's moral compass during conflicts. Sue's personality shows a combination of empathy and assertiveness. She is very protective of her loved ones, particularly her husband Reed Richards and their children, as well as her brother Johnny Storm .

Susan's relationships with her family and teammates are essential to her identity, demonstrating her kindness, loyalty, and emotional depth. Her connection with her younger brother, Johnny, is one of friendly teasing and strong familial bonds.  Sue frequently serves as Johnny's moral guide and protector, especially during his younger, more reckless years.  Despite his immaturity and tendency to irritate her, she never loses faith in his potential. Their bond depicts the push and pull of real siblings, who are frequently frustrated with one another but are ultimately attached and fiercely protective. Sue and her husband, Reed, share one of Marvel's most enduring and complex marriages. Reed's talent and scientific obsession have occasionally made him distant or emotionally unavailable, putting their relationship to the strain. Sue, on the other hand, frequently bridges that gap thanks to her patience and emotional intelligence. She urges Reed to think beyond reasoning and connect with their family on a deeper level, and Reed admires her bravery and compassion. Their marriage has been tested by miscommunication, the weight of their obligations, and Reed's sometimes reckless quest of knowledge, but Sue's emotional intelligence and perseverance have constantly kept the family on track. She is frequently the heart of the team, balancing Reed's analytical approach with her genuine empathy. Their relationship is central to the Fantastic Four narrative, mixing great cosmic adventures with the relatable challenges of family and marriage. Sue and Ben Grimm share mutual respect and a genuine connection. She was among the first to see past his rocky exterior and discover the lovely, loyal man beneath. Sue treats Ben like a member of the family, frequently defending him when others belittle or pity him due of his hideous looks. In turn, Ben is fiercely protective of Sue and regards her as a sister figure. Their connection represents acceptance, empathy, and unshakable loyalty. Sue's greatest defining trait as a mother is her closeness with her two children, Franklin and Valeria Richards.

Sue's greatest defining trait as a mother is her closeness with her two children, Franklin and Valeria Richards. She is fiercely committed to them, balancing her work as a superhero with raising kids, developing Franklin's sensitive nature while assisting him in controlling his enormous powers, and promoting Valeria's brilliance while keeping her grounded. Her love for her family motivates many of her actions, and she always prioritizes their safety and happiness which she continually demonstrates compassion, courage, and strong familial values. Sue is also regarded as one of the most respected heroes, as shown by his treatment of Spider-Man . Her connection with Peter Parker distinguishes out because she treats him like family, based on mutual respect and common challenges. She frequently serves as a mentor, offering him empathy when he is overwhelmed, forming a bond that is almost like mother and son. Namor , the King of Atlantis, presents a new dynamic. He has always had romantic affections for Sue, but she is still faithful to Reed and rejects him. Nonetheless, she empathizes with his loneliness and appreciates his sense of honor, resulting in a dynamic of tension, respect, and unspoken understanding. Sue's calm attitude belies her fragility. She has moments of uncertainty, frustration, and anger, especially when she is disregarded or her family is threatened. Finally, the Invisible Woman's personality is distinguished by her compassion and commitment including her motherly, empathic, and protective core of the Fantastic Four, as she holds the team together with a strong sense of family and morals. While she can be quiet or introverted, she's tough and powerful, but often caring, demeanor that should not be overlooked. She is a genuinely compassionate person who uses her abilities and skills to defend others, frequently valuing family over all else. Capable of jumping three times while airborne. Capable of running horizontally along walls. His passive, Chi Absorption, gives him bonus health after assisting in defeating an enemy. His primary fire, Jeet Kune Do, consists of five consecutive strikes delivered at high speed. Each successful hit decreases the cooldown of Dragon's Defense by 1 second. His secondary fire, Dragon's Defense, gives him the ability to block incoming attacks, whether they're melee or ranged, by granting him 30% damage reduction. Damage taken during Dragon's Defense is converted to bonus health after the ability ends. He can parry almost any attack in the game while under the effects of Dragon's Defense, even from behind. This includes certain Ultimates such as Iron Man 's Invincible Pulse Cannon. After using Dragon's Defense, Iron Fist's primary fire temporarily changes to Yat Jee Chung Kuen, a flurry of punches, increasing his attack speed and damage against higher health opponents. This grants Iron Fist the means to stay in close range with his opponents, especially to take down both Vanguards and Strategists alike. Harmony Recovery allows Iron Fist to recover health, converting the excess healing into bonus health. K'un-Lun Kick is a high range flying attack that covers a decent range. Its damage is more than doubled against enemies with below 50% health. This ability is highly versatile as a gap closer or a escape tool, as well as a way to finish off enemies with low health. His Ultimate, Living Chi, instantly grants him an enhanced version of Yat Jee Chung Kuen, temporarily increasing his movement speed, damage dealt, and the range of his attacks. In addition, Dragon's Defense's cooldown is reduced by 80%. When paired with Luna Snow , he gains access to Lunar Chi, which enhances his Harmony Recovery to also heal allies within a nearby radius. Weaknesses [ ] Has very low attack range, especially when Yat Jee Chung Kuen is on cooldown. Requires proper resource management to play as his defensive tools are also his offensive; the player needs to be careful to activate them at the right time to ensure his survivability while also dealing damage. Very vulnerable if his defensive and evasive tools are on cooldown.

HEALING AMOUNT - 55/s DURATION - 3s BONUS HEALTH FALLOFF DELAY - 2s BONUS HEALTH FALLOFF SPEED - 15/s Strategy [ ] Core Gameplay: Low-Health Execution & Survival Iron Fist is an agile brawler that has various ways to enhance his survivability and excellent mobility. He excels at swiftly taking down low health targets and gaining bonus health through many of his abilities. His core ability is DRAGON'S DEFENSE - which converts all sources of damage taken into bonus health during a short blocking stance. Each hit with his normal primary attack, JEET KUNE DO , will reduce the cooldown of his block to allow for better cycling and utility. Both of his primary attacks also feature a lock-on mechanic that pulls him to the target he is aiming at with no delay between each refresh of the target. Strategy: Manage Ability Cooldowns: Several of your ability cooldowns are long to make up for your high damage potential. Managing your resources will allow more oppurtunities to provide leverage in team fights. Target Priority: A disorganized backline will struggle to combat you if they can't work together. Use this to your knowledge to know what enemy to target first before you strike. Stalling Objectives: Iron Fist is one of the best heroes when it comes to stalling objectives. Utilize the best of your mobility to do so effectively. Primary Attack (1): JEET KUNE DO (Left Mouse Button) Function: Consists of six individual melee strikes, the sixth strike dealing more damage and knocking back. Each hit reduces the cooldown of DRAGON'S DEFENSE by 1s. Role: Primary source of damage, chasing targets, and cooldown reduction.

Each hit reduces the cooldown of DRAGON'S DEFENSE by 1s. Role: Primary source of damage, chasing targets, and cooldown reduction. Strategy: Combo Attacks: A fast attack speed allows you to weave in K'UN-LUN KICK at the end of an attack cycle for additional damage. Cooldown Reduction: Connecting your strikes will refresh your block faster. Anti-Air Defense: The lock-on mechanic allows Iron Fist to move towards flying enemies and eliminate them if they don't have proper survival tools. Pull Baiting: Pull Baiting techs can be used to avoid incoming attacks with a long cast time. Target an enemy outside of range to pull yourself away. Primary Attack (2): YAT JEE CHUNG KUEN (Left Mouse Button) Function: After exiting DRAGON'S DEFENSE , attack with a barrage of punches - dealing more damage to enemies with higher max health. Role: Secondary source of damage, chasing targets, and tank busting. Strategy: Target Priority: Prioritize vanguards or duelists with greater health pools to maximize damage output. Assassination: Poke characters are weak when seperated from others. Focus them when they have created distance from their team. Anti-Air Defense: Although the pull is more clunky, Iron Fist can still effectively take out flying enemies if he can match their elevation. Ability 1: DRAGON'S DEFENSE (Right Mouse Button) Function: Enter a defensive stance to convert incoming damage into bonus health, then switch to YAT JEE CHUNG KUEN and gain damage reduction. Role: Survival tool and damage absorption. Strategy: Damage Soaker: Intentionally soak up oncoming projectiles and attacks to gather more bonus health. Survival Effort: Pop the block primarily when low on health or being focused. Parry: Time the block to specifically defend against stuns or one-shot projectiles. Ability 2: K'UN-LUN KICK (SHIFT) Function: Dash forward and perform two kicks, the second one dealing more damage to enemies below 50% HP. Role: Mobility, escape, gap closer, and low-health execution. Strategy: Escape Tool: Dash out of fights towards your team or a health pack when low on health.

Role: Mobility, escape, gap closer, and low-health execution. Strategy: Escape Tool: Dash out of fights towards your team or a health pack when low on health. Execution: Deals over 100 damage if both kicks connect against an enemy below half-health. This allows you to diminish a large portion of that health pool with a single use of an ability. Closing Distance: Dash toward enemies that are at distance to pursue them out of their positioning. Coverage: Carry momentum after the dash to cover more distance and rejoin fights faster. Ability 3: HARMONY RECOVERY (E) Function: Enter an idle state to recover missing health. Gain bonus health from overhealing. Role: Self-preservation and health recovery. Strategy: Opening Fights: Grants up to 100 bonus health, decaying after 2s at a rate of 15 HP/s. Use this boost of health to gain leverage when opening up fights. Stalling: If used while airborne, you will stay hovering in the air until the ability ends. This allows you to stall out opponents with low vertical mobility. Safe Recovery: Very vulnerable while active; try to only use the ability in a safe spot it will be hard for enemies to catch up to you. Block Opportunity: Time an opponent's attack and cancel the ability early with DRAGON'S DEFENSE to get free bonus health off the bat. Ability 4: CRANE LEAP (SPACE) Function: Perform up to three additional jumps while airborne. Role: Mobility. Strategy: Gaining Elevation: Simple, but effective for scaling heights easier compared to other characters. Nimble Movement: Well-timed, consecutive jumps with strafing movement make you harder to hit when approaching an enemy. Feints: Jump backward when pursuing a target with YAT JEE CHUNG KUEN to feint out close range abilities that may knock back or provide solid defense to the target. Ultimate Ability: LIVING CHI (Q) Function: Strike with an enhanced YAT JEE CHUNG KUEN , gaining increased damage, movement speed, attack range, and a reduced cooldown for DRAGON'S DEFENSE . Role: Team disorientation, stalling, and raw damage output.

His first appearance as Iron Fist was a cameo in " Timeless " (2021) #1 in December 2021, followed by his first full appearance as the lead character in " Iron Fist " (2022) #1 in February 2022 Lin Lie is the current Iron Fist in the Earth-616 universe and the successor to Danny Rand , who had given up the Iron Fist to save the dragons of the Heavenly Cities. Danny is later killed by the Ch'i-Lin, a mystical beast who seeks to kill every Iron Fist, but was resurrected as the Ghost Fist. When equipped with his Lion's Gaze legendary skin and its corresponding Ultimate VFX, Iron Fist replaces his standard line with "Gōng xǐ fā cái!" (恭喜发财). This is a traditional Chinese New Year greeting that translates to "Wishing you prosperity and wealth". TEAM-UP BONUS - 5% Damage Boost Strategy [ ] Iron Man is a high-flying, high-damage artillery cannon who can easily rain down punishment on his enemies from above. His free flight allows him to easily take any position to start blasting away at enemies, and both his Repulsor Blast and Unibeam can punch heavy holes into any foe. Ironically, despite being called "the Invincible Iron Man", his survivability is quite low, sporting only 250 health and a lack of reactionary defensive tools. As such, it may be tempting to use his free-flight to go as high up in the air as possible to get a sizeable vantage as well as providing the illusion of safety. However, you should avoid doing this whenever possible, as so long as the enemy has a competent ranged character such as Hawkeye , Hela , or The Punisher , or even just a decently-skilled Spider-Man or Iron Fist , you can be easily shot down before you can get any value. Instead, play around cover or near teammates, peeking your head out to deal chip damage and forcing the enemy to come to you from inconvenient routes in order to deal with you. This also gives you ample time to make an escape if you think a fight has gone awry or to fall back to teammates when you need support. While at a distance of 25 meters or more, you will typically use Repulsor Blast to get damage in on enemies, though it's also a solid choice on any up-close target for good burst on direct hit. Its sizeable AoE also makes it a decent finisher on injured enemies or to hit enemies hiding behind cover. His secondary fire, Unibeam, deals a hefty stream of damage to whoever it hits, making it great for melting down a priority target. While in Armor Overdrive, the damage on it is amped up by around 50%, making it even more potent.

His secondary fire, Unibeam, deals a hefty stream of damage to whoever it hits, making it great for melting down a priority target. While in Armor Overdrive, the damage on it is amped up by around 50%, making it even more potent. Try to prioritize tanks or lone squishies with this ability, as the former's large hitboxes means that it will be quite difficult for them to avoid the attack while it quickly melts through their large health pool, and the latter will have very little time to react before being killed. Micro-Missile Barrage fires a volley of rockets in front of Iron Man, but can only be used while Armor Overdrive or Hyper-Velocity is active. Typically, it is best used as an engagement tool right before exiting Hyper-Velocity to start a fight with a bit of chip damage or as a way to start Armor Overdrive. Armor Overdrive has Iron Man enter a temporary buffed state. In this form, Iron Man's Repulsor Blast and Unibeam get a significant damage boost for roughly 10 seconds. This ability is best used right before entering a fight to surprise enemies with high firepower, though be wary of its timer, as once it ends, it will force Iron Man into a brief power-down animation regardless of what he is doing, rendering him unable to do anything for a brief moment. As an added bonus, any eliminations he earns during Armor Overdrive will grant him an additional two seconds in that state, allowing him to keep the streak going. Iron Man does not need to get the final hit to increase Armor Overdrive's duration on elimination, simply being given credit for said elimination is enough. As such, firing into an injured crowd can be an easy way to secure a refresh on Armor Overdrive's duration, as you will get said benefit so long as even one enemy ends up eliminated. With the refresh in mind, Armor Overdrive is one of the most powerful snowball abilities in the game, as all it takes is one well-timed use to eliminate a key target and then leisurely take your time blasting enemies away. Focus on playing a safe neutral around cover, chipping away at enemies and waiting for an opportunity to take them by surprise with the Overdrive and secure a fight.

Focus on playing a safe neutral around cover, chipping away at enemies and waiting for an opportunity to take them by surprise with the Overdrive and secure a fight. Alternatively, you can also flank or take an off-angle to get a good vantage on key targets such as Strategists or other lone squishies, which can then snowball into the rest of their team as well. Be warned with this latter tactic, however, as both the Overdrive and your Hyper-Velocity flight have extremely loud and distinct sound cues, so experienced players can be easily alerted to you if you rush in haphazardly. Hyper-Velocity is Iron Man's main tool for traversing the map while also serving as his means of escape. Typically, you will use this to return to a fight from spawn or to quickly reach solid vantage points, but be wary of its resource meter, as if you are caught in the open without it available, you will be in big trouble. Note that activating Armor Overdrive will instantly refill the resource meter of Hyper-Velocity, so if needed, you can pop this to instantly give yourself the boost you need to escape or after making it to a fight to instantly refresh yourself while engaging the fight in your strongest form. Iron Man's Ultimate, Invincible Pulse Cannon, has Iron Man fire a devastating blast from his experimental pulse cannon after a brief charge-up. This is an incredible tool for wiping out a clustered herd of enemies or as a way to reliably pick off a priority target before a fight starts. Because a majority of this attack's damage comes from its area-of-effect explosion, this Ultimate is best activated from a vantage point above the enemies where the blast is guaranteed to go off and is more likely to hit a group of enemies. Try to use your free-flight and Hyper-Velocity to reach unexpected angles and give your enemies as little time to react as possible before the pulse lands. Since this attack deals flat burst damage, not sustained, it is one of the few attacks in the game capable of breaking through powerful healing Ultimates such as Mantis ' and Luna Snow 's, making him a potent counter to both of those characters. Appearance [ ] Iron Man's appearance is defined by his sleek, high-tech armor, primarily in a glossy red with gold accents.

Appearance [ ] Iron Man's appearance is defined by his sleek, high-tech armor, primarily in a glossy red with gold accents. The suit is designed to be both stylish and functional, with a smooth, aerodynamic shape that allows for agility in battle and flight. At the center of his chest sits the glowing arc reactor, a powerful energy source that lights up his suit and keeps him alive. His helmet is equally iconic, with a reflective surface and glowing eyes, often in white or blue, and a retractable mouthpiece. The suit’s arms and legs are articulated for movement, equipped with repulsor beams for offense and flight thrusters in the boots. The overall look combines futuristic engineering with elegance, showcasing Tony Stark's genius and style. As Iron Man’s character evolves, so does his armor, with each iteration becoming more advanced and visually striking, reflecting his personal growth and technological prowess. Iron Man The billionaire and playboy Tony Stark, is a clever and charming genius noted for his quick wit, bravado, arrogance and larger-than-life demeanor. He's a natural showman who loves at the spotlight, frequently employing humor and sarcasm as both a coping strategy and a means of charming others around him. Despite his often arrogant and cocky personality, Tony is a highly intelligent man driven by a tireless ambition to create and push the limits of technology, business, weaponry, and engineering with his “get-things-done” attitude as the CEO of Stark Unlimited . He is always confident and sometimes to the point of arrogance, does not hesitate to display his wealth or brilliance. Tony is always known for his witty and sarcastic personality, which is a signature part of his character. One of his habits is giving other heroes nicknames like Thor being "Goldilocks" and Luna Snow being "K-pop". What makes him a well-known genius is his bright mind and creativity, making him an ultimate visionary who is constantly thinking ahead following the footsteps of his father, Howard Stark . Growing up in his shadow, he absorbed feelings of admiration and inadequacy, realizing that the world already perceived him as "worse" than his father.

Growing up in his shadow, he absorbed feelings of admiration and inadequacy, realizing that the world already perceived him as "worse" than his father. Which resulted in a lifetime conflict between confidence and insecurity: Tony thinks he is a genius, yet he continually compares his worth to unreachable standards. That duality feeds both his ambition and his moments of self-doubt, transforming him into a truly human hero despite his technological and cerebral dominance. Stark views technology as both an extension of himself and a method to make sense of the world. His brilliance, however, comes with restlessness which he is never satisfied with the status quo and is constantly looking for the next breakthrough, even if it means pushing ethical or personal boundaries. This relentless desire for development makes him a visionary, but he is also a man who is constantly at odds with his own goals. He dislikes being told what to do and generally prefers to work alone, relying on his own judgment and abilities. This can often sometimes to conflicts with others he work with, particularly when their principles do not align. As a leader and Avenger , Tony represents both inspiration and conflict, often acts as the visionary and problem solver. His relationship with other heroes is complex, respect and multifaceted as he is. Like Captain America , as they started with deep mutual respect, but often marred by ideological battles. With Mister Fantastic , who have a relationship based on mutual respect and intellectual competitiveness as both are among the best minds on the planet, although their philosophies frequently disagree. Reed approaches research with moral restraint and a commitment to discovery for the greater good, whereas Tony is more pragmatic and risk-tolerant, occasionally stretching ethical bounds. And in terms with his relationship with Emma Frost , romantically or personally, they fully trust in one another and it is intense but complicated. Their relationship represents the merger of two restored pragmatists who have walked rough paths yet continue to strive for good. Their bond is equal parts passion and strategy, love and defiance. Overall, Stark's ego masks his vulnerability, uncertainty, and debilitating self-destructive attitude, which derive mostly from his convoluted history and the weight of massive responsibilities. He is haunted by the consequences of his own innovations and mistakes, which motivates him to protect others.

Despite his occasionally rough and prideful personality, Tony is deeply devoted to those he loves about and willing to sacrifice himself when it counts the most. He is willing to help to save the universe with the use of his genius-intellect skills as proof that Tony, along with Reed, is one of the geniuses who are currently working in the Timestream Reintegration Device , to fix the multiversal crisis. He is also the one who rebooted the original body of Ultron by himself so that the robot can assist the heroes during the battle in Krakoa . He approaches challenges with a mix of creativity and boldness, frequently improvising under pressure when traditional ways fail. He is both pragmatic and idealistic, willing to take calculated risks to save lives while remaining mindful of the human and emotional consequences of his decisions. Above all, Tony's personality is defined by a combination of intelligence, wit, moral thought, and a never-ending fight to live up to both his father's legacy and his own vision of who he wants to become as the Invincible Iron Man. Official description Jeff the Land Shark is a Strategist hero in Marvel Rivals , and is the 23rd hero introduced to the game's roster. He currently has three team-up abilities: Planet X Pals — with Groot and Rocket Raccoon Symbiote Shenanigans — with Venom and Hela Mr. Pool's Interdimensional Toy Box — with Deadpool and Elsa Bloodstone Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Strengths 1.2 Weaknesses 2 Costumes 3 Abilities 4 Strategy 5 Personality 6 Achievements 7 Proficiency 7.1 Challenges 7.2 Rewards 8 Gallery 9 Trivia 10 Navigation Overview [ ] Strengths [ ] Versatile support with high healing output for both single target and area-of-effect healing while also boasting high mobility; a simple-to-use kit that makes him fit in any team composition. His passive, Oblivious Cuteness, gives him 50% damage reduction against critical hits. His primary fire, Joyful Splash is a continuous long-range stream of water that heals allies and damage enemies. This ability has infinite range and can hit multiple allies that are in its path. His secondary fire, Aqua Burst, is a projectile that deals damage in a radius, being effective to hit multiple enemies clustered together. Direct hits will knock enemies backwards slightly.

His secondary fire, Aqua Burst, is a projectile that deals damage in a radius, being effective to hit multiple enemies clustered together. Direct hits will knock enemies backwards slightly. Healing Bubble is a spherical projectile that travels in an arc, providing healing-over-time to allies in a small area around its radius. This ability can be shot from long distances, and will bounce once when hitting walls or ceilings, allowing Jeff's healing to reach allies out of his line of sight. The bubbles persist on the map for 180 seconds until picked up, even if Jeff is KO'ed. Up to three bubbles can be placed on the map at once. This allows the bubbles to be placed strategically around the map, especially near objectives and choke points, and serve as on-demand "healing packs" for the allied team. This ability also provides a 15% healing bonus from all sources, and 60% increased movement speed for 4 seconds when hitting allies. Hide and Seek is a mobility tool that has Jeff diving underground, with only his fin exposed, vastly decreasing the size of his hurtbox. While submerged, Jeff gains 60% increased movement speed, self healing-over-time, immunity to all forms of crowd control, and can climb walls. This extra speed stacks with the bonus from Healing Bubble His Ultimate, It's Jeff!, allows him to swallow both enemies and allies in a massive radius. While inside Jeff, enemies take damage-over-time while allies heal-over-time. When first activated, Jeff vanishes from the battlefield and the player has 6 seconds to choose where he will attack. The area from where Jeff disappears from creates a large pool of healing water that lasts for 8 seconds and affects any allies who step on it. After eating the enemies and/or allies, Jeff is put in his Hide and Seek, and can move around for 6 seconds. After this duration has passed, he'll automatically spit anyone he swallowed. Players can manually spit enemies and allies earlier and separately with different inputs. Overhealing is converted into temporary bonus health for allies eaten. If Jeff falls off a ledge before spitting out, both him and anyone he swallowed will also be taken down.

If Jeff falls off a ledge before spitting out, both him and anyone he swallowed will also be taken down. This ability grants Jeff one of the most powerful crowd-controls in the game, and allows him to single-handedly change the course of matches when capturing objectives. When paired with Groot , Jeff gains access to New Friends, allowing him to hop on Groot's shoulders, granting him 35% damage reduction from all sources. When paired with Venom , Jeff gains access to Guardian of the Deep, where he links himself with nearby allies, granting them healing-over-time for 3 seconds. After the ability's duration is over, linked allies receive a one-time burst of healing. Overhealing is converted into temporary bonus health, up to 100 extra health. This ability can be activated during Hide and Seek. Weaknesses [ ] While Jeff's passive decreases his damage taken from headshots, he has a very large hurtbox, especially his head, which makes it easy to deal critical hits to him. Additionally, even with the damage reduction he can still be easily taken down by enemies with high burst damage, such as Hawkeye and Hela . Despite his high healing output, Jeff can struggle to heal when the team spreads out. Joyful Splash can be difficult to aim at heroes with high mobility such as Spider-Man and Venom . Joyful Splash's piercing effect doesn't apply when damaging enemies. The ability cannot deal critical hits. Aqua Burst cannot deal critical hits, and has limited uses, with only 3 charges that refill over 3 seconds each. Hide and Seek has a limited duration based on its energy cost, meaning Jeff cannot remain submerged indefinitely. In addition, Jeff cannot capture objectives while in Hide and Seek. Jeff can put himself in dangerous situations if he misses his Ultimate, allowing the enemy team to retaliate. Peni Parker can directly counter Jeff's Ultimate directly if he uses it while inside the area of her Bionic Spider-Nest, which will result in all the nearby Arachno Mines swarming Jeff, likely taking him out. Magneto and Iron Man can preemptively fire their Ultimates after Jeff reemerges.

Magneto and Iron Man can preemptively fire their Ultimates after Jeff reemerges. Abilities that provide invulnerability and/or immunity to crowd control can completely negate Jeff's Ultimate, such as Cloak 's Dark Teleportation, Punisher 's Culling Turret and Final Judgement, Star-Lord 's Stellar Shift, among others. Hopping on Groot 's shoulders can leave Jeff vulnerable, as Groot usually fights in the frontlines. Even with the damage reduction, he can still be focused and taken down easily, or be plucked off Groot with crowd control abilities such as stuns (e.g. Mantis ' Spore Slumber) or knockbacks (e.g. Invisible Woman 's Force Physics). The team-up with Venom doesn't provide healing to Jeff himself, only to the linked allies. In addition, the healing will be cancelled if allies move 10 meters away from Jeff. [enthusiastic] Jeff the Land Shark Jeffrey, an adorable little land shark, behaves like a playful pet. Despite being a shark, he resembles a puppy rather than a predator, happily waddling around and using his canine-like legs and tail. He is curious, friendly, mischievous, lovely, and extremely loyal to his human (and superhuman) buddies. Jeff engages in unpredictable companion animal behavior such as hugging, gnawing on things he shouldn't, and jumping into danger without thinking, but in a hilariously sharky way.  Jeff's personality is pure as he doesn't speak a lot, but can communicate in small words (like "Yeah!"). His expressive motions and big, puppy eyes frequently convey more than words. His actions, such as grabbing food, jumping around and going on adventures, demonstrate a humorous mind that elevates him above a simple mascot character. One of Jeff's most distinctive characteristics is his unquenchable hunger. He will devour almost anything, from whole hamburgers to literal Pym particles, which can lead him into trouble. Despite his ridiculous antics, Jeff is a trustworthy and loving creature who will put his own needs aside to aid and protect his friends. He is a valuable fighting companion with a strong sense of heroism. In addition, there are times that he disguises himself in order to blend in, he has a variety of costumes, including an incognito dolphin costume, to avoid frightening people while he swims. His blend of cuteness, loyalty, and innocent mischief makes him an all-around favorite among some of the Marvel characters he meets. He was raised and cared by young heroes such as Gwenpool and Kate Bishop . Most of the Rivals cast finds him adorable, such as Luna Snow , Star-Lord , Squirrel Girl , Peni Parker , Black Cat and even Hulk . Even the White Queen, Emma Frost , is protective, loving, and embraces Jeff as if he is her son. Overall, Jeff the Landshark exemplifies an ideal blend of chaos, cunning, and cuteness, making him one of the most wholesome characters in the cast.

He currently has one team-up ability: Vibrant Vitality — with Mantis and Groot Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Strengths 1.2 Weaknesses 2 Costumes 3 Abilities 4 Strategy 5 Personality 6 Achievements 7 Proficiency 7.1 Challenges 7.2 Rewards 8 Gallery 9 Trivia 10 Refences 11 Navigation Overview [ ] Strengths [ ] Elusive and deceptive Strategist capable of conjuring illusions of himself to distract enemies while healing his allies. Loki's core gameplay revolves around his Doppelganger ability, which allows the player to project illusions of Loki in the targeted area. This ability has two charges, and up to two illusions can be placed at once. The illusions are stationary and last for 60 seconds upon creation. Each illusion will mimic Loki's primary fire, aiming at the same location as him, which vastly increases his damage and healing output. The illusions share equal attributes to Loki, having the same health, as well as dealing the same damage and healing. His primary fire, Mystical Missile, shoots an energy projectile that deals damage to enemies and heals allies. Loki can simultaneously heal and deal damage if his allies and enemies are very close to each other since Mystical Missile creates a small spell field on impact. His secondary fire, Deception, creates an illusion where Loki is standing while granting him invisibility. While invisible, Loki gains heal-over-time. Loki can remain invisible indefinitely until attacking. Reloading, using Devious Exchange, or creating a Doppelganger will not break his invisibility. Loki's melee, Backstab, has him pulling a knife and performing a quick thrust. It is unique as it'll deal extra damage if he hits an enemy from behind. Devious Exchange allows Loki to swap places with any of the illusions of his choice within range. This ability makes Loki incredibly slippery and hard to pin down if properly used.

Regeneration Domain conjures a rune stone in the air that creates a magical field around Loki and his illusions that provides high healing-per-second in a radius around them. The magical field also converts 30% of all damage taken into direct healing to allies. This ability is incredibly powerful and can provide clutch healing against very powerful attacks, including Ultimates. His Ultimate, God of Mischief, allows Loki to transform into any hero in the match, either ally or enemy, for 15 seconds. When Loki transforms into a hero from the enemy team, his nametag and team color will change to the opposite player and team. If the Loki player attacks this reverses back to the player's actual name and team color. While shapeshifted, Loki gains access to all the targeted hero abilities, including their Ultimate, which will be at 100% charge. Activating an Ultimate while shapeshifted gives Loki an additional 7 seconds of transformation. This duration can be extended if transforming into the Winter Soldier and repeatedly getting resets on his Kraken Impact. Weaknesses [ ] Requires high skill to play efficiently. Has low healing output if his illusions and Regeneration Domain are not available. Very vulnerable if his Devious Exchange and Regeneration Domain is on cooldown. Mystical Missile cannot deal critical hit. Backstab has a low range and is very situational. Enemy heroes can destroy Loki's illusions and the runes from his Regeneration Domain. This makes characters with high area-of-effect damage such as Iron Man effective against Loki. In addition, many opponents can take advantage of Loki's illusions for their own benefit: Captain America can build-up stacks of his Sentinel Strike to fire his shield by attacking the illusions. Elsa Bloodstone can increase her Inherited Instinct passive by attacking illusions (eliminating them, on the other hand, does not grant her additional instinct). Mantis can deal critical hits to the illusions to regain charges of Life Orbs. Mister Fantastic can build-up Elastic Strength stacks to enter his inflated state by attacking the illusions.

Phoenix can quickly land hits to apply Sparks and quickly enact her explosions for area damage. Rogue can use her Ability Absorption on the illusions to gain Loki's Regeneration Domain for herself. Squirrel Girl can shoot the illusions with Burst Acorn to extended the reach of their explosions. Winter Soldier can reset his Kraken Impact by hitting and destroying illusions marked with the Culling debuff. Wolverine can build-up his Berserker Rage by attacking the illusions. His varied toolset and plethora of tricks makes him a highly adaptable hero that can support his team, deal solid damage, and keep himself alive all at the same time. Loki's lifeline is his illusions and his ability to manage them. They are important both to his general output and as his means of survival, so learning ability management and map knowledge to maximize its placements is crucial to his success.

Loki's lifeline is his illusions and his ability to manage them. They are important both to his general output and as his means of survival, so learning ability management and map knowledge to maximize its placements is crucial to his success. As such, it is not recommended to use him if you are a beginner, as worst case scenario, you could actually end up hurting your own team with poor illusion placement. Loki's primary attack is Mystical Missile, which has him fire a magic projectile from his scepter that will damage enemies and heal allies in a radius. Unlike other explosive projectiles, the projectile itself has no effect, with the healing and damage solely coming from its spell field, meaning that there is functionally no difference between landing a direct hit or barely hitting the target with the blast radius. The large AoE on this attack makes it excel with or against team comps that like to cluster close together, especially if you have other illusions up. However, it also makes it extremely hard for Loki to hit flying heroes such as Iron Man , Storm , or Human Torch , making him ineffective if those heroes are on the field. Regeneration Domain has Loki conjure a rune stone at his location that deals a large amount of healing as well as converting all damage received by an ally within the field into healing. The stone will remain on the field until its timer runs out or until it is destroyed by an enemy. This is essentially an immortality field, as any ally within the stone is incapable of taking any damage whatsoever. Timing this effectively can allow you to completely nullify any sort of damage that comes your way, giving Loki some of the best enemy denial potential in the game. However, its extremely long cooldown of 30 seconds means that using it haphazardly will be punished heavily, so always make sure to use it with discretion. Doppelganger is undoubtedly Loki's most important ability. Upon activation, Loki conjures an immobile clone of himself onto the field that aims at whatever he is aiming at, provided they both have line of sight to said target. He can have up to two clones active at any given time: if he attempt to conjure a third, the oldest clone will disappear. If a clone is on the field for 60 seconds it will disappear. Clones do not disappear if Loki dies.

He can have up to two clones active at any given time: if he attempt to conjure a third, the oldest clone will disappear. If a clone is on the field for 60 seconds it will disappear. Clones do not disappear if Loki dies. These clones function identically to Loki himself in terms of numbers, dealing the same damage and doling out the same amount of healing with their Mystical Missiles and Regeneration Domains as he does. With these, Loki can essentially double or even triple his field output, allowing him to heal faster, cover more ground with his domains, and deal surprisingly high burst damage to anyone he can land a hit on. The clones also excel at forcing enemies to split their attention between his team and his entities, similar to how Namor does the same with his Monstro Spawn. Enemies will have to choose between either shooting down the clones to cut Loki's output while leaving themselves open to the rest of his team, or ignore the clones and attempt to weather the storm, leaving Loki to his own devices. Be warned however, as while the clones are no doubt powerful, they can also be risky to use. While in most cases them getting targeted or destroyed is only a mild inconvenience, in these two circumstances, poor clone placement can easily become fatal: Moon Knight can easily target the immobile clones to get easy ricochets with his Crescent Darts and Moon Blades, almost functioning as a pseudo-ankh. This turns what would normally be something allies like to cluster around into a borderline death trap. Winter Soldier can refresh his Kraken Impact off of a destroyed clone, allowing him more opportunities to continue his rampage during his ultimate. Devious Exchange is an incredibly powerful escape tool. Loki will swap places with any illusion within 30 meters of him, even ones out of his line of sight. Because of this ability, it may be worthwhile at times to leave a clone behind so you can have an escape route ready to go if things go awry. It can also serve as a quick means of maneuverability if you need to find a better vantage quickly. Deception makes Loki even harder for enemies to keep track of him. Loki immediately goes invisible and leaves an illusion behind, while also bestowing healing over time to himself as long as he remains invisible. He can stay invisible as long as he wants, however doing any actions other than reloading, creating another illusion, or using Devious Exchange will reveal him. Taking any damage will also reveal him. Due to the invisibility ending if Loki takes damage, this ability isn't great as an on-demand escape tool as even after going invisible, enemies will likely still be able to hit you out of it if they were already firing at you. Instead, try to use it before you get targeted by an enemy or right after using Devious Exchange in order to give enemies as little time to react to your invisibility as possible, giving you more opportunity to escape. Although you can theoretically stay invisible as long as you want, you should not stay in this mode for an extended period of time, as if you're invisible, that means you aren't healing the team or damaging the enemy, significantly hurting your team's overall output. Find the quickest opportunity to safely exit invisibility so you can get back to helping your team ASAP. God of Mischief is perhaps the most unorthodox ultimate in the game. Loki can take the form of any hero on the field, from either his team or the enemy's. Upon transformation, their ultimate will automatically be available to him. He can stay in this form for 12 seconds or however long his copied target's ultimate lasts should it also have some sort of timer. With this ultimate, Loki has two choices he can make. He can either copy a Duelist or Vanguard so he can get into the enemy and cause chaos with one of their ultimates, or copy a Strategist so he can use one of their ultimates to sustain his team.

Both options can be extremely powerful, especially to confuse any enemies attempting to keep track of ultimates, though be wary when using the former, as if you're transformed into a Duelist or Vanguard, that means your team will be down a healer for however long your ultimate lasts. Also, be wary that you do not get any sort of second chance if you get KO'd during your transformation, so don't rush in recklessly or attempt to transform while under fire. Personality [ ] https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Loki_-_Hero_Spawned_07.ogg Everyone loves a trickster — until the trick is played on them. Loki The god of mischief, Loki Laufeyson, is defined as a trickster who seeks order, a prince who desires recognition, and a god who fears being overlooked. He is clever, theatrical, and infinitely intelligent, wielding wit and trickery as both weapons and defenses.  Loki rarely acts without meaning, frequently concealing insecurity beneath sarcasm and mockery. His need to prove his worth to himself and others is what drives most of his instability. Loki is profoundly torn about his identity and belonging. He is defined by deception: he lies easily, bending the facts and manipulating people to achieve his goals, often merging charm, humor, and drama to make his falsehoods credible. Raised as an Asgardian prince but born a Frost Giant, he feels like an outsider even before he discovers the truth about his origins. This rift motivates his jealously of his brother Thor and contempt of Odin , not because he is without love, but because he never feels chosen . Loki's wickedness is generally motivated by wounded pride and the dread of being replaced.

Loki is also highly emotional despite his tries to look detached. He feels betrayal deeply and loves fiercely, even when he acts otherwise.  His relationships are complicated and volatile, particularly with Thor, alternating between antagonism, loyalty, and real affection.  He is portrayed as a villain not because he is entirely vile, but because his acts are motivated by wounded pride, fear of insignificance, and a frantic desire to exert control over a world that has always left him feeling helpless. He has always targeted Thor, Asgard , and Earth's heroes as symbols of everything he believes he has been denied as he wants to be Asgard's king. He usually targets his own brother Thor, manipulates Odin, and continually attacks Earth, frequently via surrogate villains or large-scale plots, because Thor is revered as a savior while Loki is discarded as a problem. His attacks on teams like the Avengers are motivated by anger for gods and heroes who are revered merely for being themselves. He can't face Thor, Hulk , or full teams like the Avengers head on, so he resorts to plans, bargains, and psychological warfare. Loki's relationships with his siblings are defined by jealousy, rivalry, and sometimes mutual respect, yet still, every connection represents a distinct wound in his soul. Thor genuinely loves Loki and believes there is good in him, often offering forgiveness long after it is deserved, while Loki envies Thor’s ease, strength, and favored status, mistaking that love for condescension rather than loyalty. Thor is everything Loki thinks he isn't: favored, trusted, and easily heroic. Loki's hate of Thor inspires numerous betrayals and attacks, but it is inextricably linked with true attachment. He continuously sabotages Thor, but he also saves him on numerous occasions, sometimes out of guilt, sometimes out of love that he refuses to acknowledge. Their bond is often fractured, yet it never completely breaks, making their battle tragic rather than hateful: two brothers bound by blood, history, and a love neither can express without pain.

Their bond is often fractured, yet it never completely breaks, making their battle tragic rather than hateful: two brothers bound by blood, history, and a love neither can express without pain. Loki and Hela 's relationship is one of separated siblings tied by blood but bonded solely by ambition: there is no trust or affection between them, only sharp awareness and mutual leverage. She quickly sees through Loki's plans, understanding that his desire for Asgard's throne drives everything he does, whereas Loki approaches her not out of loyalty, but because her power and legions make her indispensable.  Their relationship is simply transactional, with family serving as a convenience; each expects betrayal in due course, but is willing to cooperate in order to shape the future. And Angela is the sibling who most destabilizes Loki emotionally. She is not raised with Thor and questions Loki's view that family is characterized by hierarchy and partiality. While their connection is not particularly close, her presence strengthens Loki's belief that Odin's secrets and lies, not simply Thor's, shattered the family. Overall, Loki is a brilliant, conflicted trickster driven by insecurity as much as ambition, using lies and schemes to control a world that has made him feel small and replaceable. However, beneath his cruelty lies deep loneliness and a desperate need for recognition and belonging, and he frequently embraces the role of villain because it provides him with identity and power when love is uncertain. Loki, who is capable of empathy, growth, and even heroism, is never totally evil; instead, he is a self-aware contradiction, divided between growing better and submitting to the role the universe requires he play, particularly as the current king of Yggsgard. Luna Snow Seol Hee's early life, which she spent with her grandmother after losing her parents, instilled in her a strong sense of compassion and responsibility. Initially she pursued music to support her family. As Luna Snow she represents an interesting duality: on the one hand, she is a dazzling, captivating performer adored by fans; on the other, she is a brave, protective and a selfless hero facing serious dangers. This disparity does not divide her; it defines her. Her ability to blend her life in the spotlight with her heroic duty displays a strong, resolute character in the midst of trouble. She frequently speaks about her songs and concerts in the midst of fighting against her adversaries and even during the Timestream Entanglement . With Lin Lie , they respect each other’s skills and personalities as members of Agents of Atlas . With her relationship to other heroes, there are times that she appears to have a conceited attitude due to her status as a K-pop star, her incredible popularity and her powered capabilities with even Magneto describes her of being impertinent in their in-game interaction. Overall, Seol Hee is a performer and hero at heart, blending with grace, confidence, proud and compassion, with a strong sense of duty to her fans, the people and the world which she works constantly and is profoundly committed to bringing light and hope via her music and heroism.
