She currently has one team-up ability: Arcane Order — with Doctor Strange and Scarlet Witch Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Strengths 1.2 Weaknesses 2 Costumes 3 Abilities 4 Strategy 5 Personality 6 Achievements 7 Proficiency 7.1 Challenges 7.2 Rewards 8 Gallery 9 Trivia 10 Navigation 11 References Overview [ ] Strengths [ ] A sword-wielding skirmisher with great survivability, who excels at close-range combat, capable of getting in and out of fight using her Stepping Disc portals and Umbral Incursion. Has the highest melee range in the game due to her large sword hitbox. Her passive, Limbo's Might, converts 30% of all damage done into bonus health, up to a maximum of 150.

Has the highest melee range in the game due to her large sword hitbox. Her passive, Limbo's Might, converts 30% of all damage done into bonus health, up to a maximum of 150. This gives Magik amazing survivability as long as she continuously strikes at her enemies. Her primary fire, Soulsword, consists of slashes in a wide arc in front of her. Players can frame cancel the endlag animation of these attacks by using any of her other abilities. Her secondary fire, Magik Slash, is a charge-up attack that launches a projectile in a straight line. The damage increases based on charge time. Unlike most melee-oriented characters, Magik has a different attack for the dedicated melee bind, which is a short-range pummel with the hilt of the sword. This does not deal a lot of damage compared to her other attacks but it is very quick, and can be used to cancel her primary fire at any point during the swing. Melee can be used to quickly deal follow-up damage immediately after her sword swing connects. Umbral Incursion is a quick dash forward that covers a decent distance. Upon connection with an enemy, Magik will follow up with a rising slash that launches her opponents upwards. This ability gives Magik a lot of mobility and flexibility, as it can be used both offensively and defensively. Stepping Discs are Magik's main mobility and survivability tool. Magik is completely immune to damage while inside the portal, as well as briefly while entering and exiting them. This ability has two charges. Upon exiting a portal, she can execute two different attacks depending on the button input: By pressing primary fire, she executes Eldritch Whirl, a full 360° spin that deals reduced damage in a wide area around her. By pressing secondary fire, she uses Demon's Rage, which temporarily summons a small, stationary Limbo demon that repeatedly strikes the air in front of it. Her Ultimate, Darkchild, temporarily transforms Magik into her demonic form, which enhances all her abilities: Enemies hit by Soulsword will be hit by another two delayed slashes in addition to the initial slash. Magik Slash is faster, deals much higher damage, and has a shorter cooldown.

Her Ultimate, Darkchild, temporarily transforms Magik into her demonic form, which enhances all her abilities: Enemies hit by Soulsword will be hit by another two delayed slashes in addition to the initial slash. Magik Slash is faster, deals much higher damage, and has a shorter cooldown. Umbral Incursion is faster, covers more distance, deals more damage, and has a shorter cooldown. Stepping Discs's teleporting is faster and has a shorter cooldown. Eldritch Whirl deals two delayed slashes in addition to the initial slash and covers double the radius. Demon's Rage deals more damage and the demon has higher health. Weaknesses [ ] Magik is the only melee-oriented character whose normal attacks are affected by damage distance falloff. This means she needs to be very close to her opponents in order to maximize her damage. Her survivability is very conditional, as it depends on her dealing constant damage to trigger Limbo's Might and gain bonus health. Has no ranged attacks aside from Magik Slash, which has a cooldown. In a team with two vanguards, Magik is ideally utilised as a flanker to take out the backline of healers as quickly as possible. However, if there are less than two vanguards, Magik can also be used to fill this role, given her high mobility, AoE attacks, and passive bonus health boost. It's important to note that Magik's basic swing combo is extremely slow and ineffective. It is recommended to follow each swing with a melee jab entirely regardless of your situation, as this cancels the animation, allowing you a significantly higher damage output over time. In a scenario in which two tanks already exist on your team, Magik performs exceedingly well in targeting healers. It is generally best to flank the enemy team and attempt to reach their backline through alternative routes to prevent being noticed; however if this fails , ou can always use her Stepping Discs to grant brief invincibility, allowing you a moment to escape or reach the backline. Once there, use the Umbral Incursion dash ability to begin an extremely effective combo. If landed, the dash will launch the enemy Strategist into the air. While aloft, perform a basic attack quickly followed by a melee for the animation cancel, then another basic attack plus a second melee if necessary. This combo is enough to eliminate every Strategist, provided they are receiving no healing/have no buffs in general. Once completed, use the Stepping Discs to teleport away, ideally using the demon ability to provide cover and delay pursuit. This combo is extremely effective for shattering an enemy team's backline quickly. If there is one or no Vanguards in your team, Magik can be, though not preferably, used as a semi-tank. Her AoE ability after Stepping Discs allows you to jump into the center of a team and inflict damage in a huge radius, though this does leave you vulnerable afterwards. If undertaking this role, ensure there are at least one healer on you at all times. Magik's long-range attack has no fall-off damage and a relatively short wind-up time for the damage generated, making it especially useful for opening combos. Consider chaining a long-range attack into the dash-swing-melee combo mentioned before, as this is usually enough to kill any non-tank character (heals excluded).

Personality [ ] https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Magik_-_Setup_05.ogg I try to embrace what I've experienced. My strife has given me strength. Magik Illyana Rasputina, often known as Magik, has a layered personality shaped by her tragic background, which has left her with a harsh, frequently cynical, and distant, as well as a deep longing for forgiveness and connection. As a young girl, she was kidnapped into the hellish realm of Limbo by the demonic sorcerer Belasco, where she spent seven years struggling for survival and learning sorcery from both good and evil versions of her mentors. When she returned to Earth, only a few moments had elapsed, yet she was no longer a child, but a warrior with deep emotional scars. This made her cold, and often cynical leading to be fiercely independent and guarded. Her personality is also marked by a dark sense of humor and a cynical worldview with a sharp wit and a wicked sense of humor as she hides her fragility behind sarcasm. Magik can be tough and ruthless, but she also demonstrates profound devotion and a capacity for intense affection for her friends and comrades. She is a powerful sorceress and swordswoman who is pragmatic but can also be harsh, with a darker side that is developing and becoming more vulnerable. Magik typically projects herself as calm and detached. She rarely expresses her emotions openly and speaks in short, precise sentences, as if she is always thinking two steps ahead. This stems from years of survival in Limbo, where displaying fear or hesitancy resulted in death.

Magik typically projects herself as calm and detached. She rarely expresses her emotions openly and speaks in short, precise sentences, as if she is always thinking two steps ahead. This stems from years of survival in Limbo, where displaying fear or hesitancy resulted in death. Her time in Limbo taught her to rely only on herself, and that hard-won self-reliance manifests in her pragmatic and often cold demeanor. Beneath that exterior, Illyana is sympathetic and loyal to people she loves, but she fights to show it because she is terrified that her evil side, the Darkchild, would harm them. Recently knowing what happened to the New Mutants in her timeline during the Timestream Entanglement through their in-game dialogue with Matt Murdock , this version of Illyana must have felt a worst deal of sorrow, burden, and anguish, hinting she is from the Collapsing Timeline same with Daredevil. Despite her cold persona, Illyana is still fiercely loyal, protective, and compassionate to her loved ones and teammates like the X-Men , and fellow, now deceased New Mutants, like Sam Guthrie , Rahne Sinclair , and Dani Moonstar . Her older brother Piotr is arguably the person Illyana loves most. Colossus was her protector before her abduction into Limbo, and she has always looked up to him. Even after years in hell, when she emerged darker and more cynical, her love for Piotr never wavered. Though he is lost recently during the Entanglement, he still misses him a lot. Illyana simply does not express affection in typical ways. Instead of offering comfort, she'll give harsh advice or engage in a battle to help someone grow stronger. Her protectiveness often emerges as ruthlessness in the face of threats. She will go to terrifying lengths to defend mutants or friends, even if it means staining her soul in the process.

Additionally, Illyana's connection to Doctor Strange stems from their shared mastery of magic, and she is a student at his Sanctum . Strange has acted as both a mentor and an ally, recognizing her enormous potential and frightening instability.  He knows the responsibility of having great supernatural power and frequently serves as a moral counselor when she veers dangerously close to her demonic nature. Illyana is usually perceived as dangerous. Her link to Limbo and her alter ego, the Darkchild, allows her to lose control and reveal her evil half. When she becomes angry, her eyes glow, her horns emerge, and her voice takes on a supernatural tone, serving as a visual reminder that she is never totally human again. Even when she is peaceful, other mutants can sense her power: teleportation circles crackling around her feet, shadows flickering abnormally. The X-Men trust her, but they are wary of her; even her friends are unsure if the lady in front of them is Illyana the mutant or Magik, the demon queen. This tension between her light and dark sides gives her a haunting charisma: she is both the demon queen and the lost girl. He shines in defensive objectives. While he cannot fly, he can fall slowly after falling from high heights. His primary fire, Iron Volley, shoots relatively slow moving projectile blasts. There is a small delay in-between shots. These projectiles explode after traveling 25 meters, or upon impact, generating a spell field that deals damage in a small radius.

His primary fire, Iron Volley, shoots relatively slow moving projectile blasts. There is a small delay in-between shots. These projectiles explode after traveling 25 meters, or upon impact, generating a spell field that deals damage in a small radius. His secondary fire, Mag-Cannon, launches a projectile which damage scales on the iron rings on his back. The number of stacks (up to three) can be seen physically on the character but are also shown on screen by the arrow-shaped icon right below the aiming reticle. At max stacks, Mag-Cannon deals knockback to enemies. Magneto can shield his allies and himself using his electromagnetic fields with Metal Bulwark and Iron Bulwark, respectively. Shown as a purple bubble around the target, it expires after 2.5 seconds or after absorbing up to 200 damage. Metal Bulwark and Iron Bulwark are on different cooldowns, meaning Magneto can shield himself and an ally. All damage dealt while shielded converts into energy for Magneto's iron rings that fuel his Mag-Cannon. Metallic Curtain functions similarly to Doctor Strange 's Shield of the Seraphim, projects a magnetic field shield in front of him that absorbs all incoming projectiles while moving at a slower speed. The shield has no health, but is on a resource meter. This ability can even block certain Ultimates, such as the blasts shot by Hela 's Goddess of Death and Iron Man 's Invincible Pulse Cannon. His Ultimate, Meteor M, has Magneto floating up into the sky and charging-up a magnetic meteor that he can unleash upon will, to strike in a large radius. The damage of the meteor increases over-time before releasing. The true power of this Ultimate is when used defensively, as while channeling the meteor, a magnetic field around Magneto absorbs any enemy projectiles shot in his general direction, which adds extra damage for Meteor M. This allows Magneto to directly counter other Ultimates, such as Star-Lord 's Galactic Barrage. This Ultimate can potentially be devastating when combining the base damage with added damage from absorbed enemy projectiles. Weaknesses [ ] Limited mobility and unable to fly, despite having slow fall. Surprisingly frail if his shields are on cooldown. Unlike Doctor Strange, he can't hold his Metallic Curtain indefinitely.

This Ultimate can potentially be devastating when combining the base damage with added damage from absorbed enemy projectiles. Weaknesses [ ] Limited mobility and unable to fly, despite having slow fall. Surprisingly frail if his shields are on cooldown. Unlike Doctor Strange, he can't hold his Metallic Curtain indefinitely. If Magneto absorbs too many projectiles while charging Meteor M (displayed by a gauge when he casts), the Ultimate will be cancelled. The overloading is based on the number of projectiles, not their damage output. This means that certain attacks that fire multiple projectiles at once, such as The Punisher 's Deliverance shotgun, will absorb more projectiles than his Adjudication automatic rifle. His ult is useful in some situations, although it might be difficult to hit someone reliably except against specific DPS. To maximize the effectiveness of your shields, cycle through your defensive cooldowns before ulting.  Meteor M breaks at 100 absorption, so fire the projectile right before maxing out. Magneto Magneto's demeanor is described as vengeful, protective, resolute, unforgiving and aggressively assertive. He wants to protect mutantkind from mankind, and he doesn't care about the cost which often leads to him using violence to make political statements or force change. He was sculpted by a life filled with suffering, loss, and a never-ending pursuit of justice or vengeance, depending on one's perspective. Born as a young Jewish boy in Germany before World War II, Erik witnessed the horrors of the Holocaust, including his family's murders and the Nazi regime's inhuman violence. These early experiences instilled in him a fundamental distrust of human institutions and a conviction that authority must be utilized firmly to prevent oppression, no matter the cost which he is both sympathetic and terrifying because of his underlying trauma: he refuses to be victimized again. Erik belief system is built around a mutant supremacist philosophy. While this may be seen as extreme, it stems from a real fear that if mutants do not ascend above humans, they will be exterminated by them. He believes that peaceful coexistence is impossible not because mutants are inferior, but because of human nature, which he perceives as fundamentally afraid and hostile toward the unknown. He believes in strong, forceful leadership and frequently rejects democracy and diplomacy as ineffectual. His charisma and eloquence entice others to join his cause, but his pride and strong ideology frequently lead to conflict with both allies and foes, which is why the Brotherhood exists battling against the X-Men . More of Erik's background, him and Charles Xavier had a long and complex friendship. They've known each other since before the X-Men or the Brotherhood existed, and their true relationship stems from their shared experiences as visionaries, outcasts, and leaders. They've fought, taught, and worked together to make the world a better place at various points in time. But their friendship is tragic as they care for each other, yet their fundamental ideological differences and worldviews almost invariably separate them.

In addition, the tragic events of Genosha reinforced Erik's greatest worries that mankind would never allow mutantkind to prosper, while also breaking him emotionally and ideologically. He vowed since that horrifying day, he would fiercely protect and lead mutantkind till his death. When the Krakoa era begins, he becomes one of the leaders of the Quiet Council alongside Xavier, Ororo and Emma , where Erik evolves. He welcomed Krakoa not as a military state, but as a sovereign nation founded on ethnic unity, diplomacy, and a single cause, demonstrating his role as a statesman rather than a conqueror.  He also meets with other heroes in a less hostile way, such as Captain America , who recalls the events of WWII and how he saw Steve when he was younger. Magneto's children, Wanda , Pietro , and Lorna , reflect his complex background, divided between villainy and heroism, love and ideology, family and freedom. With Wanda's relationship with his father, it is intensely emotional, marred by disappointment, longing, and ideological struggle because she was formerly a member of the Brotherhood and rejected his extremist views, becoming a long-standing Avenger and often struggling with her identity. Despite the fact that they have not been close in recent events, Erik still cared for her. Despite his typical haughtiness, which stems from his arrogance, he does occasionally show a more amusing side. One proof is his offer of Wolverine and Colossus ' Fastball Special...  if only because he is the only one capable of throwing both of them simultaneously. During this time, Magneto attempted to create a better future, even giving his life to protect mutantkind and Krakoa's survival, such as Ultron 's attack at the Hellfire Gala . His morals became more firm, unbending, and protective of the Homo superior at any costs, although it was led by purpose rather than revenge. Magneto is voiced by James Arnold Taylor , reprising his role from other Marvel video games such as Marvel Avengers: Battle for Earth (2012), Marvel Heroes (2013), and Marvel Powers United VR (2018). Taylor is also known for his work in the Ratchet & Clank video game series, voicing the eponymous Ratchet from the second game, Ratchet & Clank: Going Commando (2003), and in all subsequent entries to date. Another role that Taylor is known for is the voice of Obi-Wan Kenobi in the Star Wars franchise, most notably being the voice for him in the Clone Wars series. This is slightly referenced whenever the player says Hello as Magneto, the line being "Hello There.", a phrase Obi-Wan Kenobi used in Star Wars: Episode 3 - Revenge of the Sith (2005). Magneto's magnetic great sword is a possible reference to the Cerebro Sword. In the comics, this sword was created by Magneto from the destroyed Cerebro device that Charles Xavier was wearing when he died as a reminder of what the mutant nation of Krakoa is facing. Magneto's signature is written in Krakoan language. Magneto's cape and belt in his default costume has a letter M in Krakoan language. His Ultimate ability, Meteor M, might be a reference to Asteroid M. This is Magneto's orbital base of operations in a hollowed-out asteroid in the comics. Magneto's Autumn statue can be found at the Grove . Magneto's pose in the X spray is a reference to his similar pose in Jim Lee's comic cover in " X-Men" Vol. 2 (1991) #1 . Mantis core gameplay revolves around her Life Orb mechanic, which fuels her heals and buffs. She has access to a maximum of 4 Life Orbs with one being regenerated every 3 seconds. Spore Slumber has Mantis lobbing a projectile that explodes in a AOE, putting one opponent caught within to sleep. It deals 10 damage and creates an illusion behind her target that can be shot by the enemy team to wake the target up. Enemies hit by the ability will be stunned for 3.5 seconds, or until they take damage. Enemies will not wake up if they take damage for the first .5 seconds of the stun. This allows Mantis to shoot once immediately after using the ability without waking the opponent up. Spore Slumber is a very versatile ability to help secure takedowns on key targets, or as a defensive measure against diving opponents. It is often useful to wait for your team and collectively damage the stunned opponent at the same time. This is a great way to secure a kill when they have more health than Mantis alone can deal with. Her Ultimate, Soul Resurgence, has Mantis enveloped by an aura that provides healing-over-time and increased movement speed. This ability lasts for 8 seconds and affects all allies within the radius around her, as well as Mantis herself. In addition, she also heals all allies in range of the ability for 200 health upon use. If her allies are at full health, 70% of the excess healing is converted into bonus health until the Ultimate is over. The over-healing can only give each player up to 100 extra health. Mantis also benefits from the speed boost, healing and over-health, making her much harder to take down. This is the second most powerful healing ability in the game (after Luna Snow 's Fate of Both Worlds), being clutch in moments where the team is getting bombarded by enemy fire.

Mantis Mantis' personality mostly appears via the central core of radical empathy. Because her ability allows her to physically perceive the internal states of others, her personality is less about a distinct "ego" and more about being a sensitive conduit for the room's energy. Mantis is an intriguing combination of tranquility, emotional intelligence, and underlying intensity. She frequently comes across as peaceful, almost otherworldly, because she feels emotions differently than most people. As an empath, she not only understands but also physically senses and absorbs emotions. This makes her extremely attentive in social circumstances, but also somewhat distant, because she sees emotions as something to be observed rather than truly owned. Her words and actions can come out as slow speaking, shy, awkward or even a bit severe, not because she is rude, but because she lacks the filters that most people employ to soften the reality. Her lack of traditional social upbringing means she is unaware of the "polite lies" that humans use to negotiate relationships. When she feels a secret, she often spills it, not out of malice, but because emotions are the most visible facts in the world to her. Mantis is genuinely loving and gentle. She sincerely wants peace and harmony, and she frequently serves as a mediator or emotional anchor in a group setting. Since joining the Guardians of the Galaxy , she serves a subtle but important role, grounding more hot-headed characters like Rocket and assisting others in confronting their inner difficulties. Her generosity, however, is not a sign of weakness; rather, it stems from a deep emotional strength. Because she understands suffering so well, she can tolerate it better than most and even utilize it to help others heal. She can also cause sleep by using her empathic abilities to overwhelm a person's psyche with deep relaxation and calm. Because she experiences emotions so strongly and immediately, she is drawn to relieving pain, resolving conflict, and restoring emotional balance. The same sensitivity that makes her kind, uncomfortable, and sensitive allows her to "quiet" others by overwhelming them with calm.

His passive, Elastic Strength, builds-up his special Elasticity gauge, which when filled grants him an inflated state for 6 seconds, empowering him. The damage of his primary fire increases and it now deals damage in a small area. He max health is doubled while inflated, and he receives a one-time heal equal to his normal max health. His movement speed is increased by 20%. Elasticity stacks are gained each time Mister Fantastic lands any offensive abilities, up to 100 stacks. Players can prematurely cancel the inflated state manually. His primary fire, Stretch Punch, elongates his arm to deal damage from a distance. This attack can hit multiple enemies at once if the player quickly moves their aim around. It cannot hit the same enemy twice this way. His secondary fire, Distended Grip, stretches one of his arms to grip an enemy. Pressing the primary fire on the same target makes Mister Fantastic throw his other arm to pull the target towards him. This ability grants 30 Elasticity even if an enemy is not hit. If there is another enemy nearby, the player can target them after gripping the first enemy, which will result in Mister Fantastic yanking both enemies into each other, knocking them up and dealing damage. Distended Grip can be used to cancel the endlag of Stretch Punch, increasing its damage-per-second potential. Flexible Elongation causes Mister Fantastic to grab a target and dash towards them while gaining 75 bonus health. This ability grants 20 Elasticity and has two charges. It can be used on either enemies or allies. If used against enemies, it deals damage, inflicts slow, and knocks back those nearby on impact. If used on allies, it also grants the target 75 bonus health. Reflexive Rubber temporarily stretches Mister Fantastic into a larger form for 3 seconds, whereupon he becomes a shield that can absorb up to 300 damage. Any attacks directed at him will be absorbed and later redirected back as a small projectile. Can be canceled prematurely by reactivating the ability. The redirected damage is equal to 60% of all absorbed damage. Mister Fantastic also becomes immune to all forms of crowd control.

After leaping at least three times, he can leap one additional time whenever he hits an enemy, up to a total of six leaps. Each leap increases the damage of the next leap by 10, up to 50 extra damage. Each leap adds a stacking slow of 10% to enemies hit, up to 60% reduced movement speed. Using this ability on areas with a low ceiling will cause Mister Fantastic to bounce faster. When paired with Rocket Raccoon , Mister Fantastic gains access to Fantastic Amplifier, which when activated allows him to temporarily exceed his Elasticity limit and manually enter his inflated state. Very small uptime and relatively long endlag between his abilities. COOLDOWN - 25s DURATION - 10s ENERGY CONSUMED DURING INFLATED STATE - 16.67/s Strategy [ ] Mister Fantastic is an unorthodox Duelist who sacrifices some raw damage output for incredible sustainability, almost functioning as a pseudo-Vanguard. His significantly higher health, ability to grant himself overhealth, and his ability to absorb damage altogether with Reflexive Rubber allows him to stay in the fight for extended periods of time, all while providing valuable backup to his team by either granting them overhealth or slowing any enemies who attempt to dive them. Still, while Mister Fantastic can help to replicate the job of a Vanguard, he does not have to tools to replace one altogether. Mister Fantastic usually wants to play around his team's frontline or as a bodyguard for his backline, bolstering his team's Vanguards and Strategists while also shooing away any dive characters who attempt to harass the backline with his plethora of slows, seizes, and large AoE attacks. Mister Fantastic's main attack is his Stretch Punch, which has him throw a far-reaching punch with a wide AoE. While its raw damage output may be low, its ability to hit multiple targets in one go makes it an exceptional crowd-control tool, letting you hit clustered groups of enemies and farm ultimate charge very quickly. While in his Inflated State, this attack's damage increases significantly. Despite being melee, this attack cannot bypass barriers from heroes such as Doctor Strange or Magneto . The AoE on this attack actually lingers for a significant amount of time, allowing you to still hit enemies even late in its animation. With that in mind, you can often sweep the attack around a large area and still be able to hit most targets, no matter how evasive they may be, making you a great answer to mobile dive heroes such as Spider-Man or Black Panther . Reflexive Rubber is what allows Mister Fantastic to survive for long periods of time.

Reflexive Rubber is what allows Mister Fantastic to survive for long periods of time. Mister Fantastic stretches his body into an absorbent elastic sheet, slowing his movement speed down by 35%, but making him completely immune to all damage and effects for a short period of time or until he sustains enough damage. If he sustains enough damage, he will shoot a projectile from his body after exiting the state for some solid ranged burst. This ability has the potential to let Mister Fantastic survive almost anything thrown his way, save for extreme amounts of sustained damage that can continue to damage him even after the state ends. Timing this ability right before a big damage attack or ultimate lands can net you tons of Elasticity and a strong amount of burst from its follow-up projectile, while also forcing the enemy on their backfoot after they realize that you're still not down. Flexible Elongation is a powerful engagement tool in Reed's arsenal. He can target either an ally or an enemy with it, quickly dashing to their location and granting himself 75 overhealth that decays quickly. If he uses it on an ally, they also receive 75 overhealth, but if he uses it on an enemy, they will be hit with a small amount of damage an a slow effect. This further bolsters Mister Fantastic's anti-dive capabilities by making it even harder for them to both secure a KO on an injured target due to overhealth and evade after getting hit. Distended Grip is a powerful tool for disorienting an enemy and setting them up for an easy KO. Mister Fantastic grabs an enemy in front of him and can choose to either grab them again to pull them toward him and deal a solid chunk of damage, or grab another enemy and slam them together. The dual grab will unfortunately rarely be used, as not only does it actually cut the damage of the attack, but it simply isn't impactful enough to warrant using over the alternative. However, the single-target pull is a great tool for stopping a retreating enemy in their tracks. Elastic Strength is the bread and butter of Mister Fantastic's gameplan and what makes him function as a pseudo-Vanguard. Landing attacks and abilities will slowly generate Elasticity, which will decay over time if he does not continue building it.

Elastic Strength is the bread and butter of Mister Fantastic's gameplan and what makes him function as a pseudo-Vanguard. Landing attacks and abilities will slowly generate Elasticity, which will decay over time if he does not continue building it. Upon reaching 100 Elasticity, Mister Fantastic enters an Inflated state, turning him into a large, hulking brute and granting him a significant amount of overhealth and a higher-damaging melee attack, however he loses access to his abilities save for his ultimate. Playing around this form to switch between a potent backline bodyguard to an incredibly tanky frontline fighter is essential to playing Mister Fantastic well. Focus on playing safe within your team while in your normal state, building up Elasticity through dealing damage and protecting the backline, and once you reach 100 Elasticity, play aggressively and divert enemy attention away from your team and to you. If need be, you can cancel the Inflated form early to gain access to your abilities if you need to either go into Reflexive Rubber or use Flexible Elongation to escape. Brainiac Bounce is an exceptional tool for crowd control and causing chaos amidst a clustered group of enemies. Mister Fantastic jumps into the sky in his Inflated state, slamming down onto the ground up to six times depending on if he hits an enemy. Enemies hit by the attack will be slowed, making it easier for him to chase them down. Mister Fantastic will gain his Inflated Overhealth upon activation, making it a great panic button when being targeted. Mister Fantastic is completely CC-immune during his ultimate, meaning he cannot be affected by stuns, seizes, knockbacks, or anything that could forcibly inhibit his movement. Using the ultimate in a room with a low ceiling can allow you to string multiple slams back-to-back in quick succession for huge burst that the enemy cannot easily react to, so luring them into such a room before using the ultimate can often be quite powerful. His teamup with Invisible Woman, Wedded Harmony, gives him even more sustainability with a force field that generates overhealth as he takes damage. In combination with his other damage mitigation tools, he can become nigh-impossible to take down without severe focus fire.

Mister Fantastic in Birnin T'Challa Dr. Reed Richards, also known as the superhero as Mister Fantastic, is one of the most brilliant minds in the Marvel Universe. His defining trait is his intellectual curiosity and relentless pursuit of scientific discovery. Reed is captivated by the unknown and is continuously striving to advance humanity's understanding of the universe. His brilliance frequently borders on obsession that he might become so preoccupied with solving a problem that he loses sight of his surroundings or those closest to him. This feature identifies him as both an inspiring visionary and a distant genius companion. His personality is distinguished by his intellect, calmness, and scientific, methodical approach to everything, and he is driven by a strong desire to understand and comprehend whether it is in the branch of physics, engineering, astronomy or any study, which may sometimes make him appear detached, socially incompetent, or even disregard personal connections in the search of knowledge. Beyond his intelligence, Reed Richards is a truly empathetic and responsible leader. As the Fantastic Four 's leader, he feels a strong sense of responsibility to both his team and the world. His scientific activities are rarely for personal gain; rather, he seeks to use his expertise to safeguard and improve humanity. This moral compass distinguishes him as a true hero, even when his judgments are difficult or misinterpreted by others. Reed's perfectionism and emotional detachment, on the other hand, can cause conflict, particularly with individuals he cares about, such as his wife, Sue Storm .  He occasionally puts intellect above emotion, which causes others to perceive him as cold or overly analytical. However, beneath his controlled façade lurks a guy overwhelmed by the weight of responsibility, someone who sincerely cares but struggles to articulate it, especially when the Timestream Entanglement happened.

Reed Richards' relationship with his wife Sue Storm is the emotional foundation of the Fantastic Four. The two have an intimate relationship based on affection, mutual respect, and years of collaboration in both research and battle. Sue's emotional intelligence balances Reed's logical thinking, and she frequently grounds him when his obsession with science causes him to become distant or overly analytical. Despite the occasional stresses produced by Reed's workaholic tendencies, Sue recognizes his sense of duty and desire to protect others. Their marriage has faced several challenges, including interdimensional threats and personal problems, yet their love has remained strong. With Johnny and Ben , Reed frequently serves as a paternal or older brother figure to Johnny, encouraging him both as a scientist and a hero. Johnny's reckless style frequently conflicts with Reed's analytical disposition, resulting in amusing banter and occasional resentment. Still, Reed really cares about Johnny's well-being and development, usually defending him or assisting him in using his talents more responsibly. While Reed and Ben Grimm share a profound friendship tinged with guilt and loyalty as Ben is his closest buddy since college, has always stood by his side. Reed and Sue's superpowered children, Franklin and Valeria, reveal a softer, more vulnerable side of him. Through them, he is not only the universe's greatest thinker, but also a father seeking to combine knowledge with love, control with trust, and logic with emotion.  H.E.R.B.I.E. , meanwhile, completes this dynamic as a steadfast presence in the Richards household, frequently acting as the glue that binds the family together when Reed's scientific ambitions threaten to drive him away. With other heroes, Reed’s relationship with Spider-Man is that of a mentor and a kindred spirit. Reed admires Peter’s scientific talent and moral integrity, as he welcomes him in their family. Now with T'Challa and Tony Stark , they share a relationship grounded in mutual respect and intellectual rivalry. They are regarded as among the greatest minds on Earth, but their ideas frequently diverge. Despite their differences, they understand each other in ways that few people can, forging a friendship based on mutual respect, intelligence, and a commitment to safeguard humanity. Mr.

His primary fire, Crescent Dart, is the core of his gameplay, being unique as it can bounce between enemies close to each other, up to three times. Crescent Dart will also bounce between the doppelganger illusions spawned by Loki . It can also bounce between his Ancient Ankh. His secondary fire, Moon Blade, launches a projectile in a straight line that deals higher damage than his Crescent Dart, but is limited by a cooldown. Much like Crescent Dart, it can also ricochet between enemies and Ancient Ankhs. Moon Blade can be fired immediately after using primary fire. It can be used to cancel primary fire's recovery frames. Ancient Ankh is a tool that further enables Moon Knight's kit and makes his projectile ricocheting even stronger. Both his Crescent Dart and Moon Blade will ricochet from it to any enemy within the Ankh's spell field range. This gives his ricochets an exceptional area-of-effect and allows the player to strategically deal quick burst damage to isolated enemies. When thrown, the Ankh briefly pulls enemies towards it while dealing a small amount of damage. The Ankh can be attached to any surface, and will remain there indefinitely until destroyed. Ankhs persist even if the surfaces they are placed on are destroyed. A maximum of two Ankhs may be active at any time. His melee attack, Triple Eclipse, is a three-hit combo with his truncheons. The third strike briefly knocks enemies up. It may be used to provide space between an attacker when Moon Knight is attacked in close range. His Ultimate, Hand of Khonshu, creates a large radial portal in the location, creating a spell field that deals high multi-hit damage. It is most effective when used in choke points and areas where enemies are grouped together. Weaknesses [ ] Relies heavily on grouped enemy positioning to achieve the most damage. Relatively poor single target damage compared to other Duelists unless an Ankh is used. His Crescent Dart and Moon Blade have a damage falloff of -20% per bounce. Not as useful in larger maps where the enemy team is less likely to stay close to each other. His effectiveness falls significantly when Ancient Ankh is on cooldown.

Many of his attacks can bounce between nearby enemies and deployables summoned using his ANCIENT ANKH ability. In combination with projectiles, Moon Knight also has a variety of mobility options such as his glider, grapple, and double jump. Overall, he is a powerful mid-range damage dealer that even flankers may struggle to deal with if caught off-guard. Primary Attack: CRESCENT DART (Left Mouse Button) Function: Throws three darts that bounce between nearby enemies and ankhs. Role: Primary source of damage. Strategy: Chip Damage: Even a single shot can chip away at the entire enemy team and force them to back up. Hitbox Priority: Target opponents with large hitboxes such as Vanguards to increase your likelihood of your shots achieving the max amount of bounces. Choke Point Dominance: Fire down at choke points to block them off as long as you maintain your distance. Damage Loss: Remember that projectiles deal 20% less damage for each bounce. Personality [ ] https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Moon_Knight_-_Setup_01.ogg I'm Marc Spector, I'm Steven Grant, I'm Jake Lockley. And we are Moon Knight. Moon Knight Marc Spector, the former mercenary turned avatar of a god, is the man behind the Moon Knight persona, is complicated and diverse, formed by trauma, identity conflicts, and a strong desire for vengeance and justice. His personality is characterized by an ongoing internal conflict, particularly with his dissociative identity disorder (DID), which gives him numerous personas, each contending for control over his actions. His DID was developed to cope with a difficult and abusive childhood. Neurotic and aggressive, Marc is fundamentally a man driven by guilt and a desire to atone for his previous violent actions.  As a mercenary, he did things that haunt him, and his encounter and resurrection by the Egyptian god Khonshu thrusts him into a new position, but one that never totally releases him from his inner conflict. His psychological experiences are complex, intertwining elements of trauma, DID, guilt, hallucinations, flashbacks caused by his PTSD and a constant battle between his human self and the influence of the supernatural (Khonshu) that shape his life. This variation of Marc is eager about inflicting Khonshu's verdict as Moon Knight, as opposed to his equivalents in other versions who question their patron god's decisions. However, he is well aware that Khonshu is a handful and extremely overpowering, since he notes how the god is continuously listening and poking him.

Moon Knight and Khonshu have a much more cordial connection here, yet they regularly insult, mock, or annoy each other, while their animosity is a type of affection rather than actual hatred. He also has his faith on Khonshu whenever he is on the battlefield, knowing the deity has his back in times of trouble. His Moon Knight avatar embodies retribution and, in many ways, represents his quest for redemption. This sense of purpose frequently clashes with his other alters, particularly Steven Grant, the mild-mannered, socially awkward socialite Marc developed to cope with the darker aspects of his existence with his compassionate and intelligent traits. And Jake Lockley, Marc's less than friendly alter, is more street-savvy, hardboiled and violent taxi driver, embodying the more primitive part of his nature. The presence of these alters: Steven, Marc, and Jake, all work to showcase a shattered mentality, with each contributing their own skills and faults, transforming Moon Knight into a character who is equal parts a deeply psychological individual and a battling vigilante as well as the avatar of the god of vengeance.  In his role as a vigilante, he is a ruthless and uncompromising figure who will not hesitate to use drastic means to fight criminals who would prey on the innocent in the dark. His sense of justice is not constrained by the same laws or norms that govern other superheroes such as Spider-Man or Captain America leading to being infamous among heroes for being completely unhinged. He does not shy away from violence, with his alter Jake Lockley especially using it, and his methods are frequently more severe than other crime-fighters, verging on a cruelty or animosity that at times leads him to be largely unpredictable. He prefers to be seen, even proudly claiming so, in his explanation as to why he wears the color white; seeking to present himself to his enemies while he takes hits on purpose, fighting through pain with reckless disregard. Despite his tortured nature, there are times that he can be quite humorous as constantly cracking jokes and delivering ridiculous one-liners while in a serious and dramatic tone.

Despite his tortured nature, there are times that he can be quite humorous as constantly cracking jokes and delivering ridiculous one-liners while in a serious and dramatic tone. Furthermore, his relationships with other Marvel characters, are frequently strained due to his unpredictable nature, despite this, he has also demonstrated an intense dedication and loyalty to others when the situation requires it.  His harsh techniques and moral uncertainty sometimes define his role as an antihero, and his connection to the Egyptian god Khonshu lend a cosmic weight to his confrontations. Moon Knight is a figure who combines elements of street heroism with an otherworldly mythos, resulting in a unique blend of crime-fighting and psychological depth. He stands out as one of most psychologically complex and morally problematic characters, combining with a raw investigation of trauma, identity and the weight of his acts, but he still strives to do what he believes is right. Additionally, these Monstros also have an automatic aimlock, meaning no matter how fast you're moving, the projectiles will always track you down. This makes Namor a great counterpick to dive characters, as many of them play close, forcing the Monstros to automatically lock onto the enemy dive, preventing them from causing unwanted pressure onto your enemy backline. A quick fast combo with Namor follows his M1 attack, his M2 attack, and then his M1 attack again. This can provide a large burst of damage while also redirecting your Monstros and enhancing them. Namor's Monstros have incredible range, being able to reach a maximum of 40 meters.

Instead of placing them high in the air making them an easy target, place them in blind spots, such as above enemy walkways or behind the frontline. This ensures the enemy team doesn't eliminate the Monstros before they get to deal valuable damage. If you're ever playing Namor against dive characters, it's important to place your Monstros closer towards your backline to give them the protection they need. It would be wise to show some respect. https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Namor_-_Hero_Spawned_08.ogg Namor Namor has a regal, dominating presence, which reflects his royal heritage. As the king of Atlantis, He is haughty, fiercely independent, and pretty arrogant, with a strong sense of superiority, particularly above "surface dwellers", whom he regards as irresponsible and destructive. His supreme authority is balanced with a great sense of responsibility for his people and kingdom, and he is willing to make difficult decisions in order to secure Atlantis' future with his famous battle cry, "Imperius Rex!", embodies this arrogant and imperious attitude as a ruler and warrior. Namor's pride conceals a deep emotional intensity. He is extremely enthusiastic about his love interests, affiliations, and vendettas. His allegiance is strong, but his temper is notoriously short, making him unpredictable and egotistical. Namor does not always follow traditional morals; he favors justice and survival over heroics. Because of his moral ambiguity, he can be a formidable ally or a dangerous enemy depending on his motives. His dual identity as both a mutant and Atlantean further adds to his inner conflict. He often feels like he belongs to two worlds but is fully accepted by neither.

His dual identity as both a mutant and Atlantean further adds to his inner conflict. He often feels like he belongs to two worlds but is fully accepted by neither. The perception of him as a villain is strongly influenced by viewpoint, context, and the situations surrounding him. Namor's arrogance, anger, and willingness to use force to protect his people or punish those who destroy the ocean make him a villain to others, particularly surface dwellers and superhero teams that value diplomacy over action. He is not afraid to attack countries, destroy cities, or kill enemies if he believes it is justified. These efforts, motivated by pride and intense commitment to Atlantis, frequently set him at odds with heroes such as the Avengers and the Fantastic Four . Namor's relationship with the Fantastic Four began as hostile, owing to his obsession with Sue Storm and dislike for the surface world. Early on, he frequently clashed with the team, particularly Reed Richards , whom he regarded as a romantic competitor. Namor constantly courted Sue, giving her a life as his queen in Atlantis. Sue was never totally convinced, but she did express sympathy for Namor, understanding the nobility underlying his violence, which fueled Namor and Reed's conflict. Despite these conflicts, Namor has occasionally joined forces with the Fantastic Four when their objectives coincided, particularly when larger threats threatened both the surface and Atlantis. Namor's relationship with the X-Men is more nuanced. As one of Marvel's original mutants, he occasionally embraced his identity and joined forces with mutantkind. He joined the X-Men at times when mutant survival was threatened. Namor's dedication to the mutant cause, however, is frequently submerged by his devotion to Atlantis. He aids mutantkind when their interests are compatible, but he remains an outsider, respected but never totally absorbed. His time with the X-Men revealed a more contemplative side of him, particularly about mutant politics and survival, although his pride and independence also caused him to clash with other members. Namor stands out as a wild card: powerful, principled in his own way, and never totally trustworthy, he is motivated by pride, purpose, and passion, reflecting the conflict between duty and personal desire.

Trivia [ ] Namor's first appearance was in " Marvel Comics " (1939) #1 in August 1939. He originally debuted in " Motion Picture Funnies Weekly " (1939) #1 in April 1939, six months before the official launch of Marvel Comics (then known as Timely Comics). This unpublished material was later expanded and repurposed as the lead feature for the company's debut issue. This makes him the oldest Marvel character based on debut in the game. His design and background in Marvel Rivals are a blend of his comic and MCU versions, maintaining his original McKenzie family lineage while incorporating the Mesoamerican cultural roots and aesthetics introduced in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Namor's name is only pronounced "Nah-mor" by him, Luna Snow and Black Panther . The entire cast refers to him as "Nae-mor". Namor's signature is a Mayan script also known as Maya glyphs. Namor is the first character to not speak as an ultimate voiceline. Additionally, Namor is so far the only character that has one ultimate "voiceline" for self&ally and one for enemy.

Peni's kit revolves around her Cyber-Webs, which grant her and her allies bonus movement speed, healing-over-time and bonus health while stepping on them. Her primary fire, Cyber-Web Cluster, is unique as it has infinite ammo, allowing Peni to keep her pressure constantly. Her secondary fire, Cyber-Web Snare, immobilizes targets hit; if the web hits a surface (ground, walls, ceiling), it creates a Cyber-Web area. This ability can even interrupt Ultimates, such as Scarlet Witch 's Reality Erasure and Spider-Man 's Spectacular Spin. This ability has a hitbox that can block projectiles, including some Ultimates, most notably Iron Man 's Invincible Pulse Cannon. Arachno-Mines are tiny bombs that can be shot and attached to any surface; if shot on a Cyber-Web, they'll be concealed and become invisible to the enemy team; if the enemy positions themselves near them, the mines will detonate after a short delay. Bionic Spider-Nest is a stationary deployable unit that creates a large Cyber-Web around its location and periodically spawns exploding Spider-Drones which lock on enemies that step on the web. Peni can manually position it. Only one can be placed at once, and its cooldown is shorter the more health it currently has after Peni deactivates it. Cyber-Bond is Peni's limited use of webslinging. She can fire a strand of web that pulls her to any surface it hits; Peni will be latched by the web until it's cancelled. This ability creates a Cyber-Web. Since this ability has a mere 3 second cooldown, it makes Peni one of the fastest tanks to cover ground. Her Ultimate, Spider-Sweeper, vastly increases her movement speed while granting her access to a sweep attack that launches enemies upwards. In addition, she gains bonus health and constantly launches Cyber-Webs and Arachno-Mines while running. TEAM-UP BONUS - +50 Max Health Strategy [ ] Peni Parker excels at mid- to long range combat, a very different playstyle from other vanguards. When playing offense it is best to continuously throw out Arachno-Mines onto the battlefield. Even when not hidden enemies do not often check for random mines and will often simply walk past and take 100 free damage. The versatility of her kit comes down to the Spider-Nest. Repositioning and making sure the nest cannot be shot out is key, by maintaining some presence using her Bionic Spider-Nests you can stop a sudden push forward from the enemy and, if being supported by your team, even stop a hard push where ultimates are used. Always have a web under your feet to allow for constant passive healing and added bonus health when not in a team fight. Her Cyber-Bond also offers her more escape potential than other vanguards, letting her quickly evade a dangerous situation and regroup with her team and start pushing back up. Personality [ ] My dad built SP//dr for himself, but I feel like I was born to pilot it. https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Peni_Parker_-_Hero_Spawned_06.ogg Peni Parker Peni Parker's demeanor combines young fragility, calm resilience, and a developing feeling of responsibility, all sculpted by the particular challenges of operating the SP//dr mech. At her most basic, she is introverted and emotionally observant, preferring computers, data, mathematics and technology's calming rationality to social chaos. Despite her shyness, she has a strong moral compass; she wants to help people not for recognition, but because she understands the weight of her father's legacy. Her father's death has a major impact on her narrative. He died in the line of duty while piloting the SP//dr, leaving huge shoes for Peni to fill. However, the way people spoke about him demonstrates that he was respected, revered, and really loved, rather than defined by tragedy. To Peni, her father represents both inspiration and emotional weight. She is dealing with grief, the dread of failing to honor his memory, and the strain of inheriting a mantle she did not ask for.

To Peni, her father represents both inspiration and emotional weight. She is dealing with grief, the dread of failing to honor his memory, and the strain of inheriting a mantle she did not ask for. However, his example becomes her strength: his kindness directs her actions, his bravery propels her onward, and his legacy is something she redefines on her own terms. Peni's inner strength is surrounded by uncertainty, which is what makes her so appealing. She struggles with feelings of isolation, sorrow, and the dread of not being "enough," all while being put into positions much beyond her years. Instead of arrogance, she faces danger with quiet tenacity, frequently considering before acting and relying on teamwork when necessary. Her relationship with the SP//dr AI serves as a strong emotional anchor for her, providing stability in a world where she frequently feels out of place. Despite the difficulties she has faced, she manages to deal by talking with others with a positive attitude, making friends with everyone, asking questions with curiosity and particularly engaging with robotics and technology. When she meets the other Spider-People, she gradually allows herself to open up. That sense of belonging allows her to recognize that she does not have to carry everything by herself. This shows in one interaction in-game is with Spider-Man , which Peter acts like a older brother to her. Peni is also renowned for making jokes and being snarky, especially with her friends and foes, and making fun of it, similarly to other Spider-People. When Peni defeats specific heroes in-game like Magik , she tells her that goth is out of style, or referring to Black Panther as "royal cat-ness". Overall, Peni gains confidence, expresses herself, and is willing to stand firm as she grows. Her journey is about discovering identity beyond loss and fate, demonstrating that courage can be kind, thoughtful, and unquestionably heroic. Her responsibilities as a hero and one of the protectors of the Web of Life and Destiny are particularly challenging, but she remains calm but strong, demonstrating that resilience does not always roar; it may hum like a machine that keeps going even under strain, following her father's legacy while piloting his mech through timelines.

Telepathic Illusion allows Phoenix to swiftly dash in the direction of movement and leave behind an illusion that explodes after a short delay, applying 1 Spark to nearby enemies. Dark Ascent grants Phoenix free flight and increased movement speed when active. This ability can be used well to quickly recover from fights whilst also repositioning yourself. Her Ultimate, Endsong Inferno, lifts her into the sky and then allows her to slowly dive down towards a targeted area on the ground. Upon landing, a massive explosion will be triggered that deals damage to enemies within a very large nearby radius and applies 1 Spark to those hit. The explosion also immediately depletes all bonus health and kills enemy spawnables, making this extremely useful even against opponents with high survivability such as Venom . Phoenix is immune to all forms of damage and stun during the casting process of the Ultimate. After the Ultimate ends, Phoenix will reappear in the air from the original casting location and regain all of her missing health. The critical aspect of her gameplay revolves around consistently applying 3 Sparks to a target, which triggers a fiery explosion. This explosion not only deals additional damage and applies a Spark to nearby enemies but also provides Phoenix with a crucial Healing Over Time (HoT) effect. Prioritize Critical Hits: Landing critical hits with COSMIC FLAMES applies 2 Sparks, significantly accelerating the explosion trigger. Aim for headshots! Sustain through Explosions: The self-healing from explosions is vital for Phoenix's survivability. Constantly proccing these explosions on enemies, especially Vanguards or grouped targets, will allow you to stay in the fight longer. AoE Pressure: The explosion's splash damage contributes to team fight pressure, especially when enemies are grouped. Primary Attack: COSMIC FLAMES (Left Mouse Button) Role: Primary source of damage and Spark application. Strategy: Maintain consistent fire on targets to quickly build Sparks. Prioritize critical hits to trigger explosions faster. Be mindful of the damage falloff beyond 10m; try to engage within optimal range for maximum damage. Use the self-healing from explosions to sustain yourself during engagements. Ultimate Ability: ENDSONG INFERNO (Q) Role: High-impact burst damage, area denial, and counter to summon/shield/bonus health heroes. Counterplay: The shockwave is incredibly powerful against heroes reliant on summons (e.g., Rocket Raccoon's Beacon, Peni Parker's Spider-Nests), shields, or bonus health. Personality [ ] https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Phoenix_-_Hero_Spawned_05.ogg I'm still the same old Jean Grey… but I'm also so much more… Phoenix Jean Grey is frequently distinguished by her great empathy, which forms the basis of her personality. Her growth from a shy teenage mutant to a confident, compassionate, intelligent and determined hero who acts as the heart of the X-Men began at a young age, when her telepathy exposed her to the emotions of others, turning her into someone who feels deeply and responds compassionately. This emotional sensitivity lends her a calm, soothing demeanor that many other X-Men rely on as she is frequently the calm center of the crisis, listening, understanding, and mediating. Jean is known for her warm and consoling nature, often acting as a mentor to younger mutants and caring deeply for her teammates. Despite her kind demeanor, Jean conceals a hidden strength that emerges during times of stress. She is tenacious, smart, and capable of making difficult decisions when it counts the most. Her bravery is motivated by moral conviction and a desire to defend others, rather than violence. This makes her not just a powerful mutant, but also a natural leader whose authority is based on trust, not fear. Jean is also motivated by an emotional struggle to reconcile her enormous powers with her yearning for a normal existence. She frequently feels a sense of responsibility, knowing that her skills might easily damage others if she loses control, leading to this internal limitation which defines her humility, she never pursues grandeur and frequently minimizes her own significance, even when many around her regard her as amazing. Her relationships, particularly with the X-Men, shape her nature. Jean appreciates connection and devotion, and she creates strong ties based on mutual respect.

She frequently provides emotional clarity to the team, stabilizing people like her husband Scott Summers while challenging others like Logan in ways that promote their growth. Her interpersonal warmth is as important to her personality as her mutant abilities. Jean Grey's relationships play an important role in her emotional development as an X-Man. She and Scott Summers has one of the most central, long-running, and complex romances. They enjoy a core love based on shared history, trust, and mutual responsibility, resulting in a partnership that frequently serves as the anchor for the entire team. Scott frequently relies on Jean as an emotional anchor, and she admires his discipline, dedication, and the quiet power that drives his leadership. Their love has its challenges, particularly Jean's struggle with her powers and Scott's pressure as team leader, but they always return to each other. Her relationship with Logan is highly contrasted, intense, passionate, and hazardous, and is based on aspects of herself that she rarely expresses, which both had a deep connection. Jean's bond with Ororo is one of great mutual appreciation, and she has a sister-like confidante who knows the weight of enormous power leading to Storm frequently serves as an emotional anchor for Jean, particularly when she is dealing with the enormous burden of her life problems, the Phoenix Force or her psychic abilities. As the Phoenix, Jean's personality changes greatly, expanding to meet the cosmic force she represents. The Phoenix Force heightens her emotions, sense of self, and wants, resulting in a character that is both sublime and volatile. What was once empathy is now omniscience, and what was once inner strength has become cosmic certainty leading Jean to be defined by passion in its most intense form: the desire for life, creation, destruction, and evolution. The Phoenix does not do things halfway; its love is unconditional, its fury ferocious, and its sadness desolate. At the same time, traces of Jean’s humanity linger within the Phoenix, creating a tension between compassion and cosmic impulse. Jean Grey follows the Phoenix wherever it goes, even in space, since the two of them have become one now.

The other, hearts. Psylocke Sai, also known as the mutant Psylocke, is the embodiment of the disciplined and contemplative warrior and empath. In a feudal Japan-inspired alternate universe, she is driven by a strong sense of duty to slaughter yōkai and protect the innocent. Her demeanor is strict and mission-driven, rarely swayed by outside distractions or personal gain. Unlike past incarnations of Psylocke, Sai's strength is not just physical but also moral: she follows a rigid code of honor akin to a wandering ronin, balancing lethal efficiency with the protection of those who cannot defend themselves. Beneath her stoicism comes a gentle melancholy, a subtle longing for the home and life she was ripped away caused by the Timestream Entanglement .  She battles not for glory, but for responsibility and a feeling of purpose, giving her the appearance of solemn nobility. Despite her cautious and solemn personality, Sai reveals a very thoughtful and emotionally nuanced side. Her separation from her native world has left her somewhat disconnected, and she frequently observes people through an old-soul lens formed by her cultural and temporal disparities.

Despite her cautious and solemn personality, Sai reveals a very thoughtful and emotionally nuanced side. Her separation from her native world has left her somewhat disconnected, and she frequently observes people through an old-soul lens formed by her cultural and temporal disparities. She may mistake current habits or terminology, but she does so with sincerity and a commitment to her personal moral compass, particularly when asking or engaging with modern heroes such as the X-Men , Guardians , and the Avengers or referring to some characters or creatures as yōkai or oni. Psylocke also has a wolf pet named Logan , which serves as her constant companion and emotional anchor, showing her loyalty, empathy, and the softer side beneath her tough warrior identity, with both of them currently living in the island of Krakoa offered by Magneto . Sai's personality is a careful balance of external control and inward depth, demonstrating a warrior whose strength is as much in her moral and mental toughness as in her mastery of martial skill, and she pledges to eliminate any threats or demons until she gets back to her home in the midst of the chaotic entanglement between timelines. Psylocke fending off Magik's Corporate Raiders counterpart in "Hostile Takeover". Trivia [ ] Sai first appeared in " King in Black " (2020) #4 in February 2021. Her first full-length appearance as a protagonist was in " Demon Days: X-Men " (2021) #1 in March 2021, which officially launched her story. Artist Peach Momoko created Sai as a reimagined Edo-period Psylocke for her "Momoko-verse" ( Earth-42141 ). In mainline Marvel Comics, the "Psylocke" mantle is tied to a complex history involving a body-swap between two characters, both of whom serve as visual inspiration for Sai's alternative costumes: Betsy Braddock: The original Psylocke, who first appeared in " Captain Britain" (1976) #8 and adopted the Psylocke codename in " New Mutants Annual " (1984) #2 after being body-swapped with Kwannon. She gave up the title after returning to her original body. Kwannon: A Japanese assassin who first appeared in " X-Men" Vol. 2 (1991) #17 . After returning to her original body, she officially claimed the Psylocke title in " Fallen Angels " (2019) #1 . Psylocke's Ultimate voice line is "Chō no mai o kurae!" (蝶の舞を喰らえ!). Although her voice actress Alpha Takahashi translates it as "Dance of the Butterflies," the literal translation is closer to "Devour the Butterfly Dance!" or "Eat this Butterfly Dance!". Sai is one of three heroes whose ultimate voice lines are spoken in a language other than English (the others being Iron Fist and White Fox ); in her case, the lines are in Japanese.

His primary fire, Bombard Mode, uses his custom-built rifle to rapidly fire bullets. This ability has one of the highest rate-of-fire in the game. His secondary fire, Repair Mode, uses his custom-built rifle to launch bouncing yellow spheres that provides healing-over-time to allies within its radius. The projectiles will ricochet off any surfaces upon contact (including walls and ceilings), with a maximum of 10 bounces. When they approach injured allies, their speed will reduce. This ability grants Rocket Raccoon incredible flexibility as he can use terrain to make the spheres bounce to allies out of reach, or to safely heal the team while hiding behind walls out of the enemy team's line of sight. Rocket can also use the spheres to heal himself with halved efficiency. If the spheres touch an ally directly it'll provide a small burst of instant healing. B.R.B. (Battle Rebirth Beacon) has Rocket Raccoon deploy a stationary gadget on the targeted location that revives a fallen ally once, within a large radius around it. Resurrected allies will appear at the beacon's location at full health. Upon reviving an ally, the beacon disappears and goes on a cooldown. While active, the beacon periodically generates armor packs and rocket jet packs every 3 seconds, shooting them randomly within its radius. The armor pack grants 25 bonus health. The rocket jet pack grants players a super jump that launches them high in the air upon pressing the jump button in mid-air. The beacon has 150 health and lasts for 300 seconds. If the player presses the button again, the beacon will be reclaimed, and the cooldown will be reduced based on the beacon's remaining health. If reclaiming a full-health beacon, the minimum cooldown will be 5 seconds. If Rocket Raccoon is knocked out while the beacon is on a full cooldown, it will be refreshed once he respawns. Players can drop the beacon before the match starts to give the whole team armor packs and rocket jet packs. Collected packs will persist even if the player controlling Rocket Raccoon reclaims the beacon or switches to another character. Strategically placing the beacon on spots out of enemy reach ensures it will not be destroyed before reviving an ally.

Collected packs will persist even if the player controlling Rocket Raccoon reclaims the beacon or switches to another character. Strategically placing the beacon on spots out of enemy reach ensures it will not be destroyed before reviving an ally. Try not to hide it too much or the allied team will not benefit from the armor packs and the rocket jet packs. Allies can see if they're within the revive radius of the beacon by the visible icon above their healthbars. Jetpack Dash has Rocket Raccoon quickly propelling himself forward. This ability will move him towards any direction of the aiming reticle, granting him flexible mobility. This combined with his small frame, the ability to wall climb, slow fall and use the rocket jump from B.R.B. makes Rocket Raccoon very hard to pin down. Using Jetpack Dash during wall climb propels Rocket Raccoon further in direction of wall climb, but any surface roughness can stop Jetpack Dash His Ultimate, C.Y.A. (Cosmic Yarn Amplifier), has Rocket Raccoon deploy a stationary gadget that grants a 25% damage boost and 100 bonus health points per second to all linked allies within its radius. The amplifier has 800 health and lasts for 12 seconds. The bonus health has a cap of 150. Players can track if they are within the effect radius by the visible energy thread connecting them to the amplifier. When paired with Groot , Rocket Raccoon gains access to Old Friends, allowing him to hop on Groot's shoulders, granting him a 35% damage reduction. Weaknesses [ ] Very vulnerable when both charges of Jetpack Dash are on cooldown, as well as if he is around open areas without nearby walls to climb. Bombard Mode has some of the lowest damage distance falloffs in the game, meaning it'll be much weaker against distant enemies. Repair Mode lacks high burst healing, on top of healing half the amount of affecting Rocket Raccoon himself. B.R.B. has some limitations. The beacon cannot revive Rocket Raccoon himself. If Rocket Raccoon is taken down while the beacon is active, it will disappear. The beacon has a limited radius; if players are too far they won't be revived.

B.R.B. has some limitations. The beacon cannot revive Rocket Raccoon himself. If Rocket Raccoon is taken down while the beacon is active, it will disappear. The beacon has a limited radius; if players are too far they won't be revived. Reclaiming the beacon will cause all the armor packs and rocket jet packs currently spawned to disappear. Players can only get a single armor pack and rocket jet pack from B.R.B. If placed on tight and small areas that cannot fit a character, it will disappear after a few seconds and go on a 5-second cooldown. B.R.B. and C.Y.A. can be destroyed by the enemy team. Jetpack Dash only propels Rocket Raccoon forward even if holding the direction backwards. This means that if the player wants to retreat behind themselves, they have to do a 180º spin and use the ability. Hopping on Groot 's shoulders can leave Rocket Raccoon vulnerable, as Groot usually fights in the frontlines. Even with the damage reduction, he can still be focused and taken down easily. In addition, any kind of hard crowd control used on Groot (e.g. stuns) will knock Rocket down from his shoulders. This stuff is for professionals only… and that don't mean you! https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Rocket_Raccoon_-_POI_Klyntar_Symbiotic_Surface_05.ogg Rocket Raccoon in Symbiotic Surface Rocket has something of a rough around the edges attitude. He is a brash, sarcastic, hot headed and trigger happy raccoon, but fiercely loyal and loving to his friends. His default attitude is hostility, fast to growl, quicker to shoot, and he never skips an opportunity to tease someone, especially when he feels defenseless. His harsh exterior is the result of a terrible history as an experimental subject, and it only takes a little to set off his temper, especially when referred to as a "rodent" or "raccoon". Rocket's confidence belies his deep insecurities and trauma as his anger frequently hides the anguish of feeling "broken" or "wrong," prompting him to lash out when someone gets too near. He despises being treated like an animal and reacts angrily to any display of sympathy. Despite his loud and chaotic personality, Rocket struggles with identity, worth, and the worry that others will see him for who he believes he is. Deep down, he is lonely and adores his newfound family in the Guardians of the Galaxy , despite his tendency to disguise this softer side behind sarcasm and humor. His intellect, however, is tempered by insecurity; he frequently overcompensates with bravado, playing tough to conceal his deep difficulties with identity and self-worth. Peter Quill and Rocket have a connection based on chaos, loyalty, and a unique form of brotherhood. On the surface, they argue incessantly over leadership, plans, music, weapons, and pretty much everything else. Both are stubborn, prideful, and insecure in their own ways, which leads to continual conflicts, such as when they crash the Milano into Klyntar . Underneath the noise, their friendship is genuine and unbreakable. They've saved each other countless times, relied on each other at their lowest points, and grown closer to brothers than teammates, particularly in protecting their family, the Guardians.

Underneath the noise, their friendship is genuine and unbreakable. They've saved each other countless times, relied on each other at their lowest points, and grown closer to brothers than teammates, particularly in protecting their family, the Guardians. Their relationship is chaotic, loud, and full of disagreements, but it is also one of the most sincere connections either of them has. He is also a bit of a kleptomaniac, often stealing things that he can get his paws on, including stuff from other heroes like Peni’s mech, Frank’s turret and so on. While it’s these traits that makes it difficult for Rocket to get along with other heroes and his status as a hero questionable, he is not without his perks, one of them being his rarely expressed kindness and care for his friends, including his closest friend Groot , which according to Rocket, is the only one who gets him. Beneath that loud exterior, Rocket is incredibly intelligent, arguably one of the brightest minds in the galaxy. He possesses a highly advanced knowledge of technology and a tactical mindset, often using those gifts in fixing up the ship or making a plan for any problems he and his team run into. He’s a good thinker, a master engineer and pilot, a weapons savant, and a quick problem-solver even under pressure. Rocket’s source of his anger is from his past of being painfully experimented on, and it’s that pain that often leads him to push others away, so that he never feels that pain again. Rocket's heart, however, is much bigger than he admits. When he lets others in, he becomes fiercely devoted, protective, and unexpectedly caring. His relationship with the Guardians exemplifies the best aspects of him: someone who is willing to risk everything for the few individuals he trusts. He's still snarky, aggressive, and ready to verbally bite someone's head off, but now it's tempered with genuine connection, leadership, and even vulnerability. He may complain, mock, or threaten to leave at any moment, but when his family and friends are in danger, he becomes the bravest person in the room. Trivia [ ] Rocket Raccoon's first appearance was in " Marvel Preview " (1975) #7 in July 1976, where he was originally introduced under the name "Rocky". He later debuted with his full name and integrated into the mainstream Marvel Universe in " Incredible Hulk " (1962) #271 in May 1982. Rocket is named and inspired by The Beatles ' song "Rocky Raccoon" from the White Album . [ 1 ] Rocket's default emote sees him posing with his gun on his shoulder. In the hero gallery, he flies during the emote, however in-game he stands on the ground during it. The interaction between Iron Man and Rocket Raccoon in Klyntar mentions that the Avengers once built a headquarters inside a Celestial's corpse. This references the Avengers Mountain which first appeared in Avengers (Vol. 8) #8 (2018) .
