Official Description Rogue is a Vanguard hero in Marvel Rivals , and the 45th hero added to the game's roster. She released in Season 5.5 . She currently has one team-up ability: Explosive Entanglement — with Gambit and Magneto Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Strengths 1.2 Weaknesses 2 Costumes 3 Abilities 4 Strategy 5 Personality 6 Achievements 7 Proficiency 7.1 Challenges 7.2 Rewards 8 Gallery 9 Trivia 10 References 11 Navigation Overview [ ] Strengths [ ] A durable hybrid tank with high means of consistently closing distance between opponents through dashes and displacement. Part of her kit revolves around reducing enemy stats to further enhance her own. Her primary fire, Power Surge Punch, performs two quick melee strikes and then a slower thrusting strike that deals slightly more damage. Her secondary fire, Defensive Stance, drains resource to reduce damage taken from the front and draw in oncoming projectiles while active. Damage blocked charges backlash energy, which increases the damage of Southern Brawl for its next activation. Southern Brawl can be used during Defensive Stance to dash forward and perform a melee strike that slightly knocks back enemies, draining all backlash energy.

Damage blocked charges backlash energy, which increases the damage of Southern Brawl for its next activation. Southern Brawl can be used during Defensive Stance to dash forward and perform a melee strike that slightly knocks back enemies, draining all backlash energy. Fatal Attraction is a short dash that can be activated again to create a temporary zone around Rogue that deals damage over time to nearby enemies. After a delay, enemies within the zone are pulled to the center. Chrono Kick Combo activates a dash that launches enemies into the air, enabling free flight for the player for a short duration afterward. During free flight, Rogue gains two ammo for a ranged projectile attack and can activate the ability again to perform a diving strike. Rogue gains bonus health every time she hits an enemy with a projectile attack. Enemies caught within the trajectory of the diving strike are pulled down alongside the player, allowing for a more efficient cycling of abilities during combos. Ability Absorption performs a dash and pins the first enemy the player collides with to the ground, restoring a minor portion of health and absorbing one of the target's abilities ( Psylocke 's Psychic Stealth, Loki 's Regeneration Domain, etc.). Rogue also receives the Unstoppable status during the absorption animation. For certain heroes that do not have an ability that can be absorbed, the cooldown of Fatal Attraction will automatically be refreshed instead. The player will gain certain buffs and inflict certain debuffs onto the target based on the role of the enemy. They will expire after a short duration of pinning down an opponent. Vanguards increase max health by 125 HP while reducing the target's max health by 20 HP, Duelists grant a 20% damage boost while reducing the target's damage by 3%, and Strategists grant healing over time while reducing the target's healing dealt by 4%. Ability Absorption can be used on Loki 's Doppelgangers, allowing Rogue to absorb the Regeneration Domain frequently at little to no risk when Loki is on the enemy team.

Ability Absorption can be used on Loki 's Doppelgangers, allowing Rogue to absorb the Regeneration Domain frequently at little to no risk when Loki is on the enemy team. Some of the strongest abilities to gain include: Adam Warlock 's Soul Bond Doctor Strange 's Shield of the Seraphim Emma Frost 's Diamond Form Gambit 's Breaking Spades Magneto 's Iron Bulwark Storm 's Goddess Boost Thor 's Awakening Rune Wolverine 's Adamantium Spirit Her Ultimate, Heartbreaker, creates a large visible area around the player that deals damage over time to nearby enemies and continuously drains Ultimate charge if they are above 80%. Rogue will also absorb stats and buffs from enemies within range based on their role. Vanguards grant up to 400 additional max health, Duelists grant up to a 35% damage boost, and Strategists grant healing over time. When paired with Gambit , Rogue gains access to Hearts As One, which amplifies Power Surge Punch for 8 seconds to create shockwaves on impact, dealing percentage damage to nearby enemies and healing nearby allies. Weaknesses [ ] Ability Absorption can be missed relatively easily unless at a very close distance or the enemy is quite slow (ex. Vanguards including Magneto , Doctor Strange ). Ability Absorption has a 25s cooldown even if missed, making it risky to try to absorb the power of a more mobile enemy Abilities from Ability Absorption can only be held for 10 seconds, preventing holding onto abilities for later use. Players also need to be somewhat familiar with the abilities Rogue can absorb before a battle since there will not be time to learn what an ability does before it times out, hindering upon game sense. Staying in Defensive Stance for too long will leave you vulnerable to long-range stuns such as Winter Soldier 's Bionic Hook or Luna Snow 's Absolute Zero, since you do not receive any form of immunity to crowd control. From a young age, Anna Marie struggled with her capacity to absorb the memories, abilities, and even the life energy of anybody she touched, which forced her into isolation and fostered a terrible fear of connection. Her key characteristics include initial insecurity and solitude as a result of her unrestrained powers, which are balanced by a projected boldness, a great sense of humor, and passionate trust. She’s warm, sarcastic, and fiercely loyal but beneath her tough Southern attitude and confidence lies deep vulnerability, guilt, and a longing for connection she fears she can’t safely have, though Rogue has a strong moral compass and passionate devotion to those she trusts. Anna's power, which forces her to experience others' memories and emotions, makes her highly attuned to the suffering of others, even her enemies. She has a lively, often flirty side, and she frequently uses humor to shelter herself from emotional pain, but she also bears the weight of duty that comes with her powers, which causes her to be cautious and brooding.

She has a lively, often flirty side, and she frequently uses humor to shelter herself from emotional pain, but she also bears the weight of duty that comes with her powers, which causes her to be cautious and brooding. Her time with the X-Men, especially under the mentoring of individuals like Professor Xavier , and her relationships with fellow mutants like Wolverine and Storm , helped her become more sympathetic and understanding, move on from the past when she was a member of the Brotherhood of Mutants . Since then, she has been a core hero, a team fighter, a joyous friend, and a protector of mutants and humans alike, combining a strong sense of responsibility and redemption Rogue is fiercely loyal to the people she loves, especially the X-Men and her beloved husband Gambit . Their relationship is one of Marvel’s most iconic, defined by longing, trust issues, and emotional restraint. From the start, their chemistry is strong—Gambit’s charm contrasts with Rogue’s guarded nature. Their bond grows through words, glances, and patience rather than physical closeness. Overtime, their feelings deepen, bringing out both the best and worst in each other and despite conflicts and distance, their connection remains strong, rooted in trust, compassion, and shared struggles. Gambit is a risk-taker, while Rogue is careful and selfless, often putting others first. Yet both feel like outsiders, fear hurting others, and question whether they deserve love. Her journey is characterized by resilience, adaptability, and a quest for self-acceptance. She is a fighter, lover and a survivor, managing the difficulties of being a mutant in a world that frequently fears and misunderstands what she is while willing to protect others. Over time, Rogue develops the ability to accept her powers rather than be defined by them, she grows into a resilient hero defined by compassion, loyalty, and hard-earned self-acceptance displaying her enduring strength and being vulnerable when she chooses to be. Her primary fire, Chaos Control, is a channeled energy beam that deals consecutive flat damage plus an additional percentage based on the target's maximum health. This ability has infinite ammo and doesn't require much aim; Scarlet Witch will automatically attack the nearest enemy within its radius. Hitting with this ability fuels her Chaos Energy, which is used to release Chthonian Burst. Her secondary fire, Chthonian Burst, launches explosive magic missiles that both deal direct damage and also a small area-of-effect near the target location. This ability requires Chaos Energy to use and has four charges. Dark Seal launches a chaotic bubble that periodically stuns enemies within its radius.

Her secondary fire, Chthonian Burst, launches explosive magic missiles that both deal direct damage and also a small area-of-effect near the target location. This ability requires Chaos Energy to use and has four charges. Dark Seal launches a chaotic bubble that periodically stuns enemies within its radius. Mystic Projection phases Scarlet Witch out of combat, making her completely immune to all damage (excluding if she's hit by a delayed damage attack). This ability has two charges. She gains a bonus movement speed of 50% and free-flight for a few seconds while phased. Her Ultimate, Reality Erasure, is a charged attack released in a large radius around her, dealing massive damage and literally vaporizing enemies defeated by it. While charging, Scarlet Witch moves 25% slower but gains free-flight. When activated she gains a 100 hp shield that begins to decay after the ultimate is finished or is interrupted. This Ultimate deals the highest damage in the game. Reality Erasure benefits the most with teammate abilities that can mitigate enemy movements and abilities or cluster them in one place, such as with Jeff 's It's Jeff! When paired with Doctor Strange , Scarlet Witch gains access to Arcane Order, granting a new team-up ability. Weaknesses [ ] Lacks any form of defensive and self-sustain tools. Chaos Control requires Scarlet Witch to get closer to her targets, which can be dangerous due to her low health. In addition, it is not very effective if her target is under constant sustained healing. Very vulnerable if Mystic Projection is on cooldown. In addition, enemy players can track Scarlet Witch's movement during this ability, appearing as a small red spherical mist. She can be easily interrupted during Reality Erasure if the enemy team discovers her location.

Strategy [ ] Scarlet Witch should be played as a frontline brawler, taking advantage of her small hitbox and easy escape access to apply pressure with her primary and burst before than retreating to the backline with her escape. Her dark seal stun should be used in tandem with her bursts to trap a cluster of enemies and damage them all at once. Scarlet Witch Scarlet Witch's personality is strongly influenced by pain, grief, and a desire to belong. As a young girl, Wanda was orphaned and reared in a tumultuous environment with her twin brother Pietro at Mount Wundagore. They were frequently on the run or influenced by powerful figures such as Magneto , seeing as his children and making them members of his Brotherhood of Mutants as they grew up. Her relationship with her brother is a fusion of love, devotion, and emotional reliance developed through pain.  They serve as each other's anchor and mirror, reflecting both the good and bad in one another. While their closeness is occasionally tested by decisions and changing courses, their shared past keeps them close, two siblings attempting to navigate a world that has rarely been kind to them. Wanda is thoughtful, shy, and usually restrained, but not passive. She is easily carried by her emotional burden and is driven by her emotions, which can make her sensitive and empathetic, but also dangerously unpredictable. Her struggle with her tremendous powers frequently coincides with periods of mental instability, resulting in a morally complex figure who alternates between heroic intentions and destructive chaos. Since the current Scarlet Witch in the main lore is from the Collapsing Timeline , she experienced a vast grief as Pietro in this timeline has died and may had personally experienced the agony of losing control in her own timeline, where sadness or love has caused her to accidentally rewrite reality in her world, she becomes deeply devoted to ensuring that such mistakes do not occur again. She witness realties corrupted by chaos and does not want authority for its own sake; rather, she frequently fears it in which in her timeline, she is currently holding reality together from a mountaintop in Europe. Her personal experience, which includes tragedy, shame, and redemption, inspires her compassion for others who are suffering, particularly those who, like her, struggle with their own nature.

This understanding shapes her attitude into one of emotional depth, cautious determination, and, most importantly, a desire to defend reality, even if it means losing everything. Her instinct to protect others frequently propels her to address threats that no one else can, bearing her magic like a wound. Though a reminder that this version of Wanda is from a different timeline, the Scarlet Witch from the Present Timeline where the X-Men underwent to a reality-altering spell by her that significantly reduced the mutant population, resulting some of the mutants like Emma Frost were far less forgiving to this Scarlet Witch, despite the fact that she is not their Wanda. When reality is threatened by malicious magic, eldritch forces, or multiversal instability, Wanda acts as a guardian rather than a conqueror. Her relationship with Chaos Magic exemplifies this protective attitude. Even though her power is founded in chaos, she utilizes it to restore balance, to hold together what others might view as torn apart. This leads to her a built on mutual respect, magical kinship, and philosophical conflict with Doctor Strange as there are times that Strange tries to help Wanda understand and control her magic. With Magneto, Wanda Maximoff spent many years believing Erik was her biological father, which defined much of her mental anguish and formed her allegiance. Their relationship was always tight and tragic as she frequently alternated between desiring Magneto's favor and rejecting his radicalism. Despite this, there were genuine affectionate moments, Erik clearly cared for his children in his own imperfect manner, and he constantly welcomes her to Krakoa . Furthermore, among the Avengers , Scarlet Witch discovered her first true sense of family and purpose. She joined early in her career, transforming from villain to hero alongside her brother. Although not their timeline's Wanda, her in-game dialogues with heroes such as Hawkeye and Captain America treated her respectfully. Wanda frequently operates on the periphery of the superhero world, frequently mistrusted or misunderstood because to her past. Her empathy deepens and her capacity to care is wide as she realizes what she could become if she loses control. Capable of webslinging, and, unlike Venom 's Venom Swing, Spider-Man has three charges of Web-Swing. Capable of wallcrawling and sprinting while on walls. Capable of double jumping. The core gameplay of Spider-Man is attaching enemies with his Spider-Tracers, which enables his kit and even changes the properties of certain abilities. His passive, Spider-Sense, alerts players of nearby enemies in the form of an icon above Spider-Man's head. His primary fire, Spider Power, is a three-hit melee combo, being two punches and a kick. This deals extra damage if an enemy has a Spider-Tracer attached to them. His secondary fire, Web-Cluster, launches a web that deals damage and attaches a Spider-Tracer on his target for a few seconds. This ability has five charges. Get Over Here! shoots a web-string that pulls enemies towards Spider-Man's location; if the target is attached with a Spider-Tracer, Spider-Man will launch himself towards the enemy instead and perform a flying kick. Amazing Combo is a rising uppercut that launches enemies upwards. It deals extra damage if the target is attached with a Spider-Tracer. This ability has two charges. His Ultimate, Spectacular Spin, is a multi-hit barrage of web clusters that deals consistent damage in a radius around him. Each hit adds a stacking effect to the enemy of -3% slow; once it reaches a certain number of stacks, enemies become stuck in webs and stunned briefly. Spider-Man gains bonus health equal to his max health during the execution of this ability. Weaknesses [ ] Can be interrupted during Spectacular Spin. Spider-Man has an incredibly high skill ceiling & skill floor. Spider-Man requires intense precision, timing, and accuracy for kills. Spider-Man is a mechanically intensive hero. Spider-Man is widely known as the hardest character to learn and to bring value in team fights. Despite having multiple abilities and combos, Spider-Man has a very low damage output unless the abilities are followed by a web tracer. Despite being very mobile and hard to pin down, with his mobility and small hitbox, he has a small health pool and no defensive or self-sustain tools making him a very fragile glass cannon.

Instead, he excels at quick, hit-and-run tactics, focused on getting in, dealing a high-burst combo to a priority target, and then getting out. He thrives when constantly harassing the enemy backline, however take care to not linger too long there, because as mentioned before, the longer Spider-Man attempts to sustain a fight, the more vulnerable he becomes. Spider-Man should always prioritize lone squishy heroes who prefer to stay in the backline, such as Strategists or ranged heroes like Black Widow , Hawkeye , Storm , Moon Knight , or Iron Man . In contrast, he should generally avoid targeting Vanguards unless he is with his team and there is no one else to fight, as he does not have the sustained damage output necessary to take them out by himself without being overwhelmed. It is highly recommended to turn off Automatic Swing in the game's settings if you wish to play Spider-Man seriously. This gives you far more control over where you can swing from, and also gives you the ability to quickly web-zip if you fire a web line at a surface more level to your current height. This tip is also shared with Venom. Spider-Man's primary attack is Spider-Power, which functions similarly to the quick melee attacks shared by all heroes. It has a three-hit combo with the third hit dealing extra damage, and benefits from Spider-Tracer's bonus damage.

It has a three-hit combo with the third hit dealing extra damage, and benefits from Spider-Tracer's bonus damage. Spider-Man can also perform a downwards hammer slam in midair if he performs a double jump, which deals decent damage. Additionally, it can also be performed if he momentarily fires his Web Sling at a surface beforehand, which also counts as a double jump. However, this strategy should not be overused due to the Web Sling's limited charges. While it is powerful in the middle of a burst combo, his primary attack is unreliable in a sustained fight due to its low damage per hit without a Tracer and incredibly short range of only 3-4 meters. Spider-Man's secondary attack is Web-Cluster, which has him fire up to five web shots at an enemy. These shots will reload automatically, however they can only do so one at a time. Upon a successful hit, they will tag the target with a Spider-Tracer for a few seconds, which not only allows Spidey to track the target through walls, but also empowers the next attack that hits them. This ability is the bread and butter of Spider-Man's damage. Always try to weave it in between normal attacks and his uppercut to maximize the damage his attacks can deal, and if it runs out, you should attempt to disengage and reengage after they are fully recharged. As expected of the Wall-Crawler, he can use his Web-Swing to cover large distances at breakneck speed. Unlike Venom, Spidey can hold up to three charges of the ability, allowing him to far more easily engage and disengage when compared to the symbiote. This ability is the key to your survival and your ability to engage the enemy, and must be used cautiously. Keep an eye on how many swings you have so you can adequately plan around whether or not you can make an escape or reach the enemy before they can react. Get Over Here! is a ranged grab that has Spider-Man fire out a web line that can pull a target directly to him. As it counts as a stun, it can interrupt certain abilities and open them up to certain abilities.

Get Over Here! is a ranged grab that has Spider-Man fire out a web line that can pull a target directly to him. As it counts as a stun, it can interrupt certain abilities and open them up to certain abilities. In contrast, if used on an enemy tagged with a Spider-Tracer, the attack will automatically target the enemy akin to other auto-target abilities like Adam Warlock's Avatar Lifestream, but instead of stunning and pulling the enemy to him, Spider-Man himself zips over to them and hits them with a kick, dealing some extra damage. Unlike Spider-Power or Amazing Combo, hitting a tagged enemy with this attack does not remove the Tracer. This ability can be used in one of two ways: to forcefully reposition an enemy into your team to make them easy pickings, or as a follow-up to a tagged enemy to instantly get in range to start hitting them. The latter is primarily effective against flying characters like Storm or Iron Man, as they would otherwise be quite difficult to hit for anyone without sufficient range to them. If Spider-Man is in front of a pit, this ability can be used to grab and drop enemies with lacking mobility options into them. Amazing Combo has Spidey dole out a devastating uppercut that deals strong damage and launches the opponent up for an easy follow-up. Like Spider-Power, it benefits from the Spider-Tracer damage bonus. After the target is launched up, they will generally be right in your face to start hitting them with your basic attacks without needing to use an additional jump. Along with his Web-Swing, Spider-Man can also double-jump and crawl or run on walls for extra movement options. Spider-Man's Spider-Sense passive allows him to detect when an enemy is nearby even when he cannot see them. When an enemy enters an 8-meter radius of him but is not within his line of sight or his screen, he will receive a warning that someone is nearby. Use this to know when enemies are attempting to get the jump on you or to know when enemies are closing in so you can alert your team. Spider-Man's Ultimate, Spectacular Spin, turns him into a spinning tornado of webs while also granting him bonus health for its duration. If the enemy stays within the Ultimate long enough without dying, they gradually slow down before becoming completely immobilized after it ends. This Ultimate turns the character with otherwise poor crowd control into a character who can almost instantly decimate or, at the very least, severely debilitate any team that attempts to cluster up. All of Spidey's abilities work in unison with each other and rely on stringing them back-to-back in order to effectively utilize them. Always try to weave Web Clusters in between basic attacks and uppercuts to maximize the damage those attacks deal, and keep an eye on how many shots/web swings you have at any given time so you know exactly when you should attempt an escape. Spider-Man Peter Parker a.k.a. Spider-Man, is marked by a complex combination of intelligence, humor, compassion, guilt, kind, reserved, clever and a strong moral compass, making him immensely relatable and human despite his superpowers. Outside of his Spider-Man persona, Peter was a typical high school student noted for his intelligence and resourcefulness. As a science prodigy, he uses his knowledge to construct his own web-shooters and devices, and he frequently outwits his opponents using intelligent strategies rather than physical might. Peter's personality is built around a strong sense of duty and always cares for his loved ones, like Aunt May . One day, this arises from the terrible death of his Uncle Ben , which he believes was partially his fault because he failed to stop a criminal when he had the opportunity. Since that tragic day for Peter, it has guided his every action as Spider-Man, driven to continue in his crusade against crime no matter the price and frequently driving him to make personal sacrifices to accomplish what is right, even if it means losing relationships, opportunities, or peace. Also, one of Spider-Man's most distinguishing characteristics is his sense of humor and wit, particularly during battles. He uses jokes, pop-culture references, and sarcasm to disarm his foes while also masking his inner dread or anxiety. This sense of humor makes Peter a more light-hearted and personable demeanor than many other superheroes, and it acts as a coping strategy for the continual danger and stress of his double life. Despite his powers, Peter is frequently depicted as fragile and emotionally complex. He deals with real-life issues like financial stress, relationship problems, school or work demands, and feelings of loneliness or self-doubt. These human difficulties make him highly relevant and grounded in reality, demonstrating that even superheroes can experience sadness, make mistakes, and cope with difficult feelings. This is also shown in one of Peter's in-game interactions with Peni , who sees him as an older brother figure.

When she asked if she did the right thing by going out every night and placing loved ones at risk, Spider-Man replied that every time he wears the mask, someone has to deal with the bullies and challenges they face. Spider-Man's relationships with major Marvel teams reflect his development as a hero. He gained companionship and mentorship with the Fantastic Four as he is always welcomed as a family by Sue Storm and Reed Richards , With his best friend Johnny Storm and fighting buddy Ben Grimm . There are times that he has recognition and legitimacy as a top-tier hero with the Avengers and mutual respect and understanding with the X-Men and the Guardians , despite not being a member of them. Spider-Man is basically a solitary act, yet his interactions with these teams demonstrate that he is a cherished and appreciated ally throughout the Marvel Universe even with other vigilantes like Punisher , Cloak , Dagger , and Daredevil . He is known as the "Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man", a hero who is not only a protector or symbol of New York, but also represents symbol of hope, resilience, justice in the face of hardship, and the power of doing what's right even when no one’s watching. Trivia [ ] Squirrel Girl's first appearance was in " Marvel Super Heroes " (1990) #8 in January 1992. Squirrel Girl's "Urban Hunter" costume was designed by Janet van Dyne , also known as the superhero Wasp. Doreen's Squirrel-a-gig, her one-man helicopter, can be found at her tree house which is the Attacker spawn at the Central Park map. Squirrel Girl admits of still having a crush on Wolverine , a possible nod to New Avengers (Vol. 2) #7 , where it was vaguely suggested that the two were involved romantically in the past, despite the fact that it was later confirmed it was just a misconception. Some of Squirrel Girl's voice lines has her boasting about defeating Doctor Doom , Thanos and Galactus . This is a running gag in her stories that she has been able to fight and win against some of the most powerful beings in the Marvel universe in one-on-one combat. Among other characters she has defeated include Deadpool , Wolverine, Magneto , M.O.D.O.K. , Terrax the Tamer, Pluto, Fin Fang Foom, The One Below All , and many others. While Squirrel Girl was born with super-powers and a prehensile tail, she's not a mutant. With her third hero story (currently unreleased) being called "X-Gene Test: Positive", it is hinted that the Rivals version of the character could play around this fact. He should typically position in places that force enemies to divert attention away from the rest of his team and instead to him, but far enough from the enemy and close enough to his team that he can easily fall back should things go awry. High ground positions that are close to an objective or flank routes that lone enemies are likely to take are where he shines. It may be tempting to play Star-Lord as an aggressive close-range dive character akin to Black Panther or Spider-Man . However, you should avoid this as much as possible, as he lacks the quick, long distance escape potential to be able to escape from the situations that those characters can.

It may be tempting to play Star-Lord as an aggressive close-range dive character akin to Black Panther or Spider-Man . However, you should avoid this as much as possible, as he lacks the quick, long distance escape potential to be able to escape from the situations that those characters can. As mentioned before, you should learn to strike a balance between taking a position that diverts attention to you and being close enough to your team to secure your escape. Star-Lord's main weapons are his iconic Element Guns. These are essentially fast-firing SMGs, laying down a quick volley of fire that remains effective at close to mid-range, but will need constant reloading due to quickly expending each magazine. As they are sustained fire as opposed to single-fire burst, getting used to tracking will be important to playing the character effectively. Avoid firing at targets at extremely far distances with it unless there is no one else to shoot, as its falloff and spread will make the weapon's damage pitiful at those ranges Stellar Shift is one of Star-Lord's most essential abilities. It essentially serves as a dodge roll, quickly repositioning him a short distance while also offering invincibility frames for its brief duration. It also reloads his guns, making it great for when you need to continue your offense in the midst of a fight. This ability is key to your survival and your ability to take 1v1s. A single well-timed dodge against a high-damaging attack or a quick reload to reduce your downtime is often all you need to come out on top in most fights. You should get used to timing the shift right before a big attack will land in order to drastically increase your survivability. As you have complete invincibility frames, you cannot be damaged at all nor can you be affected by crowd control effects like stuns, seizes, or knockbacks. With enough foresight and quick reactions, Star-Lord can become near-impossible to pin down without severe focus-fire. Blaster Barrage is your primary damaging ability. Star-Lord fires his blasters wildly all around him, dealing damage in a wide AoE around him. This attack can be used even if your Element Guns are out of ammo, making it great as a finisher after expending your magazine.

Blaster Barrage is your primary damaging ability. Star-Lord fires his blasters wildly all around him, dealing damage in a wide AoE around him. This attack can be used even if your Element Guns are out of ammo, making it great as a finisher after expending your magazine. However, note it will not replenish your ammo, meaning that if your magazine was empty before using it, you will still need to reload after it ends. This is also great for warding off enemy flankers and divers, as its auto-hit nature completely nullifies their greatest strength: their ability to dodge. With this ability, Star-Lord is one of the best characters in the game for managing a flank route, as his mere presence will often have flankers thinking twice before attempting to engage. While using this ability, you can still use your Rocket Propulsion or Stellar Shift, or even cancel it early by pressing the ability key again. Rocket Propulsion will allow you to chase a retreating enemy or to keep close to a flier like Iron Man or Storm to continuously damage them, while Stellar Shift will end the barrage early. Cancelling a barrage early either manually or with a shift can allow you to surprise an enemy by hitting them with higher DPS with your main weapons when compared to the low but reliable damage that the barrage offers. Rocket Propulsion allows you to take almost any position you desire while also serving as a decent escape tool with enough foresight. Star-Lord can use his rocket boots to fly around wherever he desires for a short duration, moving at roughly the same speed as Iron Man does during his Hyper Velocity. He can only use this ability while his boots have fuel: if it runs out, he will be forced back down to earth. Galactic Legend is an exceptional ultimate for securing an important fight. Upon activation, Star-Lord will put on a modified helmet and give his rocket boots infinite fuel, allowing him to fly around to his heart's content. With his new helmet, he now has auto-aim on his main weapons that are effective up to 30 meters away, and his weapons' falloff range increases from 10 meters to 25, giving him much more range. He also reloads 70% faster, allowing him to lay down significantly more fire in significantly less time.

This ultimate makes Star-Lord a nightmare when in an open area with little cover, as he can easily shoot down squishy enemies who can't be healed or protected in time. Due to the threat this ultimate offers, it is not uncommon for enemies to withhold their defensive abilities or ultimates until you decide to use it, as your ultimate lacks the damage output necessary to break through these abilities by itself. You should keep track of which heroes and ultimates have been used so you can use yours at an opportune moment, however in some cases it may be worth using your ultimate to force out one of the enemy's, making them more vulnerable for the next team fight. Star-Lord's teamup with Adam Warlock, Leader' Soul, gives him access to Warlock's Regenerative Cocoon ability, functioning identically to how it does with Warlock. It is great for giving extra staying power in a fight, but must be used carefully so you don't waste it on a lost battle. Star-Lord Peter Quill's personality is influenced by his upbringing and the opposing influences of his human mother and alien father, J'son of Spartax. Meredith Quill, Peter's mother, raised him on Earth, and he grew up with warmth, affection, and earthly values, especially Peter's love for classic rock music or songs from the 70s-80s influenced by her mother. His mother's loving spirit instilled in him a strong feeling of loyalty and emotional sensitivity. However, her tragic death while Peter was young left him emotionally damaged and isolated. At a young age, he was trained by a band of space pirates known as the Ravagers, grows up in a harsh, lawless world leading to an upbringing that shapes him into a shrewd, streetwise, and a rebellious impulsive person. Now known as the outlaw named Star-Lord, he learns to live via wit and cunning, gaining a rogue-like charm that combines arrogance, confidence, temper and genuine likability. At the same time, the emotional neglect he experienced caused him to adopt a boastful, humorous and sarcastic exterior in order to conceal his deep-seated abandonment concerns. Peter's father, J'son, is the cold, authoritarian presence in his life, in stark contrast to his mother's tenderness. While J'son provides Peter with power and lineage, he also represents manipulation and control, encouraging Peter to hate and reject his father's goal of empire in favor of defining his own identity.

Quill's relationship with the Guardians of the Galaxy , marks a watershed moment in his emotional maturation.  Rocket , like Peter, masks his pain with sarcasm and aggressiveness, and their relationship is frequently one of mutual taunting and antagonism.  Both are natural leaders in their own right and frequently disagree on decisions, methods, and even little grievances. Rocket's loud, cynical temperament regularly clashes with Peter's more emotive and impulsive leadership style. One example is their argument during their crash on Klyntar regarding the Milano's malfunction. However, there are times that this friction conceals a profound mutual respect and a brotherly tie formed through shared grief, fights, and a shared knowledge of what it means to be shattered and alone. The Guardians are the family Peter never had. Flawed, chaotic, but ultimately devoted bunch that lets him to open up and grow. Through his encounters with them, there are times Peter progressively learns to accept responsibility, be vulnerable, and lead through empathy rather than ego. They become not only his teammates, but also his chosen family. Each member provides something he was missing, such as loyalty, trust, forgiveness, opposition, and belonging. Through them, Peter learns to lead the group in times of space threats, fight for something bigger than himself, and open up emotionally, even when it hurts. Their chaotic, dysfunctional, but fiercely loyal connection is what finally restores Peter to his childhood home and where he is currently learning to be a responsible leader. He is a combination of a charismatic outlaw while being a loyal guardian willing to protect the ones he cared and loved. Trivia [ ] Star-Lord's first appearance was in " Marvel Preview " (1975) #4 in January 1976, though this version was later retconned to be an alternate reality version from Earth-791 . The modern version of Peter Quill debuted in the mainstream Marvel Universe in " Thanos " (2003) #8 in May 2004. Star-Lord is voiced by Scott Porter , reprising his role from Guardians of the Galaxy: The Telltale Series (2017), Marvel Ultimate Alliance 3: The Black Order (2019), and Marvel Future Revolution (2021). Star-Lord listens to classic rock. [ 2 ] He is a fan of Dazzler and Lila Cheney . [ 3 ] Star-Lord's early design was supposed to be based on his comic look which is the color blue and red with the full helmet on. Some of the early concept designs also showed that his character design was supposed to be based off of Michael Jackson's outfit in the Thriller music video. When getting a final hit on his ultimate ability Galactic Legend, Quill says: "Another one bites the dust!". This may be a reference to the song "Another One Bites the Dust" by the British rock band Queen . His interaction with Phoenix mentions Kitty Pryde and asks about her if she remembers him. This refers to Star-Lord and Kitty being lovers in the comics. [ 4 ] During early versions of the game, his first story ended with the Guardians escaping Klyntar by slingshotting their ship on the Celestial's corpse. Since Season 0, the story has been updated and now ends with Star-Lord deciding to stay on the planet and thus the title Quantum Slingshot no longer makes sense. Constant free-flight, granting her high ground advantage to attack enemies from above. Her primary fire, Wind Blade, launches projectiles that can pierce through enemies. Her secondary fire, Bolt Rush, launches a spell field in a straight line that deals area-of-effect damage. Storm's core gameplay revolves around her Weather Control, which grants herself and nearby allies with passive buffs. She can switch between two stances: Tornado and Thunder. She can switch between two stances: Tornado and Thunder. Tornado grants Storm a 16% bonus movement speed, while her allies gain 8%. Thunder grants Storm a 16% bonus damage, while her allies gain 8%. Goddess Boost is a cooldown ability to temporarily enhance the effects of Weather Control for 8 seconds with a 15 second cooldown: Enhanced Tornado increases Storm's movement speed bonus to 40%, while her allies' to 20%. It also slows down nearby enemies by 15%. Enhanced Thunder increases Storm's bonus damage to 30%, while her allies' to 12%. It also summons lightning to strike down at nearby foes every 2 seconds. Her Ultimate, Omega Hurricane, allows Storm teleport to the targeted location and summon a large hurricane around her and deal massive damage to enemies caught in it. When first activated, Storm vanishes from the battlefield and the player has 5 seconds to choose where she'll spawn. Storm can move while in her hurricane. During this ability she gains almost double her max health as bonus health. Weaknesses [ ] Low damage output in general, with both her Wind Blade and Bolt Rush having small hitboxes that require pinpoint accuracy to land. Despite being in constant free-flight, Storm has no access to quick mobility tools like Iron Man or Star-Lord , having to rely on the smaller speed boost from the Tornado Weather Control, even when enhanced. Has no defensive or self-sustain tools outside of her Ultimate. Can still be targeted and taken down during Omega Hurricane. During Omega Hurricane her Weather Control is temporarily disabled. I fight for her. Storm Storm, born Ororo Munroe, is one of the most iconic and respected mutants. As a powerful weather manipulator and a longtime member of the X-Men , Ororo embodies strength, grace, and deep moral conviction. Raised in the shadows of both African and American cultures, Ororo’s upbringing shaped her into a fiercely independent and compassionate leader. Her royal Kenyan lineage and her experiences growing up as an orphan on the streets of Cairo gave her a unique blend of humility and majesty. These early life struggles forged her unshakable will and empathy for the oppressed, making her an ideal protector of both mutants and humans. She is a kind, responsible, and courageous leader with a strong will and motherly character, but she also suffers from repressed anger as a result of a horrific childhood event.  Her strong sense of responsibility motivates her to protect her fellow mutants and advocate for peaceful coexistence with humans, resulting in a pragmatic survivor who is fiercely devoted to people she cares about.

Ororo is recognized for being profoundly empathic, always aware of the pain of others, and frequently serves as a voice of reason and peace within the X-Men. She believes in protecting life and keeping balance, and she handles her powers with reverence and care, rather than hubri and carries herself with regal authority, reflecting both her royal ancestry and her inner discipline. Despite her peaceful demeanor, Storm has a fierce spirit. She is not to be underestimated when pushed; she demonstrates incredible courage, tenacity, and even aggression. Her resolve is unparalleled; even without her abilities, she has proven herself a capable and brave leader. She loves freedom for herself and others, has a strong sense of justice, and is deeply spiritual and linked to nature, all of which affect her worldview and leadership style. And that's why she has a seat in the Quiet Council during the Krakoan era. Storm is considered as a goddess, and for good reason, given her abilities and the cultural backdrop of her origins. The locals in Africa, watching her capacity to bring rain and regulate the weather in a drought-prone region, believed she was a divine being, a true weather goddess. Storm's relationship with other mutants, including Wolverine , Jean Grey , and Professor X , are complex and based on years of shared hardship, trust, and growth. Her relationship with Wolverine is built on mutual respect, battle-tested loyalty, and a knowledge of each other's emotional depths. Logan frequently refers to her as "Ro," a symbol of intimacy and trust that few people experience. With Xavier, she holds him in high regard as a mentor and visionary, but she has also confronted him on several occasions when his principles or actions contradict her own.

And with Jean Grey, they're like sisters. Their relationship is based on empathy, emotional intelligence, and shared leadership among the X-Men. Storm frequently serves as an emotional anchor for Jean, particularly when she is dealing with the enormous burden of the Phoenix Force or her psychic abilities. They have complete trust in one another, and Storm has frequently defended Jean when others were skeptical of her abilities. Jean respects Ororo's moral clarity and natural authority. When Jean is overcome by emotions or cosmic power, Storm is one of the few who can calm her down and talk clearly without fear. Ororo was once married to T'Challa , becoming his queen. Together they ruled the African nation of Wakanda. Their relationship is blend with love, politics, legacy, and personal struggle. Their love story is about passion, power, and sacrifice. Even though they are separated, they are nonetheless equals in power and vision, both rulers in their own way, battling for a better society. And even after their marriage ended, Storm and T'Challa's emotional bond remained strong. They've since worked together as allies, demonstrating mutual admiration and care, yet their relationship hasn't totally reignited.  Whether romantic or platonic in the present era, their link carries weight beyond memories, even from other versions of themselves, representing unity, respect, and the complexity of love in a universe that is continuously at war. Has higher maximum health compared to other Duelists. His passive, Warrior's Gaze, briefly grants the Punisher vision of enemies who disappear out of his line of sight for 3 seconds. This means that players using the Punisher will still see the highlighted silhouette of opponents even if they are behind walls and obstacles.

His passive, Warrior's Gaze, briefly grants the Punisher vision of enemies who disappear out of his line of sight for 3 seconds. This means that players using the Punisher will still see the highlighted silhouette of opponents even if they are behind walls and obstacles. Punisher is able to switch between two primary fire weaponry at will: Adjudication is a long-range automatic rifle that deals consistent rapid-fire damage at a long range. Deliverance is a mid-to-short-range shotgun that packs incredible power at closer targets. It deals higher damage the closer the Punisher is to his targets, and can reliably one or two-shot most standard-health enemies if all shots deal critical hits. His secondary fire, Scourge Grenade, has the Punisher lobbing a smoke grenade that deals a small amount of damage on impact but creates a large smoke cloud that obscures enemy vision. The Punisher leaps backwards when throwing the grenade, making it an effective dodging or spacing tool to widen the gap between him and his opponents, as well as to temporarily disorient them. Combined with his passive, this gives the Punisher a combat advantage as he can still see his enemies even while they are obscured by the smoke screen. Vantage Connection launches a hook with a cable that can attach to any surface, enabling the Punisher to move rapidly through it like a zipline. This ability provides the Punisher with incredible flexibility. It can be used to gain terrain advantage and high ground over his opponents, as well as to perform evasive maneuvers to reposition in combat. The cable persists after fired, allowing players to use it again freely. By manually exiting the zipline earlier by pressing the jump button, players can keep the Punisher's momentum and be slingshot forward and high in the air, granting him excellent mobility to travel very long distances. Culling Turret deploys a stationary armored skull-shaped turret that causes the player to enter first-person view. The turret allows the Punisher to rapidly fire explosive bullets that both deal direct damage as well as explosive damage in a small radius. The bullets fired by the turret are not affected by damage falloff, meaning they will deal full damage no matter how far the Punisher is from his targets.

The turret has no duration, and the Punisher will remain on it until the ability is canceled, upon running out of bullets (200 in total), or if the turret is destroyed. The turret has 600 health and effectively counts as a second healthbar for the Punisher; even if the turret is attacked and destroyed by the enemy team, he will not be taken down. The Punisher can still be healed while mounted on the turret. While mounted on the turret, the Punisher becomes unstoppable and completely immune to all forms of crowd control. This also applies during the transformation. This even includes certain displacement Ultimates, most notably Jeff the Land Shark 's It's Jeff! His Ultimate, Final Judgement, temporarily equips the Punisher with two massive Gatling guns and a shoulder-mounted missile launcher, both with infinite ammo. The gatling gun have one of the highest rate-of-fire in the game, after Star-Lord 's Element Guns. The missiles automatically lock onto the nearest characters, up to three at once. While under the effects of Final Judgement, Punisher becomes unstoppable, completely immune to all forms of crowd control. This also applies during the transformation. This even includes certain displacement Ultimates, most notably Jeff the Land Shark 's It's Jeff! Weaknesses [ ] Despite his higher health, he is still significantly frail, being susceptible to dives and flanking. Vulnerable if both his Scourge Grenade and Vantage Connection are on cooldown. Punisher cannot enter and exit his Culling Turret at will; if the player exits the turret by pressing the assigned button, the turret will disappear and trigger its cooldown. Punisher moves 20% slower (40% while shooting) during Final Judgement.

TBA Strategy [ ] Punisher serves as the game's premier starter damage dealer, with all of his weapons and abilities being very simple but effective. He is a great character for anyone familiar with conventional shooter games like Call of Duty or Counter Strike. Due to his lack of on-demand mobility, Punisher is best played near his team, sticking close to his Vanguards and Strategists so he can lay down continuous damage while staying nice and protected. Adjudication serves as Punisher's primary means of damage. It is a simple but effective assault rifle, being useful at basically any range for getting in damage, however it shines at mid-range. When at a close distance or against a large target, his Deliverance shotgun is often a better choice.

Adjudication serves as Punisher's primary means of damage. It is a simple but effective assault rifle, being useful at basically any range for getting in damage, however it shines at mid-range. When at a close distance or against a large target, his Deliverance shotgun is often a better choice. As with any shotgun, it excels at shredding up-close enemies, and it especially shines against Vanguards, as their large hitboxes will guarantee that most, if not all, of the gun's pellets will connect. While the gun has a standard reload if done from an empty chamber, it can also individually reload shells if there are still shots left. In prolonged combat with the weapon, try to reload in between shots in order to minimize downtime. Scourge Grenade serves as Punisher's primary "get-off-me" tool. Not only does it fire a smoke bomb that briefly obscures enemy vision, but it also causes Punisher to leap backwards, putting some distance between him and the target. This is a great tool for disorienting enemy flankers and taking their favorable engage away from them. If need be, it can also serve as a ranged finisher against an injured target when Punisher is out of ammo, the enemy is behind cover, or if he is otherwise unable to hit them with other means. Culling Turret offers Punisher even more firepower to work with. After a brief set-up animation, Punisher will man a powerful HMG emplacement that fires explosive rounds, giving him incredible DPS and AoE crowd control. While in the turret, he is completely immobile, but is also immune to all CC effects such as stuns, knockbacks, or seizes, and can block up to 600 damage from the front. The turret will disappear if Punisher either manually exits it, expends all of its ammo, sustains too much frontal damage, or stays in it for 20 seconds. This ability is best used as either a deterrent for a push or as a way to punish a team who has committed to a fight. When trying to position the turret, avoid constantly using the same spot over and over. Instead, constantly reposition between vantage points to keep opponents guessing from exactly where the turret's fire will be coming from.

When trying to position the turret, avoid constantly using the same spot over and over. Instead, constantly reposition between vantage points to keep opponents guessing from exactly where the turret's fire will be coming from. While the turret can block all means of damage from the front, Punisher is still completely vulnerable to attacks from behind, making him easy pickings for a flanker when in this state. If the enemy has flankers, make sure to keep an eye and ear open for them. Vantage Connection is Punisher's primary means of mobility. He will fire a grapple line that he can zip along at breakneck speeds to quickly reach alternate positions. After exiting the grapple, Punisher will always leap vertically, allowing him to clear any ledges. Due to its long cooldown and slow start-up, it is unreliable as an on-demand escape option. However, setting up near a grapple can allow you to use it as a quick escape. This ability can only be used when grounded. Setting up grapples near spawn is also a solid choice, as it can allow you to quickly return to a fight after respawning. Punisher's Ultimate, Final Judgement, has him pull out two powerful gatling guns and a set of shoulder-mounted rocket launchers, turning himself into a one-man army. In this form, he has one of the highest damage outputs in the game, shredding through tank and squishy alike, however he cannot use any of his abilities and can instead only move and shoot. It is best to think of this ultimate as a stronger Culling Turret, punishing an enemy team for committing to a push by bombarding them with relentless damage. Keep in mind that Punisher himself does not become any more durable in this form, so be wary of activating this when out in the open, as you will be painting a huge target on your back once the enemy sees you coming. Similar to Culling Turret, Punisher is completely CC-immune during his ultimate, so feel free to challenge anyone who attempts to stun, displace, or otherwise disorient you. Punisher's team-up with Rocket, Infinite Punishment, gives Punisher one of the highest non-ultimate damage outputs in the game, allowing him to turn any sightline into a hailstorm of death.

The Punisher to Cloak Frank Castle, also called by everyone as The Punisher, is a complex and emotionally troubled character motivated by an unrelenting sense of justice and revenge. At his core, Frank is a man shaped by pain, particularly the violent murder of his wife and children, which becomes the defining event of his existence. Before this terrible event, he was a distinguished Marine who was disciplined and dedicated to his nation. However, after losing his family, he evolves into a vicious vigilante, using his anguish and military expertise to carry out a one-man war on crime. His personality becomes grumpy, rigid, compulsive, and unyielding, with little tolerance for moral ambiguity or second chances and no mercy for killing criminals in the underworld like crime bosses, traffickers, gang members and even the corrupt system like the dirty cops. Unlike heroes who may cooperate with law enforcement, the Punisher operates as a wanted fugitive and that varies from most vigilantes like Spider-Man . He is cold-blooded and cruel when it comes to eliminating criminals, yet he cares about the lives of others who are innocent. He is a borderline sociopath who is obsessed with killing criminals; he does not simply solve crimes, but brutally punishes those who commit them. What distinguishes Frank from most anti-heroes is his use of illegal techniques like kidnapping to complete his mission, and he is properly feared and admired by those who know him. Frank views the system as broken and corrupt, feeling that only final, lethal punishment can truly stop evil. This absolutism isolates him from others and contributes to his lone-wolf nature.

Frank views the system as broken and corrupt, feeling that only final, lethal punishment can truly stop evil. This absolutism isolates him from others and contributes to his lone-wolf nature. He believes that criminals are beyond redemption and that the legal system is too corrupt, slow, or inefficient to truly combat evil. In his opinion, punishment must be final death is the sole guarantee that a criminal would not harm anyone again. This black-and-white worldview directly contradicts Daredevil 's ideas. Matt Murdock, both a lawyer and vigilante, is a firm believer in the possibility of redemption and the value of due process. He regards the law, despite its flaws, as an important structure for sustaining order and justice. Frank regards Daredevil's morality as naive and potentially harmful and believes that allowing criminals to live only offers them more opportunities to harm others. Castle's connection with other Marvel heroes is complicated and often contentious as a result of his violent ways and inability to adhere to traditional heroic ethics. He respects Captain America more than almost any other hero - not just as a soldier, but as a symbol of what Frank feels America should be, even when Steve disagrees with Frank's methods. And when interacting with other characters in the roster, sometimes this version of the Punisher takes the task too seriously leading to his dialogue of himself and towards others feels humorous with the extreme “edginess” part of the comic exaggeration of his character. Like when Luna Snow introduces herself as a singer, Frank says he hates listening to music and only focuses on his task in eliminating criminals or bragging about his capabilities such as Magneto in a threatening manner not knowing what Erik will do to him. In recent events, Frank is now an unstoppable force after taking a "knock-off Super-Soldier Serum" that strengthens his abilities, changes his physique, and extends his lifespan, as he resides in the year 2099 , eliminating endless criminals and threats in his way with an access of advanced weaponry. Frank's mentality and skill set combine to make him a persistent, highly dangerous vigilante capable of conducting precise and brutal battle against his targets. Underneath the fury and rage, Frank Castle still grieves and recalls what he has lost.

He frequently displays signs of humanity and compassion for children, empathy for other victims of abuse, and rare moments of vulnerability. Nonetheless, he regards himself as beyond salvation, condemned to a life of violence. A man, in many respects, both tragic and terrifying: once a hero, he is now obsessed by his pain, waging an endless, solo war that frequently blurs the line between justice and revenge to the point he does not fear death. Trivia [ ] The Punisher's first appearance was in " The Amazing Spider-Man " (1963) #129 in February 1974. The Punisher's logo in Marvel Rivals seems to take inspiration from the "demon skull" logo used in " Punisher " Vol. 13 (2022-2023) while Frank Castle leads The Hand. Some of his voice lines mention his war journal, which he uses to record his missions and experiences. It is also a reference to The Punisher War Journal comic series. This version of Frank has taken a serum that has significantly extended his prime and lifespan, allowing him to be active in 2099. In the comics, the mantle of "The Punisher 2099" is held by Jacob Gallows, not Frank Castle.

This version of Frank has taken a serum that has significantly extended his prime and lifespan, allowing him to be active in 2099. In the comics, the mantle of "The Punisher 2099" is held by Jacob Gallows, not Frank Castle. Frank’s alternate 2099 costume in the game is based on Gallows' second armor. Before the game's release, his lore story "Initiation Ceremony", had a different story where Frank teams up reluctantly with Natasha after she tracks him to Shanghai, where he reveals a Doom-controlled freighter preparing to launch a satellite that could lock down Earth’s space routes. His primary attack, Rocky Jab, allows him to make two quick melee punches towards his enemies. His secondary attack, Stone Haymaker, charges up for 2 seconds before delivering lots of melee damage to enemies in front of him. This attack applies to all enemies within range directly in front of him, piercing through enemies. The Thing gains 50 bonus health whenever using the attack, whether he hits an enemy or not. This bonus health quickly decay afterwards. Embattled Leap allows for The Thing to leap from a distance to his allies granting them and himself a 25% damage reduction shield for a few seconds. He can do this twice with a cooldown of 3 seconds inbetween. Each leap has a cooldown of 13 seconds. His Yancy Street Charge allows him to charge forward at a fast pace dealing damage and launching up any enemies caught in the path. When this ability ends he will smash the ground creating a seismic zone that launched up enemies within range and prevents them from using their mobility abilities while inside. He can stop this charge at any point before it runs out to create the seismic zone earlier. The Thing gains 200 bonus health whenever using the attack, whether he hits an enemy or not. This bonus health quickly decay afterwards. His Ultimate, Clobberin' Time, makes him smash the ground that creates a ripple of seismic rocks that travels forward and launches up enemies as well as stunning them for 2 seconds. When paired with Invisible Woman , The Thing gains access to Cooperative Comrades, which when activated converts 100% of damage taken into bonus health for 5 seconds, up to 100. Elsa Bloodstone and Jeff the Land Shark are the only enemy characters who can force the Thing to move, and they must use their ultimates to do so. The Thing Ben Grimm, better known as The Thing from the Fantastic Four , has a personality forged out of pain as heroism, a combination of a gruff, tough exterior and a kind, sensitive heart. He's a tough, no-nonsense character shaped by hardship. Growing up on the tough streets of New York's Lower East Side, particularly on Yancy Street, he developed a gritty determination and a strong feeling of loyalty to those who supported him. His youth there was fraught with suffering, grief, and the need to mature quickly, but it also instilled in him the grit, humor, and streetwise toughness that define him as an adult. This early upbringing shaped him into someone who talks tough, acts tougher, and seldom backs down from conflict.  Ben's sentiments toward Yancy Street are confusing yet extremely emotional since, despite his complaints, he remains loyal to the neighborhood and protective of anyone who lives there. When danger strikes Yancy Street, The Thing is usually always the first to respond, with his signature phrase "It's clobberin' time!", demonstrating that underlying his grumbling is genuine affection and pride. His relationship with her Aunt Petunia also demonstrates his sentimental side. Petunia helped raise Ben after his parents died, becoming one of the few solid and beneficial influences in his tumultuous Yancy Street upbringing.  Despite his rough, monstrous exterior, The Thing has a deeply tender heart. He is fiercely loyal to his friends, especially his family in the Fantastic Four, and often serves as their emotional backbone. Beneath his tough shell, Ben Grimm values connection, joking with teammates and stepping into a protective, big brother role when needed. His bond with Reed is complex, as Reed is both his closest friend and the man responsible for his transformation, earning Ben’s admiration but also quiet resentment. Sue Storm brings out his gentler side, which she has always treated him with kindness, and he responds with deep respect and protectiveness. With Johnny , Ben shares a playful rivalry full of insults and teasing that hides a strong brotherly affection, especially when it truly matters. And around Reed and Sue’s children, Ben becomes a warm and protective uncle figure.

And around Reed and Sue’s children, Ben becomes a warm and protective uncle figure. Now with other heroes like Hulk , their clashes are well-known as Ben often pushes himself to fight the Hulk even when outmatched, refusing to back down because of pride and determination. The relationship between the two is one of Marvel's most iconic rivalries, characterized by a complex mix of professional competition, mutual respect, and underlying empathy. And with Spider-Man , they have a pleasant, bantering friendship. Both deal with hardship through comedy, therefore their conversations are filled with wisecracks and taunting with Ben respects Peter as an underdog who never gives up, and Peter admires Ben's heart more than his power. They've partnered up several times, and while they continually make fun of each other, their friendship is based on genuine trust and affection. Overall, Ben's sense of humor is one of his distinguishing characteristics.  His wit is humorous, sardonic, and occasionally self-deprecating, and he uses banter to disguise his suffering, frequently employing comedy to cope with his anxieties over his monstrous appearance. This combination of hardness and sensitivity makes him one of Marvel's most relatable heroes: flawed, dissatisfied, but determined to do kindness. Thor's gameplay revolves around his passive, Thorforce, which grants him bonus health depending on what type of ability he uses. Thorforce is displayed as icons underneath the aiming reticle. His primary fire, Mjölnir Bash, deals a small amount of damage but has the added effect of instantly replenishing a single charge of Thorforce per successful hit. His secondary fire, Hammer Throw, is a ranged attack of relatively limited distance that can deal damage both when hurled and also when the hammer returns to Thor. Storm Surge is Thor's main mobility tool. It allows him to perform a quick lunge with his hammer in any direction, with the distance and damage increasing the longer it is charged (from 10 meters to up to 20 meters when fully charged). If Thor hits an enemy, they're pushed back and carried alongside the attack. This move is versatile and allows Thor to get in and out of combat easily. It costs one charge of Thorforce. This ability makes Thor formidable to dive at the backline to push Strategists out of position and ensure the team takes them down. It also makes Thor exceptional at defending his allies, as he can also push away enemy team divers attacking his team's own backline. Lightning Realm creates a spell field that deals damage and slows down enemies by 30%. It also restores Thorforce based on the number of enemies hit. Enemies will take damage whenever they cross through the spell field. Awakening Rune temporarily enhances Thor's Mjölnir Bash, turning it into a ranged attack, being his best tool for zoning from a safe distance. This ability lasts for 5 seconds and costs three charges of Thorforce. In addition, Thor deals damage-over-time to all nearby enemies. Thor also gains a larger amount of bonus health than usual. His Ultimate, God of Thunder, has Thor leaping into the air while charging Mjölnir, which creates a spell field in a large radius around him that deals a small amount of damage. It's followed by Thor slamming the hammer down to the ground and dealing high damage. When paired with Angela , he gains access to Thunderstrike Pike, which allows him to hurl a Thunder Spear, which restores Thorforce for each enemy hit. When the ability is activated again, Thor leaps towards the area where the spear hit.

Thor The well-known God of Thunder, Thor is presented as a complex and developing character, combining the qualities of an honorable and gallant prince, and, eventually, a modest and self-aware warrior. Thor is arrogant, proud and stubborn at the start of his story, motivated by a thirst for glory and battle. He frequently behaves rashly, certain in his strength and position as Asgard 's crown prince. His portrayed with a strong sense of duty, honor, and a deep connection to Asgard and its traditions. As the Norse God of Thunder, he speaks in a more archaic, Shakespearean manner like “thee” and “thou” which gives him an almost mythic quality and reinforces his divine heritage. His arrogance, rebellious and desire for war almost caused a disaster, prompting his father, Odin , to exile him to Earth. This exile marks an important turning point in his life, beginning to form his character. He gains humanity, knowledge, and compassion from his experiences on Earth. Thor begins to gain humility, empathy, and a greater sense of duty as he spends more time among mortals. His interactions with people like Jane Foster, and later the Avengers , teach him the importance of compassion and teamwork. With Thor as a founding member of the Avengers, and despite feeling like an outcast due to his mystical background, he passionately respects and values those around him.

Thor, despite his valor, is not perfect.  He can be impulsive, headstrong, and occasionally blinded by pride, which can lead to mistakes in both battle and diplomacy.  His sense of honor can make him stiff, and he has difficulty understanding ideas outside of his Asgardian background.  However, these flaws make him more human, demonstrating that even gods must deal with responsibility, consequences, and empathy. Thor's connection with his family is complex and significant. With his brother Loki , the god of mischief, frequently seeks power and use deception to destroy Thor or Asgard. And Thor, despite being betrayed numerous times, frequently attempts to redeem him. Despite Loki's schemes, Thor sincerely cares for him as a brother. He recognizes the good in Loki, even when others don't, and hopes for his redemption even if it comes at a high personal cost. Their relationship is defined by cycles of betrayal and reconciliation, a bond often fractured, yet it never completely breaks, making their battle tragic rather than hateful: two brothers bound by blood, history, and a love neither can express without pain. With his sister Angela , she originally saw Asgard as an enemy and battled with Thor since she was raised in the realm of Heven rather than with his family. Thor strives to connect with her as the truth becomes clear. Angela stays distant, independent and focused to protect their sister Laussa , but eventually learn to respect one another as warriors and relatives. And with his parents, Thor's connection with Odin, the All-Father, is marked by conflict, admiration, and deep turmoil, whereas his mother figure Frigga is a calming, caring, and nurturing presence in his life. He is fiercely loyal to his friends and family, and his sense of justice is unwavering and is willing to protect Asgard no matter the cost. Despite his growth, Thor’s character is nonetheless defined by flaws. He suffers severe losses, pain, and struggles. These events have left him dealing with remorse, anguish, and a crisis of identity. Thor matures from a brash god of thunder to a selfless protector of the realms who is willing to put others ahead of himself, even sacrificing his desires or status for the greater good.

His primary fire, Encephalo-Ray, is a hitscan attack with high rate-of-fire that deals continuous damage per round and a burst of energy at the end. His primary fire, Encephalo-Ray, is a hitscan attack with high rate-of-fire that deals continuous damage per round and a burst of energy at the end. Imperative: Patch summons a drone on a targeted ally that provides heal-over-time to them and all allies within the displayed radius. Players can track how many allies are being healed by the number next to the icon that appears at the ally being followed by the drone, as well the visible radius of the drone effect (which is also visible to other teammates). Non-Ultron players assigned with the drone will get an icon above their healthbars as an indicator. This ability has no cooldown nor duration, and can be swapped freely between allies. The drone cannot be targeted by enemies nor destroyed. The player assigned with the drone receives higher healing-per-second. His secondary fire, Imperative: Firewall, grants Ultron bonus health, as well to allies within a small radius around him. This ability also affects the ally assigned with Imperative: Patch and all allies within their radius. Dynamic Flight causes Ultron to perform a quick dash in the selected direction and gain 40% movement speed for 8 seconds. This gives Ultron a great reposition or disengage tool to avoid focused fire or divers. His Ultimate, Rage of Ultron, summons various Ultron Drones that bombard Encephalo-Rays alongside Ultron for 9 seconds in a small area. This ability simultaneously deals damage to enemies and heals allies. Ultron becomes unstoppable and gains a small self-healing effect during the entire duration. Ultron can use Dynamic Flight while channeling his Ultimate. When paired with Iron Man , Ultron gains access to Nano Ray, which temporarily enhances his Encephalo-Ray for 8 seconds, channeling a piercing energy beam that simultaneously deals damage to enemies and heals allies. Weaknesses [ ] Very vulnerable in the air, being an easy target if caught in the open. Slow movement speed outside of Dynamic Flight. There is a delay in-between rounds of Encephalo-Ray, resulting in Ultron having inconsistent damage-per-second. In addition, Encephalo-Ray cannot deal critical hits. Lacks any form of burst healing outside of Rage of Ultron. Imperative: Patch has some limitations.

There is a delay in-between rounds of Encephalo-Ray, resulting in Ultron having inconsistent damage-per-second. In addition, Encephalo-Ray cannot deal critical hits. Lacks any form of burst healing outside of Rage of Ultron. Imperative: Patch has some limitations. The drone will disappear if the ally assigned moves away out of Ultron's line-of-sight after 5 seconds. Ultron cannot assign the drone to himself, resulting in very limited self-sustain as he relies on a secondary healer or to stay within the drone's radius on an ally to heal himself. The healing radius becomes smaller the higher the assigned ally is in the air. This means that placing the drone on a flying hero is not very effective to heal the party. Imperative: Firewall has some limitations. The cooldown only triggers after the bonus movement speed effect runs out.
