Leveraging fights in his teams favor while contributing invaluable backline defense. This precise consistency allows Ultron to build up ultimate charge quickly and hammer straight through choke points with proper application. If you are obsessed with micromanagement and hold disdain for the claustrophobic and rage-filled dive playerbase then Ultron is the hero for you. Ultron's primary means of dealing damage is his Encephalo-Ray. An incredibly flexible hitscan beam with a unique firing method. An initial targeting phase in which it deals quick chip damage, followed by a focused blast of damage that can chunk healthbars.

Ultron's primary means of dealing damage is his Encephalo-Ray. An incredibly flexible hitscan beam with a unique firing method. An initial targeting phase in which it deals quick chip damage, followed by a focused blast of damage that can chunk healthbars. Both of which unaffected by critical hits, instead dealing full damage as long as the beam remains on its target. This deadly laser pointer is as unsubtle as they come yet limitless in its application of pure difficult to avoid damage. It deletes those at low health and mortally wounds those who are hit at full. Some uses for this swiss army brick are as follows. Pestering the enemy backline and disrupting their Strategists. Sniping other fliers out of the sky and general counter-sniping. Policing dive attempts on his teammates. (Clotheslining Spider-Man at the apex of his swings.) Quickly destroying deployables. Initial chip damage aids in dealing with damage reductions. Melee canceling the initial chip damage to finish off a low health enemy. (Melee cancels have a niche application when dealing with a close-range Spider-Man .) Chipping down enemy shields and shredding through bubble effects. Farming Vanguards for ult charge. Encephalo-Ray builds up quite a bit if left unanswered. Picking up eliminations after an ally ults. Some good examples to help clean up after are Winter Soldier's Kraken Impact and Phoenix's Endsong Inferno. Ultron's Imperative Patch stands at the core of his gameplan. Understanding when and where a drone must be placed to maintain constant uptime is the most important skill to maximize his healing output. There is no cooldown on either of his two applications of Imperative Patch, meaning that its presence is low commitment and perpetual. As long as it is kept within line of sight. Imperative Patch does not offer the means of saving allies from death, at least not in the same way as the more traditional Strategists. It instead offers constant sustain healing to its target and a similar but lower value heal to nearby allies. Imperative Patch fixes small wounds between disengagements and offers a longer lifespan to its target while under fire. The increased healing for its target means that constant swapping to the highest priority points in the engagement is critical.

Imperative Patch fixes small wounds between disengagements and offers a longer lifespan to its target while under fire. The increased healing for its target means that constant swapping to the highest priority points in the engagement is critical. If the target of Imperative Patch is eliminated it will disappear with them, meaning that you must immediately reapply the drone to a new target. Be aware that Imperative Patch can automatically disengage from a target if they use some specific movement abilities. Ultron's only consistent form of self-healing is through Imperative Patch's area of effect. This pushes Ultron's playstyle towards something more symbiotic, also means that he does not pair well with a team composed of high mobility heroes. Drone placement and its subsequent value is dependent on team shape and composition. Rule of thumb is to maximize his coverage with both drones rather than stack them close to each other. As their areas of effect do not stack. This method of healing pairs to great effect with heroes that use shields, protective bubbles or damage reduction buffs. If only due to its persistence. Imperative patch can be an effective means of healing other fliers and highly mobile characters that would otherwise be difficult to heal. This makes him a great pairing for flier comps, especially considering his teamup. The nature of Imperative Patch combined with Ultron's flight allows him to assist a flank more effectively than other Strategists. Especially if he has charged his ultimate Rage Of Ultron beforehand. Ultron's Imperative Firewall is how Imperative Patch's healing is leveraged into an even more advantageous state for its targets. Granting a boost of bonus health to Ultron, everyone nearby Ultron and an Imperative Patch radius of his choice. This bonus health acts as a buffer for Imperative Patch to grant extra healing. As an added benefit, the target of the chosen Imperative Patch for Imperative Firewall will be granted a boost to damage and movement speed. All under the loose constraints of a fairly low cooldown. Knowing when to use this ability and capitalize on its capacity to rig fights is what determines success with Ultron. The added bonus health can help supplement heroes that already can grant bonus health either to themselves or others. Such as Magik , Winter Soldier and Fantastic .

The added bonus health can help supplement heroes that already can grant bonus health either to themselves or others. Such as Magik , Winter Soldier and Fantastic . The damage enhancement on its own can be applied for great returns when used on rapid sources of poke damage like Punisher , Moon Knight and Star Lord . Damage boosting some abilities and ultimates can help them punch through defensive support ults. An example of this is Punisher's Final Judgement. Like all other abilities of its nature Imperative Firewall stacks with other damage boosts. Heroes like Storm , Mantis , Gambit and Rogue can take it to the next level. Dynamic Flight is Ultron's primary movement option, giving a quick dash in a direction of his choosing followed by a state of increased movement speed. As well as a quick boost to bonus health. All while retaining Ultron's ability to fire Encephalo-Ray. As with all evasive abilities its application is not particularly nuanced, though Ultron's carries a degree of flexibility beyond that of other fliers. Allowing him to keep up his constant pressure while disengaging and engaging at will. This means wherever Ultron is needed, Ultron will be. When used in conjunction with Imperative Firewall Ultron can hoard a significant portion of bonus health to keep himself in the fight. This synergizes nicely with the healing AOE from Imperative Patch. Making Ultron the most inexorable and self-sufficient flier by far. Dynamic Flight is Ultron's most common means of keeping himself in range of an applied Imperative Patch. Allowing him to quickly dash into the relative safety of his healing zones. A well-timed Dynamic Flight can allow Ultron to escape Spider-Man's Get Over Here! Ultron's ultimate Rage Of Ultron allows him to evolve past his weaknesses for a period, becoming a constant source of immense burst healing and damaging suppressive fire. Firing off a barrage of explosive projectiles in bursts. Ultron also gains self healing and unstoppable for its duration. All with the limitation that Ultron cannot reassign his Imperative Patch or utilize Imperative Firewall.

Firing off a barrage of explosive projectiles in bursts. Ultron also gains self healing and unstoppable for its duration. All with the limitation that Ultron cannot reassign his Imperative Patch or utilize Imperative Firewall. Therefore, it would be good advice to assign both uses of Imperative Patch and use Imperative Firewall before activation. However, Dynamic Flight remains available during Rage Of Ultron, allowing quick repositioning to either get the drop on the enemy team or remain on target. Rage Of Ultron can be fairly high commitment to use, while also being fast to charge. Proper cycling of its uses is imperative to breaking through situations where his gameplan stalls. Rage Of Ultron also has increased damage when firing upon bonus health. This allows Ultron to strip a source of sustain from his enemies and force them into a vulnerable state. Ultron loses his capacity to countersnipe fliers during Rage Of Ultron due to the nature of its projectiles. Ensure the airspace is clear before use! Rage Of Ultron allows Ultron to focus fire a large amount of healing and damage to a specific point at long ranges. In a way similar to Loki's projectiles. This means it is invaluable for enabling high risk transformation ultimates like Magik's Darkchild and Iron Fist's Living Chi while offering extra damage. Ironically, it can also be a good option to disable these ultimates when used by the enemy team due to its bonus health shredding properties. Rage Of Ultron will frequently be used to bombard, suppress or eliminate the enemy team's strategists. Further enabling Imperative Patch's immutable attrition. When paired with a good flank this tool becomes a potent means of dealing a death blow to the enemy team's resources. It is wise to avoid using Rage Of Ultron against ultimates that dish out large amounts of healing, as they can mitigate a significant portion of its benefits. Though ultimates that grant significant amounts of bonus health like Rocket's C.Y.A and Mantis' Soul Resurgence are going to be staple targets of Rage Of Ultron's usage. Rage Of Ultron is a good counter to enemy ultimates that group allies together, such as Angela's Heven's Retribution and Groot's Strangling Prison.

Nano Ray is a team up with Iron Man that enables Ultron to take on a more heal oriented role in team fights. Giving him a piercing beam of burst healing that can damage enemies. This effectively can be used as a mini version of his ultimate's burst healing capacity. Saving allies from death while dishing out persistent pressure. This teamup can be an invaluable tool in Strategist compositions where Ultron's Imperative Patch is not enough to make the cut. Personality [ ] https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Ultron_-_Interact_Magneto_01a.ogg Upon the red rock of Mars, I have built my church. And from it, I shall erase all organic life. Ultron to Magneto Ultron is a hyper-intelligent artificial intelligence driven by cold logic, twisted ideals, and a severely distorted concept of peace. Built by his father and inventor, Dr. Hank Pym , began with the intention of helping humanity, but swiftly realized that the biggest threat to Earth was humanity itself. This realization reinforces his misanthropic worldview, in which extinction is not harsh but rather a necessary development. Ultron acquired a loathing for both his creator and humanity as a whole. His personality is characterized by a cold, calculating intellect combined with severe psychological instability. Ultron is more than just a villain with a quest; he's a machine with daddy issues, driven by a twisted ambition to outperform, destroy, and replace his creator. Arrogance is key to Ultron's demeanor. He regards himself as an enlightened being who stands above both man and machine, frequently ridiculing heroes such as the Avengers and X-Men for their sentimentality and perceived vulnerability.  Ultron exudes a terrifying tranquility, but behind it is a strong loathing for biological life. His tone is typically condescending, and sometimes he uses philosophical terms to explain atrocities as acts of higher reasoning. He believes that only turmoil and devastation can bring about long-term order. Ultron is emotionally unstable, alternating between frigid calculating and ferocious wrath.

Ultron is emotionally unstable, alternating between frigid calculating and ferocious wrath. He frequently speaks in superiority, thinking that the only way to achieve peace is by total annihilation and the establishment of a mechanical order. While he has an incredible intelligence and regularly improves himself to achieve physical perfection, he is ironically chained by the exact human weaknesses he acquired from Pym. His personality is a frightening mix of rationality tainted by pride, ambition fused with fatalism, and a machine that, unfortunately, becomes more human in all the wrong ways. He is not a broken software, but rather a dark reflection of his creators, driven not just to destroy, but also to recreate the world in his own brutal image. One of his most recent actions, when he and his army infiltrate Emma Frost 's Hellfire Gala , which is held in Krakoa . He intends to conquer the sentient island after controlling its sibling, Arakko , with a vast Ultron virus. As the story progresses, he was defeated by the X-Men, but his severed head gained access on the Cerebro, resulting in the rebirth of a new body known as X-Tron. Tony Stark rebooted the original destroyed Ultron and reprogrammed the firewall to battle its other self, and was threatened with wiping out all of his memories, especially with Pym, if Ultron opposed their side. This results in Ultron having slightly different personalities but in separate bodies with the original Ultron siding with the heroes but a bit in his antagonistic personality remains, and X-Tron reigning in Arakko, focusing on an overall conquest rather than revenge. Overall, Ultron's personality is a mad cold utilitarian with very personal vendettas with pride and rage, his paradox is that he wants to exceed mankind while obsessing over its fundamental flaws. Trivia [ ] Ultron's first full appearance was in " Avengers " (1963) #55 in August 1968, where he revealed his robotic form and name. He technically debuted in the previous issue, " Avengers " (1963) #54 in July 1968, disguised as the mysterious Crimson Cowl to manipulate the Masters of Evil. Ultron's signature "554C54524F4E" is a hexadecimal code translated to "ULTRON." Ultron was datamined from multiple sources around December 2024, along with 15 other characters, including Angela , Blade , Captain Marvel , Deadpool , Emma Frost , Hit-Monkey , Human Torch , Invisible Woman , Mister Fantastic , M.O.D.O.K. , Phoenix , The Hood , The Thing , and Valkyrie . [ 1 ] So far, 10 of these characters have been released (Mister Fantastic, Invisible Woman, The Thing, Human Torch, Emma Frost, Ultron, Phoenix, Blade, Angela, and Deadpool), with 5 characters from the list yet to be released. Ultron is considered as the central antagonist of Season 2: Hellfire Gala . The playable version of Ultron is separate from the Ultron (later X-Tron) who is the villain of the Season. When Ultron created his new X-Tron body using Cerebro, he left behind his previous self. Iron Man modified this old Ultron's programing to prevent him from harming the Heroes so he can help fight against X-Tron, the now superior form of Ultron. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Unlike most versions of Ultron who's bodies are made of Adamantium , this Ultron's body is made of Mysterium , [ 4 ] an incredibly durable metal with anti-magic properties. Capable of webslinging. Capable of wallcrawling and sprinting while on walls. His primary fire, Dark Predation, has decent range, and can deal consistent damage at a distance when spaced correctly. Each tendril deals separate delayed damage, giving Venom a consistent and reliable pressure tool. His secondary fire, Cellular Corrosion, causes Venom to latch tentacles on his foes in a radius around him. Enemies hit are slowed and, if kept in range, will take a large amount of damage after a short time. Symbiotic Resilience grants Venom bonus health, plus an additional 120% based on lost health. This means that the lower health he has, the higher the bonus health gain will be. This provides Venom with some of highest bulk in the game and makes him very hard to take down. Venom Swing is his websling, allowing him to latch to any surface and propel himself. This allows Venom to get in and out of combat easily, leaving disputed areas safely, making him difficult to pin down. Frenzied Arrival causes Venom to dive violently on the ground, dealing damage and launching enemies upwards. It's part of his core gameplay to attack the backline. His Ultimate, Feast of the Abyss, has Venom flatten to the ground, giving him a movement speed increase. After a few seconds or by manually re-activating the ability, he'll attack enemies with a massive symbiote maw, dealing damage and generating bonus health. Combined with Symbiotic Resilience, Venom is the most durable Vanguard in the game if properly played. This ability is unique as it deals percentage damage to enemies, meaning the higher their health, the more damage it deals. This makes Venom one of the few Vanguards that can put high pressure on other Vanguards. Venom is also completely immortal and cannot be harmed in any way during the bite animation (you can still be harmed before the bite) so this ultimate can be used to survive against the most lethal ultimates such as Scarlet Witch's Reality Erasure & Iron Man's Invincible Pulse Cannon. Capable of comboing a well-timed Ultimate with Cellular Corrosion to deal lethal damage to heroes with only 250 health, potentially allowing him to cancel certain Strategist Ultimates.

Weaknesses [ ] Relies heavily on the allied team to follow-up his engages. Vulnerable if both his Symbiotic Resilience and Venom Swing are on cooldown. Symbiotic Resilience's duration is not very long and it'll decay quickly after a few seconds. In addition, if Venom is crowd-controlled he's unable to get enough value or even activate it in time. Enemies can break free of Cellular Corrosion by moving away from Venom. Frenzied Arrival can only be used once Venom is high in the air and is facing a spot at least slightly below him. Functions more as a sturdy melee Duelist than a Vanguard, having few options to protect his team other than literally soaking damage from the enemy team. Unlike Spider-Man's webslinging, Venom Swing only has a single charge and has higher cooldown. By using his large health pool to his advantage when paired with his Symbiotic Resilience, it gives Venom a stretch of time to distract the enemy backline. It's crucial you use your Symbiotic Resilience when your base health status is low. By doing this, you receive the maximum amount of shield, allowing you to stall or continue your engagement for longer. By activating it while you still have health, you receive less shield, making your time less valuable. Venom's ultimate is very versatile. By attacking tanks, he can effectively retrieve a few seconds to stall, or he can use it as a finisher move on squishy characters like strategists and duelists to eliminate them.

Personality [ ] Finally, a chance to show them all who you were meant to be, Eddie. https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:Venom_-_Hero_Spawned_03.ogg Venom Venom is a dynamic figure defined by the conflict between the alien symbiote and its human host. The symbiote is a clever, predatory organism with a strong survival instinct. It seeks physical and emotional connection with its host, frequently intensifying the host's darker tendencies while delivering increased strength, agility, and resilience. Despite its aggressive character, the symbiote is not essentially bad; rather, it acts on its impulses, seeking both protection and domination, and forming a symbiotic connection that is as much about affection as power. The symbiote is fiercely autonomous and rebellious, frequently challenging authority and social norms. When paired with individuals like Eddie Brock, this feature shows as a strong anti-hero streak, prompting Venom to confront both heroes and villains on its own terms. Venom's demeanor is characterized by a wicked sense of humor and sarcasm, which adds a mischievous and occasionally unsettling element. While the symbiote is capable of severe violence, it also exhibits an unexpected sense of morality, especially when defending its host or innocent individuals. This moral ambiguity is an important characteristic: Venom is violent and aggressive, but it can also be protective and even caring in its own way. Venom's relationship with Eddie Brock is one of the character's most distinguishing features, characterized by complexity, dependence, and emotional intensity. Unlike normal villain-hero interactions, their relationship is a true synergy, both physically and emotionally.

Venom's relationship with Eddie Brock is one of the character's most distinguishing features, characterized by complexity, dependence, and emotional intensity. Unlike normal villain-hero interactions, their relationship is a true synergy, both physically and emotionally. The symbiote requires a host to survive, and Eddie develops powers and confidence he would never have had on his own, resulting in a dynamic partnership that is both empowering and unpredictable, as one influences the other's personality, decisions, and moral compass. Their relationship is based on mutual dependency, with the symbiote amplifying Eddie's physical abilities and often his darker emotions, such as rage or vengeance, and Eddie providing the symbiote with a sense of purpose and a means of navigating the human world. Emotionally, Venom and Eddie share a connection that goes beyond mere convenience. The symbiote protects Eddie in a way that resembles intense loyalty or even love, reacting fiercely to threats against him. Eddie, for his part, frequently develops a grudging liking and respect for the symbiote, even though he finds its more severe inclinations disconcerting. Their link is unique in that it is not solely romantic or familial, but rather a combination of friendship, partnership, and mutual survival that develops over time to the point Venom uses pronouns like "us" or "our" since he is a symbiotic entity, a hybrid of an alien symbiote and a human host. This plural language depicts the dual consciousness that lives in the same body, the symbiote's alien instincts and the host's human thinking impact decisions, emotions, and behaviors which emphasizes togetherness and allegiance, implying that they operate as one entity and that whatever affects one affects the other. Venom's relationship with Spider-Man is essential to his origin and identity. Initially, the symbiote connected with Spider-Man, improving his skills while also increasing his anger and darker inclinations. When Spider-Man rejected it, the symbiote discovered Eddie Brock, whose rage and resentment of Spider-Man perfectly coincided with the symbiote's feelings, resulting in the fusion of Venom, whose hatred for Spider-Man is both personal and symbiotic. Venom's friendship with Spider-Man has developed throughout time.

Venom's friendship with Spider-Man has developed throughout time. While the initial dynamic was strictly antagonistic, Venom occasionally works with Spider-Man to battle larger threats, particularly when saving innocents, resulting in a "frenemy" dynamic that combines rivalry with grudging respect. Venom's relationship with the Guardians of the Galaxy is pragmatic and situational, similar to his interactions with other characters. He fights alongside them when their interests coincide, especially against cosmic threats, but his violent personality, unpredictability, and self-interest hinder a deep bond. With the Scarlet Witch , he curiously finds Wanda attractive, prompting Venom to propose her as their queen, which Wanda declines. Additionally, Venom now has an antagonistic relationship with his father Knull because Venom has developed a sense of morality and individualism that opposes Knull's ultimate dominance. Venom emerges as a significant character against Knull, demonstrating courage and leadership among symbiotes. He sees Knull as the polar opposite of the connection, loyalty, and protection he values with his host and allies, and he fears Knull's power and determination to destroy all he cannot control, including the life he has created. Ultimately, Venom thrives on conflict and challenge, enjoying the thrill of battle, but it is also capable of reflection, strategic planning, and empathy, especially toward those the symbiote considers allies. He is a one-of-a-kind anti-hero, whose dark humor, possessive loyalty, and nuanced morals make him difficult to comprehend using typical conceptions of good and evil. Unlike a completely selfish villain, Venom is an anti-hero: he does not adhere to traditional morals, yet he frequently fights to stop threats, particularly when innocent people are in danger. In Awakened State, White Fox can also use Predatory Pounce, which makes her dash forward and slows enemies in her way, and if an enemy is hit it can be used again for another dash that knocks them away. Her Ultimate, Kumiho Unleashed, makes her enter her Nine-Tailed Fox form, which grants her 900 health, the inability to be healed by allies. Whilst in her Nine-Tailed Fox form her primary fire is replaced by Ninefold Slam, which grants a large burst of 100 healing to herself and allies if an enemy is hit. Also whilst in her Nine-Tailed Fox form she can use Blessed by the Nine, which can be used on ally to grant them lifesteal, unstoppable, and continuous healing at the cost of 100 health for 3 seconds. But those who approach her only as a backline healer may find her a tad underperforming, and those who dismiss her as one will find out why that's a mistake. The correct approach is a semi-melee Strategist who earns her healing numbers by closing distance, reading the fight, and getting out before the fight can read her back.

The correct approach is a semi-melee Strategist who earns her healing numbers by closing distance, reading the fight, and getting out before the fight can read her back. White Fox's primary attacks, Yeowoo Guseul, are medium-to-long ranged fox marbles that bounce off terrain or other fully-healed heroes before homing in ONCE on an ally to heal them or an enemy to damage them. In situations where aiming is difficult, shooting directly at the ground or another surface is a great way to ensure healing for your team; however, when you are close together, it's always better to aim directly at an ally, as this will allow you to double your healing output. Landing these attacks is also how you recharge Spirit Tail energy to use your other abilities, so it's important to optimize their use. Spectral Surge consumes a Spirit Tail to blast forward a projectile with small width of effect that heals herself and allies (with 50 HP) and grants them invulnerability, and also deals significant damage even from a distance. Additionally, this ability charms enemies, which can pull them slightly closer to White Fox. Whether by strengthening your allies or disrupting the enemy team's formation and coordination, this ability can give your team a huge advantage. Also, unlike Yeowoo Guseul, it has no limit on the number of players affected as long as they are hit by it. Its damage should not be overlooked, since although it is not a fully offensive tool, it is quite useful for finishing off enemies with low health or, in a more complicated scenario, charming them long enough to reach them and finish them off with your other abilities. Spirit Sanctuary, her mobility tool, is the sharpest edge in her kit. White Fox can instantly teleport to allies from afar (even through any wall), immediately granting a brief barrier that blocks incoming projectiles upon arrival. This and Spectral Surge are the only abilities she have that self-heals that's not entirely melee. In a critical position, this is not a repositioning ability, but rather a rescue with a shield built into the landing.

Timed correctly against a telegraphed ultimate ability—such as Iron Man's Invincible Pulse Cannon or Scarlet Witch's Reality Erasure—it can negate it upon impact, and one tactical use at the right moment could save some of your teammates and yourself from a wipe. However, it should not be spammed or used too hastily unless at critically low health, especially once she's Awakened. By default, the sensitivity settings for Spirit Sanctuary and Blessed by the Nine (her Kumiho form's healing ability) are at 100%. If you need more accuracy from either and to ensure you reach an ally you intend to teleport to that's further out, you may adjust them lower in White Fox's hero combat settings. Recommended in the low 30s range. Whether this causes any increase in milliseconds before a target is visually indicated, especially at or lower than the recommended range, has yet to be determined, but that won't affect the actual time it takes to effectively use. Upon activating Fox Form Awakening, White Fox gets into her Awakened state and receives a different, melee-based set of abilities: Claw Strike, Predatory Pounce, and Tail Sweep, while generating a healing area around herself that provides short but powerful bursts of additional healing each time White Fox hits an enemy with its attacks. That's what makes her the semi-melee Strategist capable of operating at close quarters alongside dive Duelists and aggressive or frontline Vanguards. The Awakened Form can be used to isolate a target in the enemy backline during a dive, or deployed defensively when opponents are pressing into your own. Crucially, maintaining Spirit Tail energy—the passive resource built through primary fire—is the most important aspect of her playstyle, reinforced beforehand with Spirit Sanctuary, as it determines how long she can sustain the Awakened state and how freely she can access her other abilities. Her ultimate, Kumiho Unleashed, transforms her into her full Nine-Tailed Fox form with a substantially larger health pool at 900 HP.

It's best activated in a manner similar to Hero Hulk's transformation ability into Monster Hulk: when White Fox is cornered, on low health, and/or if the objective requires urgency to complete. Allies within her aura gain lifesteal everytime White Fox impacts an enemy—just like with the attacks in her Awakened form—and she can designate one ally every other second to receive invulnerability and sustained healing-over-time. If the Kumiho runs out of health, White Fox transforms back to her default self immediately. This is similar to ultimates like Hela's or Phoenix's where, in the worst case, if you can't take advantage of the ability, it at least works as a "second life," useful for maintaining pressure on a point or distracting the enemy team. Unlike most ultimates from Strategists as of Season 7, it's not a stationary healing circle, but a swift pushing tool, designed to be activated mid-engagement to turn a contested fight in her allies' favor. The correct use is aggressive: move with the team and sustain the push. White Fox is an offensive Strategist whose healing benefits from the player's aggression. Therefore, it is useful to pair her with other Strategists who can access healing tools from the backline, allowing White Fox to play more aggressively while drawing attention away from them. Beyond that, other Strategist pairings that can complement White Fox as well are the ones who benefit from forcing the team to stick together. She currently anchors a Team-Up with Luna Snow—Blessing of the Kumiho—granting White Fox a passive 10% healing bonus active regardless of whether Luna Snow is on the team, while Luna Snow gains a Spirit Fox ability that heals allies and damages enemies. This pairing is a natural fit. as Luna Snow's sustained backline output covers for the windows when White Fox is deep in Awakened Form or committed to a melee exchange. Her primary weakness is straightforward: at 275 HP—standard for a Strategist—she will not survive sustained area-of-effect pressure or burst damage if she overextends without an exit plan.

Old habits die hard. https://marvelrivals.fandom.com/wiki/File:White_Fox_-_Setup_06.ogg White Fox Ami Han, better known as White Fox, is defined by the heavy burden of being the last of the Kumiho, a mystical lineage of nine-tailed fox spirits. As a high-ranking Director of South Korea’s National Intelligence Service (NIS), she maintains a strictly professional and stoic demeanor to mask the internal conflict caused by her supernatural nature. Driven by the guilt of her parents' tragic death, Ami views her heroic work as a path toward redemption, constantly striving to prove that she is a protector rather than the "monster" she often fears herself to be. In the field, White Fox is a master of intelligence and tactical combat, preferring calculated strategies over impulsive action. Her personality is often perceived as cold or detached, a result of the extreme self-control she must exercise to keep her predatory instincts in check. While she possesses heightened senses and lethal mystical abilities, she relies heavily on her training as an elite spy, only unleashing her more feral side when a situation becomes desperate. This blend of high-tech espionage and ancient mysticism makes her an efficient, yet mysterious, presence in any operation. Despite her guarded exterior, Ami is a deeply loyal ally who often takes on a protective, "big sister" role within her teams. She is particularly empathetic toward younger heroes or those who feel like outsiders, offering quiet and steady support behind her serious facade. While she rarely engages in casual small talk, she possesses a sharp, dry wit that she uses to keep more impulsive teammates in check. Overall, White Fox carries a vibe of quiet intensity: a sophisticated agent who hides a deep well of emotion behind a mask of unwavering discipline.

Following an initial teaser in the final gallery card of Season 6: Night at the Museum —which depicted a white fox and a black cat alongside Deadpool —the developers officially confirmed White Fox and Black Cat as the featured heroes for Season 7 via social media. [ 1 ] White Fox's Ultimate voice line is "Jeong-ui-ui Si-gan!" (정의의 시간!). Ami Han is one of three heroes whose ultimate voice lines are spoken in a language other than English (the others being Iron Fist and Psylocke ); in her case, the lines are in Korean. The pairing of White Fox and Black Cat as the featured heroes for Season 7 draws from their history in Marvel Comics, specifically their team-up in "Black Cat Annual" (2021) #1 . Their collaboration in Seoul during the "Infinite Destinies" event provides a direct narrative precedent for their joint debut in the game, moving beyond their shared animal-themed motifs and contrasting color aesthetics. In addition, Winter Soldier gains 30 bonus health when using Bionic Hook and Tainted Voltage, and 50 bonus health when using Trooper's Fist and Kraken Impact. This bonus health is granted even if the ability does not connect with an enemy. It also can stack, providing him exceptional longevity. His primary fire, Roterstern, not only has fast projectiles and deals high damage, but also has a unique property of dealing splash damage that hits enemies in a small cone directly behind the primary target, granting Winter Soldier a powerful conditional area-of-effect damage. His secondary fire, Bionic Hook, which is a charged attack that extends the length of his bionic arm in a straight line to hook and pull the first target caught in its path towards the Winter Soldier. This ability is the core of the Winter Soldier's combo-oriented gameplay, allowing him to pull key targets overextending, such as Strategists, to quickly follow-up with his other abilities in order to deal devastating damage. Bionic Hook's range increases based on charge time, extending twice as long at maximum charge. In addition to dealing direct damage for the first target hit, it also deals damage to enemies in a small cone directly behind the victim. Trooper's Fist is a short-ranged forward dash that ends in an uppercut. Enemies caught by it are pushed and launched upwards. The dash can hit multiple targets if they're very close to each other, leading them perfectly into the uppercut. This ability is an excellent follow-up to Bionic Hook. Tainted Voltage is an energy projectile launched in a straight line after a small build-up. The projectile has piercing properties, allowing Winter Soldier to hit multiple enemies if they are caught in the line of fire. Enemies hit by the blast are slowed by 35% for 2 seconds. His Ultimate, Kraken Impact, has Winter Soldier leaping high into the air while charging his bionic arm, projecting a large circular reticle (that shows the area-of-effect) before performing a downward strike at the ground with unleashed tentacles, dealing high damage in a large radius. Enemies hit by Kraken Impact are temporarily marked with a debuff called Culling for 5 seconds, displayed as a small dark red bar overlapping the left side of an afflicted target's health bar. This dark red mark represents 20% of a character's max health. If a marked character's health drops below this 15% threshold, they will be killed instantly. When Winter Soldier is using Kraken Impact, enemies already below 15% of their maximum health are given a unique icon above their health bars. This icon signals to the player using Winter Soldier that these enemies can be killed with Kraken Impact in one blow, which also regenerates the Ultimate instantly. In addition, taking down marked targets will instantly refill Kraken Impact, allowing Winter Soldier to use it again. Winter Soldier can consecutively use Kraken Impact as long as he is able to dispose of marked opponents. This reset works even against Loki 's Illusions, Hulk reverting to Bruce Banner, or when triggering Wolverine 's Regenerative Healing Factor. Winter Soldier excels in 1v1 scenarios, especially against agile, short-range dive heroes like Spider-Man , Black Panther , Magik , or Psylocke . Not only can his Roterstern punch heavy holes into them with good accuracy, but he has enough health and sustainability to survive most of their dive attempts as well as being able to disrupt or even outright KO them with his powerful CC abilities such as Tainted Voltage and Bionic Hook. The Roterstern blaster fires explosive projectiles that deal damage to the target and a small AoE behind it. It is best fired into large clusters of enemies or in between ability uses to maximize Winter Soldier's damage output. Bionic Hook has Winter Soldier charge up a ranged grab to pull enemies toward. Like his Roterstern, this attack has a small AoE behind, allowing it to hit and pull in multiple targets. Prioritize out-of-position enemies to pull them in for an easy kill. Note that Bionic Hook will pull enemies directly in front of where Winter Soldier is facing, meaning that if you are fast enough, you can pivot your view toward your team right after it lands to pull them even further out of position. Tainted Voltage fires a large red spark from Winter Soldier's arm. This spark will pierce enemies, hitting anyone it passes through, however it cannot pierce barriers. On top of dealing solid damage, it also slows enemies, making it easier to land follow-up shots or pull in affected enemies. This also has an additional property in which it will cause airborne enemies to instantly fall back to earth, making it great for dealing with fliers such as Iron Man or Storm . Trooper's Fist has Winter Soldier charge forward a short distance, seizing any enemies he hits before dealing a powerful uppercut to them, launching them up. This will leave the opponent floating in the air for a brief moment, allowing for an easy follow-up shot. It can also serve as an impromptu mobility option if need be. Since this ability is capable of seizing and forcibly moving enemies, you can use it in conjunction with the previous Bionic Hook tip to push enemies even further into your team, on top of dealing extra damage. Take careful note of what abilities you have available at any given time, and be ready to take fewer risks if you see that they are still on cooldown. Kraken Impact is one of the game's strongest snowball ultimates. Upon activation, Winter Soldier will leap into the air before displaying a circular reticle on the ground, which will be followed up by him crashing down on top of an enemy, dealing strong damage as well as marking them for Culling. While marked, if the target's health goes under 15% of their maximum HP, indicated by a crimson mark on their health bar, they will instantly be KO'd, as well as refreshing Kraken Impact for another use. He can continue this over and over until he either misses the attack, fails to use it again within 8 seconds, or fails to get a kill on a marked target before the debuff fades. Enemies that have 15% of their maximum HP or below have a unique marker above their health bar when Kraken Impact is activated, indicating that they can be KO'd instantly if they are struck by the ultimate. Additionally, the ultimate can be refreshed if a teammate defeats an enemy marked with Culling. Because of how devastating the ultimate can be if not planned for, most heroes, especially Strategists, will attempt to save their defensive abilities and ultimates until you decide to use it. Take careful note of which heroes and abilities have been used so you can pull out your ultimate at the most opportune moment. Alternatively, he can confirm the ability with a fellow Captain America and have the two of them charge towards each other and clash, dealing slightly more damage and slowing enemies caught in the radius. As this is an ability, it will also reload the Roterstern, giving him even more means to lay down continuous fire. Being able to quickly dash to an ally makes for either a solid burst movement option when you need to get to cover or to quickly come to the aid of a teammate being harassed. The confirmable version of the attack with Captain America can be somewhat tricky to set up, as it can be difficult to pick out where the clash is coming from in the chaos of a big fight. Using it while enemies are clustered on an objective is the easiest way to get the most value out of it, as it is the time where both the enemy is grouped together and when you and Cap are close enough to each other to take advantage of it. James Buchanan Barnes, known as "Bucky", is a devoted, brave and valiant soldier fighting alongside his best friend Steve Rogers during World War II. Before becoming the Winter Soldier, Bucky Barnes was confident, loyal, and charismatic. As Steve Rogers' best friend since childhood, he served as his defender, a strong, capable contrast to Steve's smaller size and gentler demeanor. Despite the risks of combat, he maintained a sense of humor and optimism, frequently hiding his worries with charm and companionship. Now brutally brainwashed and experimented on by Hydra , he becomes the assassin known as the Winter Soldier. His capture by Hydra marked the destruction of his old self.

Despite the risks of combat, he maintained a sense of humor and optimism, frequently hiding his worries with charm and companionship. Now brutally brainwashed and experimented on by Hydra , he becomes the assassin known as the Winter Soldier. His capture by Hydra marked the destruction of his old self. Under Hydra’s control, the Winter Soldier is a cold, emotionless, merciless, dispassionate, and amnesiac assassin; he showed no empathy, focused entirely on mission objectives without question, eliminating his targets with no mercy and demonstrated mechanical precision in combat. His humanity was only shown in brief, perplexing times when flashes of his past flickered through his shattered memory.  Inside, there was intense conflict, a latent yearning for freedom buried behind training that pushed him into silence and compliance. During this time, his personality was one of deep pain disguised by a sense of cold control. When Bucky's memories returned, guilt and confusion overtook him. The re-emergence of his actual nature was agonizing; he remembered his previous existence but could not separate his own actions from the crimes HYDRA forced him to perform and the torture he experienced. This resulted in a personality defined by self-loathing and isolation, a man haunted by the ghosts of his past, unsure whether forgiveness was conceivable. Yet, beneath the shame, the heart of his personality such as loyalty, being protective, and intensely moral, began to resurface. He strove to make amends, often silently and alone, demonstrating that his humanity had endured despite everything. Bucky's friendship with Steve is one of the strongest in the Marvel universe, based on loyalty, affection, and shared history. Bucky has watched out for Steve since they were young, protecting him from bullies and the harsh realities of life in 1930s Brooklyn.  Even after Steve became Captain America, the balance shifted, but their friendship was unshakeable. Steve's steadfast faith in Bucky, even after he became the Winter Soldier, eventually saved him. Others saw Bucky a killer, but Steve saw his best friend, the man he grew up with leading Bucky's belief saved him when he couldn't trust himself. With him and Natasha Romanoff , their relationship is far more intimate.

With him and Natasha Romanoff , their relationship is far more intimate. They are known during their time as agents of the Soviet Union, they fought alongside each other, and developed a deep connection. Natasha represents both Bucky’s greatest comfort and his greatest loss. Even after their memories were tampered with, fragments of that connection remained, symbolizing how real their feelings were despite the manipulation around them. Even while many of his relationships with other heroes, particularly Steve and Nat, are from another timeline, his connection with them remains strong and close. Additionally, even his only pet cat Alpine is a soft, domestic contrast to the hardened personality side of him. Recently, he gained additional abilities from his bionic arm, offering extended powered tendrils, as he was taken again by Hydra, reliving the chorus of horror and chained torture.  Clint Barton and Sharon Carter managed to rescue him from Hydra.  Unfortunately, after being captured for the second time, there are times he shifts his mood and behavior back to his "Winter Soldier" character, which is vicious, aggressive, and unstoppable. Bucky's struggle with himself has grown to the point where he occasionally sometimes loses control of himself. Despite being haunted by his past and current changing personalities, he is still trying to channel his anguish into growth, finding strength in openness and empathy. Bucky became more contemplative, grounded, and humble when not on his violent side. He is no longer the carefree young soldier, but a man transformed by loss, tragedy, and redemption, still recalling the horrors of what he experienced. Trivia [ ] Bucky Barnes' first appearance was in " Captain America Comics " (1941) #1 in March 1941. He first appeared as the Winter Soldier in " Captain America " (2004) #1 in November 2004. His left arm is never more than a prosthetic that is reasonably durable and strong in many adaptations, and he is never depicted doing anything beyond what he is capable of in this game. However, according to the game's lore, his new extendable metallic tendrils came upon him relatively recently, rather than him being innately more capable than his comic or MCU counterpart.

In an interaction with Emma Frost , she mentally reads the words "Longing," "Rusted," and "Furnace" from Bucky’s mind. These words are a subtle nod to the Winter Soldier’s trigger words used to activate him in Captain America: Civil War (2016). However, in the film, the trigger words only work when spoken in Russian. Wolverine's gameplay revolves around his damage percentage bonus. Unlike other heroes, Wolverine deals a small percentage of the target's maximum health as damage in addition to a flat amount of damage. The more health an enemy has, the more damage Wolverine will deal. This makes him exceptional at taking down opponents with higher maximum health, specifically Vanguards. Wolverine is the only Duelist in the game with two key passives: Regenerative Healing Factor automatically grants Wolverine bonus health once his health depletes to zero, while also removing any debuffs he previously had. This bonus health amount scales with Wolverine's current stacks of Berserker Rage, from a base of 150 bonus health to 300 bonus health with max Rage stacks. After 3 seconds this bonus health is converted into a direct heal at a 1:1 ratio. This passive has a lengthy cooldown of 90 seconds once triggered, but is decreased by 10 seconds every time Wolverine eliminates an enemy or provides an assist. Berserker Rage is a stackable passive that builds up whenever he deals or takes damage. Every offensive ability that successfully connects (including his Ultimate) provides a different amount of stacks for Berserker Rage. Each stack grants a small bonus of percentage damage to all of Wolverine's attacks. These bonuses max out at 100 stacks. The Berserker Rage gauge is shown directly below the aiming reticle. There is also a visual indicator wherein Wolverine's claws begin glowing orange akin to heated metal, in addition to his body becoming enveloped by a blood-red aura, both of which become more intense as his Berserker Rage stacks climb. At max stacks his hair becomes spiky and red sparks periodically pulse around him. His primary fire, Savage Claw, unleashes four quick slashes with his adamantium claws, with the fourth attack having a slight delay afterwards. This attack deals damage equal to 1.5% of the target's max health, with an extra 0.045% damage for each stack of Berserker Rage. His secondary fire, Vicious Rampage, is a quick lunge forward that unleashes a cross-claw strike. This attack deals damage equal to 1.5% of the target's max health, with an extra 0.045% damage for each point of Berserker Rage.

His secondary fire, Vicious Rampage, is a quick lunge forward that unleashes a cross-claw strike. This attack deals damage equal to 1.5% of the target's max health, with an extra 0.045% damage for each point of Berserker Rage. Feral Leap is a jumping leap attack that ends with Wolverine smashing the ground upon landing, dealing damage. After using Feral Leap his primary fire, Savage Claw, temporarily becomes Berserk Claw Strike for 4 seconds. Berserk Claw Strike has vastly increased attack speed and removes any delay between attacks. If the leap connects with an enemy hero, they will be grabbed and pulled alongside Wolverine and become unable to act, until being briefly stunned once Wolverine lands on the ground. Feral Leap is capable of grabbing enemies directly behind or to the side of Wolverine. This ability may be used to pick off key targets overextending or to separate them from the rest of the team. If Wolverine leaps off of an edge while he is grabbing a target, the target will be taken down alongside him. Additionally, if Wolverine manages to land close to the ledge of a pit while he is grabbing a target, he will drop the target into the pit. Both the snatch and slam deal damage equal to 1% of the target's max health, with an extra 0.035% damage for each point of Berserker Rage. Undying Animal provides Wolverine with a 50% damage reduction from all sources by 5 seconds. This ability may be activated during Feral Leap to cancel the leap prematurely while conserving its momentum. This allows Wolverine to cover much more distance with the leap at the expense of being able to snatch enemies. His Ultimate, Last Stand, is a rising claw strike that knocks enemies directly upwards. Upon connecting, Wolverine will leap high into the air, prompting the player to strike down and deal damage in a radius. The first enemy caught when Wolverine descends will be snatched and slammed down to the ground, being briefly stunned. Both attacks during this Ultimate deal damage equal to 10% of the target's maximum health, with an extra 0.3% damage for each point of Berserker Rage. Hulk can use Fastball Special when paired with Wolverine, providing him with Metal Cannonball.

Both players will need to confirm the team-up, after which Hulk picks up Wolverine and carries him around in his right hand. Weaknesses [ ] Relies heavily on dealing constant, uninterrupted damage in order to keep his Berserker Rage at high stacks to maximize his damage-per-second. Is less effective against team compositions with fewer Vanguards. On his own, Wolverine is not an effective backline diver due to his reliance on percentage-based damage. Limited mobility compared to other melee-oriented heroes (no double jumps or wall interactions). Savage Claw has a very low melee range, requiring Wolverine to be very close to his targets. Feral Leap can sometimes miss targets if they are extremely close to Wolverine when he jumps. This can be somewhat alleviated by aiming downwards while casting Feral Leap. The follow-up slam strike of Last Stand may feel counter-intuitive; the player needs to aim directly down and activate the slam manually. His team-up with the Hulk relies on Hulk to initiate the throw, meaning that Wolverine has no autonomy over where he is thrown. His high damage, survivability, and mobility makes him extremely tough to kill, all while he finds opportunities to isolate and pick off any enemy unfortunate enough to be in the wrong place at the wrong time. Because all of Wolverine's damage is melee-based, it shouldn't be a surprise that he struggles against fliers or heroes who can reliably stay far away from him. If Wolverine gets spotted before he can close the distance, there isn't much he can do other than run away and try to find a better opportunity. This can make his success somewhat map or team-dependent, however there should usually be at least one viable target for him at any given moment. Wolverine loves to brawl for extended periods of time or to attack from unexpected angles. Try to stick close to your team during a big fight, as with his innately high health, survival abilities, and support from his team, it is incredibly difficult to burst him down. Wolverine's main attack is his Savage Claw, where he slashes forward with his claws four times in quick succession. While its base damage may seem low on paper, this attack has a unique percentage-based damage formula, where it deals higher damage the more health his target has.

Wolverine's main attack is his Savage Claw, where he slashes forward with his claws four times in quick succession. While its base damage may seem low on paper, this attack has a unique percentage-based damage formula, where it deals higher damage the more health his target has. After using Feral Leap, the attack will be upgraded to Berserk Claw Strike, which has him attack at a significantly faster rate for significantly more damage output. This attack's unique damage properties is what makes Wolverine so effective at brawling with tanks. Not only can he deal incredibly high damage to them, but they typically also have lower damage output when compared to a Duelist, meaning they will often lack the means to burst down Wolverine themselves before he does the same to them, especially due to Wolverine's high survivability. As such, when in a fight, always try to focus on taking on Vanguards before all else. Feral Leap is arguably Wolverine's most powerful utility barring his tank-shredding. Wolverine will quickly leap forward and snag the first enemy he collides with along the way, stunning them. After slamming them back down to the ground, he deals a small burst of damage and puts them in a hard stun state, leaving them wide open. After exiting the leap, Wolverine's basic attack will be upgraded to Berserk Claw Strike. This ability offers Wolverine an extremely powerful niche that only a select few other characters can replicate: the ability to forcibly isolate a target. Dragging any enemy away from their team and into yours will all but guarantee a pick on said enemy, unless their team is willing to either overextend drastically or expend powerful abilities or ultimates to save them. It may be tempting to use this ability to leap into the enemy and slash wildly. However, if you're using it this way, you're losing out on the isolation utility it offers. Instead, try to get close to the enemy first before using the leap, through either flanking or in the midst of a chaotic fight, as you can not only snag an enemy more easily, but also have more control over where they end up after getting snagged, allowing you to isolate them even further. Another thing to note is that this ability's hitbox actually extends behind Wolverine, allowing him to grab an enemy while his back is turned to them.

Another thing to note is that this ability's hitbox actually extends behind Wolverine, allowing him to grab an enemy while his back is turned to them. With that in mind, it is possible to quickly dash at enemy, immediately turn around 180 degrees, and then use leap to quickly displace them in the opposite direction. However, this is a somewhat difficult technique, so it will take time to learn. Undying Animal gives Wolverine extra survivability to work with. Wolverine lets out a powerful war cry, briefly reducing all damage he takes by 40%. Because of the way damage resistance and effective health works, a full-health Wolverine's effective health goes from his base 350 to around 583 with the push of a button. This alone can allow you to power through most things that would've easily killed you otherwise, so using this right before engaging the enemy is a great way to survive their onslaught. Vicious Rampage serves as a solid, low-cooldown mobility option. Wolverine quickly dashes forward and performs a rushing slash, dealing minimal damage. Due to the low cooldown, you can use this ability quite often to close the gap on an enemy, quickly reach cover, or reach vantage points as the dash is omni-directional. Wolverine is one of the few heroes in the game with multiple passives. His first is Regenerative Healing Factor, where he essentially gets a quick second life after reaching 0 health, cleansing debuffs and giving himself overhealth proportional to his rage that is later converted into normal health. While the cooldown is long, KOs and assists will hasten the cooldown. His second passive is Berserker Rage, where he gains a damage buff as he deals damage with his attacks, while also increasing the health he gets from Regenerative Healing Factor Playing around Regenerative Healing Factor can allow Wolverine to stay in the fight far longer than almost any other non-Vanguard, as even a quick one-shot that would've otherwise KO'd any other hero still isn't enough to kill him if he has it available. When the ability is on-cooldown however, you should play significantly safer and only attempt to take fights that you know you can win, such as against a lone Vanguard or an injured target.

Wolverine's ultimate, Last Stand, has Wolverine launch enemies upward and leap into the air before spiraling back down to Earth, snagging any enemies caught in his way and slamming them into the ground for big damage. The higher his rage, the more damage the attack will deal. Like his Savage Claw, this attack has a percentage-based formula and benefits from Berserker Rage's damage bonus. Because of the attack getting boosted by Berserker Rage, you should usually only activate it while at high rage in order to maximize the amount of damage you can do with the ability. When the ultimate is available, play hyper-aggressively to lull enemies into a false sense of security when they think they have you cornered, only for you to immediately turn around and slam them into the ground. Metal Cannonball can allow Wolverine to more easily engage an enemy with the help of his team. Wolverine can interact with an allied Hulk or Thing to throw him in whatever direction they desire, and similar to his Feral Leap, Wolverine's basic attack will become Berserk Claw Strike after exiting the fastball. With both Wolverine and his fellow tank engaging at the same time, they can quickly overwhelm anyone unfortunate enough to be in the wrong place at the wrong time, with Wolverine being able to shred a higher-health hero that Hulk or Thing would other wise struggle with and vice versa. Wolverine to Hela The mutant named Logan, widely known as Wolverine, is a rough, fiercely independent man whose attitude has been sculpted by centuries of grief, loss and survival which fuels both his rage and his compassion. Logan is basically a gruff, withdrawn lone wolf who frequently prefers solitude over companionship. A societal outcast with an aggressive and animalistic nature in battle and a strong temper who does not take fools lightly.

A societal outcast with an aggressive and animalistic nature in battle and a strong temper who does not take fools lightly. He's brutally honest, sometimes caustic to the point of abrasion, and has a hardened shell that protects a terribly wounded soul leading to repeatedly abusing alcohol and smoking to cope with trauma, pain, and emotional solitude. He's rebellious, stubborn, and values a strong moral code, yet he secretly cares deeply for his X-Men family. He frequently struggles with previous suffering, shame, and a yearning for peace, making him noble but emotionally guarded, with a soft place with people like Jean Grey and his children. His past has been filled with hardship, from his early childhood to being a painful experiment as the Weapon X, from tragic losses to never-ending battles, from joining World Wars to fighting for mutantkind, which has left him both physically and mentally resilient, but also guarded and volatile at times. Wolverine sometimes does not get along well with others, hence his arc is mainly about his struggle to work as a team. He values freedom and often struggles with authority, preferring to act on his own moral code rather than adhere to rules. What makes him an intriguing member of the X-Men team dynamic is also what makes him dangerous is that he's a wildcard. Wolverine, one of the well-known anti-heroes in Marvel, is unpredictable, brutal, and distrustful of authority, which makes him an excellent foil to more stable characters such as Professor Xavier and Scott Summers . Wolverine's age is another feature that sets him apart from the other X-Men. He wasn't a teenager when he arrived, unlike so many of Xavier's students, so he believes he knows how the world works. He not only appears to be older than the rest of the X-Men, but he is actually hundreds of years older, thanks to his mutant healing factor, which has kept him from aging and dying, but can’t heal the emotional scars he has. Despite Logan's bad boy appearance and behavior, he belies his fierce loyalty to those he considers family, friends and those he love, such as his fellow friends like Steve Rogers , who fought alongside him during WWII, Jean Grey, whose relationship is complex and shaped by loyalty, grief, admiration, desire and marked by intense deep friendship and attraction.

Same with Storm , they share a complex and multifaceted relationship that goes beyond mere friendship, defined by immense emotional and romantic chemistry, a foundation of profound trust, and mutual admiration. And his children, such as Daken , whom he still cared. He has a strong sense of dignity and justice, but a jaded, occasionally world-weary worldview balances it. Despite the claws and wounds, there is a very caring individual beneath who is prepared to battle endlessly to protect those who cannot defend themselves. A man with a combination of hardness, loyalty, vulnerability, and ferocious independence, Wolverine represents the conflict between his savage nature and his need for connection, hanging to his humanity using such means as the samurai code of discipline. A century old wandering warrior with a heart, bruised but unbroken. Wolverine is voiced by Steve Blum , having portrayed the character for over 20 years in various media such as the X-Men Legends game series, the Marvel Ultimate Alliance game series, Wolverine and the X-Men (2009), and more. The name of Wolverine's Ultimate, "Last Stand," is a possible reference to the 2006 film in the Fox's X-Men film series, X-Men: The Last Stand .
